deck.name: Basic Spanish for English Speakers
deck.subject: Languages
deck.level: Beginner to A2 (get by in daily life)
deck.description: What to learn first so the rest gets easier: 26 plainly named units, in the order they should be learned, including what you need to get by in Mexico.

cards.target: ¿Cómo estás? · ¿Cómo está usted?
cards.native: tú or usted: tú for friends, peers and kids; usted for elders, strangers, bosses and service. When in doubt, use usted.
cards.exampleTarget: Buenas tardes, señora. ¿Cómo está usted?
cards.exampleNative: Good afternoon, ma'am. How are you?
cards.remember: Casual words (¿qué onda? = what's up?, órale = OK, come on, no manches = no way) are for friends only.
cards.meaning: How are you? (to a friend) · How are you? (polite)
cards.replyNative: Very well, thank you. And you?

cards.target: Buenos días · Buenas tardes · Buenas noches
cards.native: Greetings follow the clock: días until about noon, tardes from midday until dark, noches after dark (hello and goodnight). Hola, buenas and buen día work any time.
cards.exampleTarget: Buenas noches, Don Ernesto.
cards.exampleNative: Good evening, Don Ernesto.
cards.meaning: Good morning · Good afternoon · Good evening / Good night

cards.target: ustedes
cards.native: In Mexico ustedes is the only "you all", for friends and strangers alike. It uses the same verb form as ellos.
cards.exampleTarget: Ustedes son muy amables.
cards.exampleNative: You all are very kind.
cards.meaning: you all

cards.native: Questions and exclamations open with an upside-down mark.
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Tienes hambre? ¡Qué bueno!
cards.exampleNative: Are you hungry? Great!
cards.meaning: a question mark at both ends · an exclamation mark at both ends

cards.target: sí · si · tú · tu · él · el · sólo · solo
cards.native: An accent can change the word: sí yes / si if, tú you / tu your, él he / el the, sólo only / sol@ alone.
cards.exampleTarget: Sí, él es mi amigo y tu hermano también.
cards.exampleNative: Yes, he is my friend and your brother too.
cards.meaning: yes · if · you · your · he · the · only · alone

cards.target: me llamo · nos vemos · lo siento · que le vaya bien
cards.native: Fixed phrases hide verb forms you haven't studied yet (reflexive, command, wish). Learn them whole.
cards.exampleTarget: Me llamo Tony. Que le vaya bien.
cards.exampleNative: My name is Tony. Hope it goes well.
cards.meaning: my name is · see you · I'm sorry · I hope it goes well for you

cards.target: hola · buenas · buen día
cards.native: hi · hi · good day (any time of day)
cards.exampleTarget: ¡Hola! ¿Qué tal?
cards.exampleNative: Hi! How's it going?
cards.remember: All three work at any hour.

cards.target: buenos días
cards.native: good morning (until about noon)
cards.exampleTarget: Buenos días, señora.
cards.exampleNative: Good morning, ma'am.
cards.replyNative: How did you wake up this morning? (usted)

cards.target: buenas tardes
cards.native: good afternoon (midday until dark)
cards.exampleTarget: Buenas tardes, señor. ¿Cómo está usted?
cards.exampleNative: Good afternoon, sir. How are you?

cards.target: buenas noches
cards.native: good evening · good night (after dark)
cards.exampleTarget: Buenas noches, señorita.
cards.exampleNative: Good evening, miss.
cards.remember: Used for both hello and goodbye after dark.

cards.target: ¿qué tal?
cards.native: how's it going?
cards.exampleTarget: Hola, Marco. ¿Qué tal?
cards.exampleNative: Hi, Marco. How's it going?

cards.target: ¿y tú? · ¿y usted?
cards.native: and you? (tú · usted)
cards.exampleTarget: Muy bien, gracias. ¿Y usted?
cards.exampleNative: Very well, thanks. And you?

cards.target: muy bien · bien · regular · más o menos · mal
cards.native: very good · good · okay · so-so · bad
cards.exampleTarget: Estoy bien, gracias. · Más o menos.
cards.exampleNative: I'm fine, thanks. · So-so.
cards.remember: bien (well) and mal (badly) never change form.

cards.target: excelente · todo bien
cards.native: excellent · all good
cards.exampleTarget: Todo bien. ¿Y tú?
cards.exampleNative: All good. And you?

cards.target: señor · señora · señorita
cards.native: sir, Mr. · ma'am, Mrs. · miss
cards.exampleTarget: Buenos días, señor García.
cards.exampleNative: Good morning, Mr. García.
cards.remember: These titles go with usted.

cards.target: joven
cards.native: young man (to get a waiter's attention) · young
cards.exampleTarget: ¡Joven! La cuenta, por favor.
cards.exampleNative: Excuse me! The check, please.
cards.remember: As a describing word, joven = young: Es muy joven.
cards.replyNative: Could you bring us more water, please?

cards.target: ¿cómo te llamas? · ¿cómo se llama usted?
cards.native: what's your name? (tú · usted)
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Cómo se llama usted? → Me llamo Tony.
cards.exampleNative: What's your name? → My name is Tony.

cards.target: me llamo…
cards.native: my name is…
cards.exampleTarget: Me llamo Ana. Mucho gusto.
cards.exampleNative: My name is Ana. Nice to meet you.
cards.remember: From llamarse (to be called), literally "I call myself".

cards.target: ¿de dónde eres? · ¿de dónde es usted?
cards.native: where are you from? (tú · usted)
cards.exampleTarget: ¿De dónde es usted? → Soy de Oregon.
cards.exampleNative: Where are you from? → I'm from Oregon.
cards.remember: The little word de (of, from) goes first.
cards.replyNative: And how long have you been here?

cards.target: soy de…
cards.native: I'm from…
cards.exampleTarget: Soy de Guadalajara. Soy mexicana.
cards.exampleNative: I'm from Guadalajara. I'm Mexican.
cards.replyNative: And you, are you from here?

cards.target: mucho gusto · encantad@
cards.native: nice to meet you
cards.exampleTarget: Mucho gusto. · Encantado. (a man) · Encantada. (a woman)
cards.exampleNative: Nice to meet you.
cards.remember: encantad@ (delighted) matches the person speaking.

cards.target: igualmente
cards.native: likewise
cards.exampleTarget: Mucho gusto. → Igualmente.
cards.exampleNative: Nice to meet you. → Likewise.
cards.replyNative: I hope to see you soon.

cards.target: el gusto es mío · es un placer · un placer
cards.native: the pleasure is mine · it's a pleasure · a pleasure
cards.exampleTarget: Es un placer, maestra. → El gusto es mío.
cards.exampleNative: It's a pleasure, teacher. → The pleasure is mine.

cards.target: Don · Doña
cards.native: warm title of respect before an older adult's first name
cards.exampleTarget: Buenos días, Don Ernesto.
cards.exampleNative: Good morning, Don Ernesto.
cards.remember: Not nobility, just warmth. You'll hear it constantly.

cards.target: por favor · gracias · muchas gracias · de nada
cards.native: please · thank you · thank you very much · you're welcome
cards.exampleTarget: Muchas gracias, señora. → De nada.
cards.exampleNative: Thank you very much, ma'am. → You're welcome.

cards.target: perdón · lo siento
cards.native: pardon, sorry (a small bump) · I'm sorry (you mean it)
cards.exampleTarget: ¡Perdón! · Lo siento, no tengo efectivo.
cards.exampleNative: Sorry! · I'm sorry, I don't have cash.
cards.remember: lo siento (I'm sorry) comes from sentir, to feel.

cards.target: con permiso · propio
cards.native: excuse me (passing through) · go ahead (the reply)
cards.exampleTarget: Con permiso. → Propio.
cards.exampleNative: Excuse me. → Go ahead.

cards.target: disculpe
cards.native: excuse me (usted; to get attention)
cards.exampleTarget: Disculpe, ¿dónde está el baño?
cards.exampleNative: Excuse me, where is the bathroom?
cards.replyNative: Do you know what time it is?

cards.target: pásale
cards.native: come in · go ahead (MX)
cards.exampleTarget: ¡Pásale! La comida está lista.
cards.exampleNative: Come in! The food is ready.
cards.remember: A command form of pasar (to come in, to pass).

cards.target: provecho
cards.native: enjoy your meal
cards.exampleTarget: Provecho. → Gracias.
cards.exampleNative: Enjoy your meal. → Thanks.
cards.remember: Said to anyone eating, even strangers in a restaurant.

cards.target: ¿mande?
cards.native: pardon? what was that? (respectful, MX)
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Mande? ¿Puede repetir?
cards.exampleNative: Pardon? Can you repeat that?
cards.remember: The polite Mexican way to say "what?".

cards.target: aquí tiene · aquí tienes
cards.native: here you go (usted · tú)
cards.exampleTarget: Aquí tiene su cambio.
cards.exampleNative: Here's your change.
cards.replyNative: Can you give me a receipt, please?

cards.target: no entiendo · ya entiendo
cards.native: I don't understand · now I get it
cards.exampleTarget: No entiendo. ¿Puede repetir? · Ah, ya entiendo.
cards.exampleNative: I don't understand. Can you repeat that? · Ah, now I get it.
cards.remember: From entender (to understand).

cards.target: ¿puede repetir? · ¿puede hablar más despacio?
cards.native: can you repeat that? · can you speak more slowly?
cards.exampleTarget: Perdón, ¿puede hablar más despacio, por favor?
cards.exampleNative: Sorry, can you speak more slowly, please?
cards.remember: puede (you can) + infinitive, from poder (to be able to).

cards.target: ¿habla inglés? · ¿cómo se dice…?
cards.native: do you speak English? · how do you say…?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Cómo se dice "market"? → Se dice "mercado".
cards.exampleNative: How do you say "market"? → You say "mercado".

cards.target: ¿me puede ayudar?
cards.native: can you help me?
cards.exampleTarget: Disculpe, ¿me puede ayudar? Estoy perdido.
cards.exampleNative: Excuse me, can you help me? I'm lost.

cards.target: estoy perdid@
cards.native: I'm lost (matches you)
cards.exampleTarget: Estoy perdida. ¿Dónde está la plaza?
cards.exampleNative: I'm lost. Where is the plaza?
cards.replyTarget: ¿Me lo puede enseñar en el mapa?
cards.replyNative: Can you show me on the map?

cards.target: ¿cómo llego a…?
cards.native: how do I get to…?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Cómo llego al centro? · ¿Cómo llego a la catedral?
cards.exampleNative: How do I get downtown? · How do I get to the cathedral?
cards.remember: a (to) + el (the) squeezes into al.

cards.target: la cuenta, por favor · ¿puedo pagar con tarjeta?
cards.native: the check, please · can I pay by card?
cards.exampleTarget: La cuenta, por favor. ¿Puedo pagar con tarjeta?
cards.exampleNative: The check, please. Can I pay by card?

cards.target: adiós · nos vemos
cards.native: goodbye · see you
cards.exampleTarget: Adiós, maestra. Nos vemos el jueves.
cards.exampleNative: Goodbye, teacher. See you Thursday.
cards.remember: nos vemos (see you) is from verse, to see each other.

cards.target: hasta luego · hasta pronto · hasta mañana
cards.native: see you later · see you soon · see you tomorrow
cards.exampleTarget: Hasta mañana, señora.
cards.exampleNative: See you tomorrow, ma'am.

cards.target: cuídate · cuídese
cards.native: take care (tú · usted)
cards.exampleTarget: Gracias, Don Ernesto. Cuídese.
cards.exampleNative: Thanks, Don Ernesto. Take care.

cards.target: que te vaya bien · que le vaya bien
cards.native: hope it goes well (tú · usted)
cards.exampleTarget: ¡Que le vaya bien, señor!
cards.exampleNative: Hope it goes well, sir!
cards.remember: A fixed wish form. Learn it whole.

cards.target: saludos · saludos a…
cards.native: regards · say hi to…
cards.exampleTarget: ¡Saludos a tu mamá!
cards.exampleNative: Say hi to your mom!
cards.replyTarget: Se los doy de tu parte.
cards.replyNative: I'll pass them on from you.

cards.target: yo · tú · usted · él · ella
cards.native: I · you · you (formal) · he · she
cards.exampleTarget: Yo soy de Oregon. Ella es de México.
cards.exampleNative: I'm from Oregon. She's from Mexico.
cards.remember: The verb ending shows the person, so Spanish often drops the pronoun: Soy de Oregon (I'm from Oregon).

cards.target: nosotros · nosotras · ellos · ellas · ustedes
cards.native: we (m. · f.) · they (m. · f.) · you all
cards.exampleTarget: Nosotros somos estudiantes. Ustedes son maestros.
cards.exampleNative: We are students. You all are teachers.
cards.remember: A mixed group takes the masculine. In Mexico ustedes is "you all" for friends and strangers alike.

cards.target: el museo · la plaza · los museos · las plazas
cards.native: Every noun is masculine or feminine. The / a: el · un (m.), la · una (f.); plural los · unos, las · unas.
cards.exampleTarget: El parque es grande. Las plazas son bonitas.
cards.exampleNative: The park is big. The plazas are pretty.
cards.meaning: the museum · the square · the museums · the squares

cards.target: -o = m. · -a = f. · -ción, -dad = f. · some -ma = m.
cards.native: Endings predict gender: -o masculine, -a feminine, -ción / -sión and -dad feminine. A few sneaky -ma words are masculine: el problema, el sistema, el programa, el tema, el idioma.
cards.exampleTarget: La estación · la ciudad · el problema
cards.exampleNative: the station · the city · the problem
cards.remember: Most -ma words are still feminine: la cama (the bed). Other exceptions met so far: el mapa (map), el día (day), la foto (photo), la moto (motorbike). agua (water) is feminine but takes el.
cards.meaning: -o = masculine · -a = feminine · -ción, -dad = feminine · some -ma = masculine

cards.target: el hotel → los hoteles · el libro → los libros
cards.native: Plurals: add -s after a vowel, -es after a consonant.
cards.exampleTarget: El examen es difícil. Los exámenes son difíciles.
cards.exampleNative: The exam is hard. The exams are hard.
cards.meaning: the hotel → the hotels · the book → the books

cards.target: el museo famoso · la plaza famosa
cards.native: Describing words match the noun in gender and number. -o / -a words have four forms; -e or consonant words only add -s / -es.
cards.exampleTarget: el café popular · los cafés populares · la idea interesante
cards.exampleNative: the popular cafe · the popular cafes · the interesting idea
cards.remember: Same for both genders: especial, natural, popular, tropical, diferente, excelente, interesante, importante, terrible, útil (useful), común (common).
cards.meaning: the famous museum · the famous square

cards.target: el carro rojo · muy activo
cards.native: Describing words go AFTER the noun (the reverse of English). muy goes right before the describing word.
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo un carro rojo. El mercado es muy activo.
cards.exampleNative: I have a red car. The market is very busy.
cards.remember: A few common ones can go first: buen (good), mal (bad), próximo (next).
cards.meaning: the red car · very active

cards.target: alto → altos → alta → altas
cards.native: Agreement check order: number first, then gender. A mixed group (men and women) takes the masculine.
cards.exampleTarget: Los hermanos de Ana son altos. (brothers and sisters)
cards.exampleNative: Ana's siblings are tall.
cards.meaning: tall (one man) → tall (men) → tall (one woman) → tall (women)
cards.replyTarget: Sí, toda la familia es alta.
cards.replyNative: Yes, the whole family is tall.

cards.target: un buen doctor · un mal día
cards.native: bueno and malo drop the -o right before a masculine singular noun.
cards.exampleTarget: Es un buen doctor. Hoy es un mal día.
cards.exampleNative: He's a good doctor. Today is a bad day.
cards.meaning: a good doctor · a bad day
cards.replyTarget: Mañana va a ser un buen día.
cards.replyNative: Tomorrow is going to be a good day.

cards.group: Rules: how Spanish relates to English
cards.target: estación · nación · decisión
cards.native: -ción / -sión = English -tion / -sion, and they're feminine.
cards.exampleTarget: La decisión es importante.
cards.exampleNative: The decision is important.
cards.meaning: station · nation · decision

cards.group: Rules: how Spanish relates to English
cards.target: ciudad · universidad
cards.native: -dad = English -ty (city, university), and they're feminine.
cards.exampleTarget: La universidad está en la ciudad.
cards.exampleNative: The university is in the city.
cards.meaning: city · university

cards.group: Rules: how Spanish relates to English
cards.target: escuela · estudiante · España
cards.native: Spanish adds e- before s + consonant: school → escuela, student → estudiante, Spain → España.
cards.exampleTarget: El estudiante está en la escuela.
cards.exampleNative: The student is at school.
cards.meaning: school · student · Spain

cards.group: Rules: how Spanish relates to English
cards.target: enfermo → infirmary · dormido → dormitory
cards.native: Many words share Latin roots with English: if you know the English cousin, you can guess the Spanish (sano → sanitary, abierto → aperture, fuerte → fort, débil → debilitate).
cards.exampleTarget: La puerta está abierta.
cards.exampleNative: The door is open.
cards.remember: Cognate cards in the lessons are memory hooks, not rules to memorize.
cards.meaning: sick → infirmary · asleep → dormitory

cards.target: casa · en casa
cards.native: house · at home
cards.exampleTarget: Estoy en casa hoy.
cards.exampleNative: I'm at home today.
cards.replyNative: Do you want to come to my house?

cards.target: cuarto (m.) · recámara (f.)
cards.native: room · bedroom
cards.exampleTarget: Mi cuarto está desordenado.
cards.exampleNative: My room is messy.
cards.remember: recámara is the Mexican word for bedroom.
cards.replyNative: I have to clean my bedroom.

cards.target: cocina · sala · baño (m.)
cards.native: kitchen · living room · bathroom
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Dónde está el baño? → Está al lado de la cocina.
cards.exampleNative: Where is the bathroom? → It's next to the kitchen.

cards.target: jardín (m.) · alberca (f.)
cards.native: garden, yard · pool (MX)
cards.exampleTarget: El perro está en el jardín.
cards.exampleNative: The dog is in the yard.
cards.replyNative: Does the house have a pool?

cards.target: oficina (f.) · trabajo (m.)
cards.native: office · workplace
cards.exampleTarget: Ramón está en la oficina.
cards.exampleNative: Ramón is at the office.
cards.replyNative: What time does he get off work?

cards.target: escuela (f.) · salón (m.) · clase (f.)
cards.native: school · classroom · class
cards.exampleTarget: Los niños están en la escuela.
cards.exampleNative: The kids are at school.

cards.target: universidad (f.) · biblioteca (f.) · laboratorio (m.)
cards.native: university · library · laboratory
cards.exampleTarget: La biblioteca está cerca de la universidad.
cards.exampleNative: The library is near the university.
cards.replyNative: Do you study at the library?

cards.target: banco (m.) · farmacia (f.)
cards.native: bank · pharmacy
cards.exampleTarget: La farmacia está al lado del banco.
cards.exampleNative: The pharmacy is next to the bank.
cards.replyNative: What time does the bank open?

cards.target: hospital (m.)
cards.native: hospital
cards.exampleTarget: Mi hermano está en el hospital.
cards.exampleNative: My brother is in the hospital.

cards.target: mercado · supermercado · tienda · papelería
cards.native: market · supermarket · store · stationery store
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo que ir al supermercado.
cards.exampleNative: I have to go to the supermarket.

cards.target: mall (m.) · puesto (m.)
cards.native: mall · stall, stand
cards.exampleTarget: Hay un puesto de tacos en la esquina.
cards.exampleNative: There's a taco stand on the corner.
cards.replyNative: Shall we go get some tacos?

cards.target: restaurante · café · bar · cantina
cards.native: restaurant · cafe · bar · neighborhood bar
cards.exampleTarget: El restaurante está en el centro.
cards.exampleNative: The restaurant is downtown.
cards.remember: café also means coffee.

cards.target: hotel (m.) · aeropuerto (m.)
cards.native: hotel · airport
cards.exampleTarget: El hotel está lejos del aeropuerto.
cards.exampleNative: The hotel is far from the airport.

cards.target: playa (f.)
cards.native: beach
cards.exampleTarget: La playa está muy bonita hoy.
cards.exampleNative: The beach looks very pretty today.

cards.target: parque (m.) · plaza (f.)
cards.native: park · plaza
cards.exampleTarget: El parque está enfrente de la plaza.
cards.exampleNative: The park is across from the plaza.
cards.replyNative: Shall we walk for a while?

cards.target: iglesia (f.) · catedral (f.)
cards.native: church · cathedral
cards.exampleTarget: La catedral es muy histórica.
cards.exampleNative: The cathedral is very historic.

cards.target: museo · concierto · estadio
cards.native: museum · concert · stadium
cards.exampleTarget: El museo es famoso.
cards.exampleNative: The museum is famous.

cards.target: ciudad · centro · calle · esquina · cuadra
cards.native: city · downtown · street · corner · block
cards.exampleTarget: La farmacia está a dos cuadras, en la esquina.
cards.exampleNative: The pharmacy is two blocks away, on the corner.

cards.target: edificio (m.) · piso (m.)
cards.native: building · floor (also an apartment)
cards.exampleTarget: El edificio es nuevo.
cards.exampleNative: The building is new.
cards.replyNative: What floor do you live on?

cards.target: parada (f.) · camión (m.)
cards.native: bus stop · bus (MX)
cards.exampleTarget: La parada del camión está enfrente de la farmacia.
cards.exampleNative: The bus stop is in front of the pharmacy.
cards.replyNative: How often does the bus come?

cards.target: país (m.) · lugar (m.) · mundo (m.)
cards.native: country · place · world
cards.exampleTarget: México es un país muy bonito.
cards.exampleNative: Mexico is a very pretty country.
cards.replyNative: Which place do you like best?

cards.target: estación (f.) · nación (f.)
cards.native: station · nation
cards.exampleTarget: La estación está cerca.
cards.exampleNative: The station is close.
cards.remember: -ción words are feminine, like English -tion.

cards.target: idea · tema · problema · sistema · programa · idioma
cards.native: idea · topic · problem · system · program · language
cards.exampleTarget: El problema es común. El idioma es importante.
cards.exampleNative: The problem is common. The language is important.
cards.remember: idea is feminine; every -ma word here is masculine (el tema, the topic; el idioma, the language).
cards.replyNative: How many languages do you speak?

cards.target: grupo · tipo · nivel · parte
cards.native: group · type, kind · level · part
cards.exampleTarget: El nivel es diferente, pero no es difícil.
cards.exampleNative: The level is different, but it isn't hard.
cards.remember: parte is feminine: la parte.

cards.target: servicio (m.)
cards.native: service
cards.exampleTarget: El servicio es excelente.
cards.exampleNative: The service is excellent.

cards.target: vocal (f.) · consonante (f.)
cards.native: vowel · consonant
cards.exampleTarget: Las vocales y las consonantes son diferentes.
cards.exampleNative: The vowels and the consonants are different.
cards.replyNative: How many vowels are there in Spanish?

cards.target: decisión (f.)
cards.native: decision
cards.exampleTarget: Es una decisión muy difícil.
cards.exampleNative: It's a very hard decision.

cards.target: ruido (m.)
cards.native: noise
cards.exampleTarget: Hay mucho ruido afuera.
cards.exampleNative: There's a lot of noise outside.

cards.target: sorpresa · pasión
cards.native: surprise · passion
cards.exampleTarget: Los tacos son mi pasión.
cards.exampleNative: Tacos are my passion.
cards.replyNative: And which one is your favorite?

cards.target: grande / pequeñ@
cards.native: big / small
cards.exampleTarget: La casa es grande, pero el jardín es pequeño.
cards.exampleNative: The house is big, but the yard is small.
cards.remember: grande (big) stays the same for both genders.

cards.target: nuev@ / viej@
cards.native: new / old (things)
cards.exampleTarget: El carro es nuevo y la casa es vieja.
cards.exampleNative: The car is new and the house is old.
cards.remember: Use viejo (old) for things, mayor (older) for people.

cards.target: car@ / barat@
cards.native: expensive / cheap
cards.exampleTarget: El hotel es caro, pero la comida es barata.
cards.exampleNative: The hotel is expensive, but the food is cheap.
cards.remember: Hoy está barato = it's cheap today.

cards.target: fácil / difícil
cards.native: easy / hard, difficult
cards.exampleTarget: El examen no es fácil, es muy difícil.
cards.exampleNative: The exam isn't easy, it's very hard.
cards.remember: fácil (easy) is for things, not people.

cards.target: larg@ / cort@
cards.native: long / short (a thing, hair)
cards.exampleTarget: Este capítulo es muy largo. El viaje es corto.
cards.exampleNative: This chapter is very long. The trip is short.
cards.remember: False friend: largo = long, not large.

cards.target: interesante · importante · especial
cards.native: interesting · important · special
cards.exampleTarget: La clase es interesante y muy importante.
cards.exampleNative: The class is interesting and very important.
cards.remember: Same form for both genders.

cards.target: excelente · fantástic@ · perfect@ · maravillos@
cards.native: excellent · fantastic · perfect · wonderful
cards.exampleTarget: El servicio es excelente y la comida es perfecta.
cards.exampleNative: The service is excellent and the food is perfect.

cards.target: diferente · común · normal · típic@
cards.native: different · common · normal · typical, traditional
cards.exampleTarget: Es una comida típica de Oaxaca.
cards.exampleNative: It's a typical dish from Oaxaca.

cards.target: modern@ / históric@
cards.native: modern / historic
cards.exampleTarget: El hotel es moderno, pero el centro es histórico.
cards.exampleNative: The hotel is modern, but downtown is historic.

cards.target: natural · tropical · nacional
cards.native: natural · tropical · national
cards.exampleTarget: El parque es tropical y natural.
cards.exampleNative: The park is tropical and natural.

cards.target: misterios@ · útil · terrible
cards.native: mysterious · useful · terrible
cards.exampleTarget: La catedral es misteriosa. El mapa es útil.
cards.exampleNative: The cathedral is mysterious. The map is useful.
cards.replyNative: Will you lend it to me?

cards.target: delicios@ · increíble
cards.native: delicious · incredible
cards.exampleTarget: La salsa es increíble y los tacos están deliciosos.
cards.exampleNative: The salsa is incredible and the tacos are delicious.
cards.remember: está delicioso = this food tastes delicious right now.
cards.replyNative: Will you give me the recipe?

cards.target: frecuente · activ@
cards.native: frequent, regular · active, busy
cards.exampleTarget: El mercado es muy activo.
cards.exampleNative: The market is very busy.
cards.remember: A person: only after a noun, un cliente frecuente (a regular customer).

cards.target: próxim@ · siguiente
cards.native: next (coming up) · next (the following one)
cards.exampleTarget: El próximo lunes tengo cita. El parque está en la siguiente calle.
cards.exampleNative: Next Monday I have an appointment. The park is on the next street.
cards.remember: próximo (next) matches its noun: la próxima semana (next week).

cards.target: ruidos@ / tranquil@
cards.native: noisy / calm, quiet
cards.exampleTarget: La calle es ruidosa, pero la casa es tranquila.
cards.exampleNative: The street is noisy, but the house is quiet.

cards.target: pesad@ / liger@
cards.native: heavy / light
cards.exampleTarget: La mesa es muy pesada, pero la silla es ligera.
cards.exampleNative: The table is very heavy, but the chair is light.
cards.remember: A person who es pesad@ is annoying.
cards.replyNative: I'll help you with the table.

cards.target: lent@ · oscur@ · fresc@
cards.native: slow · dark · fresh, cool
cards.exampleTarget: Hoy la computadora está muy lenta.
cards.exampleNative: Today the computer is very slow.

cards.target: y · e
cards.native: and (e before an i- or hi- sound)
cards.exampleTarget: Laura e Iván. Madre e hija.
cards.exampleNative: Laura and Iván. Mother and daughter.
cards.remember: It's about the sound, not the letter.

cards.target: o · u
cards.native: or (u before an o- or ho- sound)
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Siete u ocho? ¿Mujer u hombre?
cards.exampleNative: Seven or eight? Woman or man?

cards.target: pero
cards.native: but
cards.exampleTarget: Estoy cansado, pero estoy contento.
cards.exampleNative: I'm tired, but I'm happy.

cards.target: Soy de Oregon. (yo soy de Oregon)
cards.native: The verb ending already shows who is talking, so the pronoun (yo, tú, él…) is usually dropped. Add it only for emphasis or contrast.
cards.exampleTarget: Soy maestra. ¿Y tú? → Yo soy estudiante.
cards.exampleNative: I'm a teacher. And you? → I'm a student.
cards.meaning: I'm from Oregon. (I am from Oregon)

cards.target: la mamá de Ana · el carro del vecino
cards.native: Spanish has no 's. Possession is "the X of Y": la mamá de Ana = Ana's mom.
cards.exampleTarget: ¿De quién es? → Es de Mario.
cards.exampleNative: Whose is it? → It's Mario's.
cards.remember: de + el = del (of the).
cards.meaning: Ana's mom · the neighbor's car
cards.replyNative: Oh, shall I take it to Mario?

cards.target: El mercado es activo. → ¿El mercado es activo?
cards.native: A yes / no question keeps statement order. Just add ¿ ? and let your voice rise.
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Tú eres de México? · ¿Martha está en casa?
cards.exampleNative: Are you from Mexico? · Is Martha home?
cards.meaning: The market is busy. → Is the market busy?

cards.target: Ella no es maestra.
cards.native: no goes in front of the verb (and in front of lo, la, me if there is one: No lo conozco).
cards.exampleTarget: No soy de aquí. No tenemos que trabajar.
cards.exampleNative: I'm not from here. We don't have to work.
cards.meaning: She isn't a teacher.

cards.target: soy · eres · es · somos · son
cards.native: ser = who or what someone is at the core. Memory aid DOCTOR: Description, Occupation, Characteristic, Time & dates, Origin, Relationship.
cards.exampleTarget: Soy alto. Soy maestro. Soy amable. Son las dos. Soy de Oregon. Es mi hermana.
cards.exampleNative: I'm tall. I'm a teacher. I'm kind. It's two. I'm from Oregon. She's my sister.
cards.meaning: I am · you are · he / she is, you (polite) are · we are · they are, you all are

cards.target: Soy maestra.
cards.native: A job after ser takes NO article, unlike English "a teacher".
cards.exampleTarget: Él es doctor. Somos estudiantes.
cards.exampleNative: He is a doctor. We are students.
cards.remember: ✗ Soy una maestra. (Say Soy maestra, I'm a teacher.)
cards.meaning: I'm a teacher.

cards.target: es · son
cards.native: One thing takes es; more than one takes son.
cards.exampleTarget: El libro es interesante. Los libros son interesantes.
cards.exampleNative: The book is interesting. The books are interesting.
cards.meaning: is · are

cards.target: mi mamá · mi papá · mis hijos
cards.native: Possessives match the THING owned, not the owner. mi, tu, su change only for number.
cards.exampleTarget: Mi casa · mis casas · su libro · sus libros
cards.exampleNative: my house · my houses · his book · his books
cards.meaning: my mom · my dad · my children

cards.target: nuestro carro · nuestra casa
cards.native: nuestro is the only possessive that also changes for gender.
cards.exampleTarget: Nuestros amigos son de aquí. Nuestras clases son los martes.
cards.exampleNative: Our friends are from here. Our classes are on Tuesdays.
cards.meaning: our car · our house

cards.group: Grammar: pronouns: me, lo, le, and the personal a
cards.target: mío · tuyo · suyo · nuestro
cards.native: Long possessives (mine, yours, his / hers / theirs, ours) go after the noun or stand alone. They match the thing owned.
cards.exampleTarget: Este libro es mío. ¿Es tuya la mochila? → No, es suya.
cards.exampleNative: This book is mine. Is the backpack yours? → No, it's his.
cards.remember: Seen: el gusto es mío, the pleasure is mine (L1); la tuya, yours (L5).
cards.meaning: mine · yours · his / hers / theirs · ours

cards.target: mi · mis
cards.native: my
cards.exampleTarget: Mi hija es maestra. Mis amigos son de aquí.
cards.exampleNative: My daughter is a teacher. My friends are from here.
cards.remember: Changes only for number.

cards.target: tu · tus
cards.native: your (tú)
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Tu casa es grande? Tus perros son bonitos.
cards.exampleNative: Is your house big? Your dogs are pretty.
cards.remember: tu (your) has no accent; tú (you) does.

cards.target: su · sus
cards.native: his · her · your (usted) · their
cards.exampleTarget: Su mamá es doctora. Sus libros están en la mesa.
cards.exampleNative: His mom is a doctor. His books are on the table.
cards.remember: Context tells you whose.
cards.replyNative: Which hospital does she work at?

cards.target: nuestro · nuestra · nuestros · nuestras
cards.native: our
cards.exampleTarget: Nuestra casa es pequeña, pero nuestro jardín es grande.
cards.exampleNative: Our house is small, but our garden is big.
cards.remember: The only possessive that changes for gender. It matches the thing owned.

cards.target: la tuya
cards.native: yours (your one)
cards.exampleTarget: Mi mamá tiene cuarenta y dos años. ¿Y la tuya?
cards.exampleNative: My mom is forty-two. And yours?

cards.target: familia (f.)
cards.native: family
cards.exampleTarget: Mi familia es grande.
cards.exampleNative: My family is big.
cards.replyNative: How many siblings do you have?

cards.target: papá · padre (m.) · mamá · madre (f.)
cards.native: dad, father · mom, mother
cards.exampleTarget: Mi papá es ingeniero y mi mamá es maestra.
cards.exampleNative: My dad is an engineer and my mom is a teacher.

cards.target: padres (m.)
cards.native: parents
cards.exampleTarget: Mis padres son de Puebla.
cards.exampleNative: My parents are from Puebla.
cards.remember: padres means parents, not only fathers.
cards.replyNative: And do they still live there?

cards.target: espos@
cards.native: husband · wife
cards.exampleTarget: Mi esposa está en el trabajo.
cards.exampleNative: My wife is at work.
cards.replyNative: What does she do for a living?

cards.target: hij@ · hij@s
cards.native: son · daughter · children
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo dos hijos: un hijo y una hija.
cards.exampleNative: I have two children: a son and a daughter.
cards.remember: hijos covers sons and daughters together.

cards.target: herman@ · herman@s
cards.native: brother · sister · siblings
cards.exampleTarget: Mi hermano es alto y mi hermana es baja.
cards.exampleNative: My brother is tall and my sister is short.

cards.target: abuel@ · abuel@s
cards.native: grandpa · grandma · grandparents
cards.exampleTarget: Mis abuelos son mayores.
cards.exampleNative: My grandparents are elderly.

cards.target: tí@ · tíos
cards.native: uncle · aunt · aunts and uncles
cards.exampleTarget: Mi tía está en el hospital.
cards.exampleNative: My aunt is in the hospital.
cards.replyNative: I hope she gets better soon.

cards.target: prim@
cards.native: cousin
cards.exampleTarget: Mis primas son muy chistosas.
cards.exampleNative: My cousins are very funny.

cards.target: sobrin@
cards.native: nephew · niece
cards.exampleTarget: Mi sobrino tiene seis años.
cards.exampleNative: My nephew is six.
cards.replyNative: Does he go to school yet?

cards.target: suegr@
cards.native: father-in-law · mother-in-law
cards.exampleTarget: Mi suegra es muy amable.
cards.exampleNative: My mother-in-law is very kind.

cards.target: novi@
cards.native: boyfriend · girlfriend · groom · bride
cards.exampleTarget: Su novio es de Colombia.
cards.exampleNative: Her boyfriend is from Colombia.

cards.target: pareja (f.)
cards.native: partner · couple · pair
cards.exampleTarget: Mi pareja es muy trabajadora.
cards.exampleNative: My partner is very hardworking.
cards.remember: Always la pareja (the partner), even for a man, so the describing word stays feminine.
cards.replyNative: How long have you been together?

cards.target: amig@
cards.native: friend
cards.exampleTarget: Luis es mi amigo. Somos buenos amigos.
cards.exampleNative: Luis is my friend. We are good friends.
cards.replyNative: How long have you known each other?

cards.target: vecin@ · los vecinos de arriba
cards.native: neighbor · the upstairs neighbors
cards.exampleTarget: Los vecinos de arriba siempre están muy ruidosos.
cards.exampleNative: The upstairs neighbors are always very noisy.
cards.replyNative: Have you talked to them yet?

cards.target: compañer@ · compañer@ de trabajo
cards.native: classmate, partner · coworker
cards.exampleTarget: Mi compañera de trabajo es muy amable.
cards.exampleNative: My coworker is very kind.

cards.target: hombre (m.) · mujer (f.)
cards.native: man · woman
cards.exampleTarget: El hombre es alto y la mujer es baja.
cards.exampleNative: The man is tall and the woman is short.

cards.target: niñ@ · bebé
cards.native: kid (boy · girl) · baby
cards.exampleTarget: Los niños están en el jardín. El bebé tiene tos.
cards.exampleNative: The kids are in the yard. The baby has a cough.
cards.replyNative: Did you take him to the doctor yet?

cards.target: persona (f.) · gente (f.)
cards.native: person · people
cards.exampleTarget: Es una persona muy amable. La gente aquí es amigable.
cards.exampleNative: He's a very kind person. The people here are friendly.
cards.remember: persona (person) is always feminine; gente (people) is singular: la gente es… (people are…)

cards.target: cliente · clienta
cards.native: customer · client
cards.exampleTarget: Somos clientes frecuentes.
cards.exampleNative: We are regular customers.
cards.replyNative: Is there a discount for customers?

cards.target: dueñ@ · jefe (m.)
cards.native: owner · boss
cards.exampleTarget: El dueño es muy amable. Tengo que hablar con el jefe.
cards.exampleNative: The owner is very kind. I have to talk to the boss.

cards.target: maestr@ · estudiante
cards.native: teacher · student
cards.exampleTarget: Soy estudiante y ella es maestra.
cards.exampleNative: I'm a student and she's a teacher.
cards.remember: No article after ser: not una maestra (a teacher).

cards.target: doctor(a) · enfermer@ · dentista
cards.native: doctor · nurse · dentist
cards.exampleTarget: Él es doctor y ella es enfermera.
cards.exampleNative: He is a doctor and she is a nurse.
cards.replyNative: Do they work at the same hospital?

cards.target: abogad@ · contador(a)
cards.native: lawyer · accountant
cards.exampleTarget: Mi hermano es abogado.
cards.exampleNative: My brother is a lawyer.
cards.remember: contador (accountant) comes from contar, to count.
cards.replyNative: Does he have his own office?

cards.target: ingenier@ · mecánic@
cards.native: engineer · mechanic
cards.exampleTarget: Mi papá es ingeniero.
cards.exampleNative: My dad is an engineer.

cards.target: cajer@ · meser@ · cociner@
cards.native: cashier · waiter, waitress · cook
cards.exampleTarget: Soy cajero en una tienda.
cards.exampleNative: I'm a cashier in a store.

cards.target: emplead@ · gerente
cards.native: employee · manager
cards.exampleTarget: La gerente es de Monterrey.
cards.exampleNative: The manager is from Monterrey.

cards.target: escritor(a) · periodista · artista
cards.native: writer · journalist · artist
cards.exampleTarget: Ella es escritora.
cards.exampleNative: She is a writer.
cards.remember: -ista words are the same for a man or a woman.

cards.target: policía · turista
cards.native: police officer · tourist
cards.exampleTarget: No soy turista, soy de aquí.
cards.exampleNative: I'm not a tourist, I'm from here.
cards.remember: Same form for a man or a woman.

cards.target: profesión (f.) · trabajo (m.) · carrera (f.)
cards.native: profession · job, work · degree program, career
cards.exampleTarget: Mi trabajo es interesante. Su carrera es difícil.
cards.exampleNative: My job is interesting. Her degree program is hard.
cards.remember: carrera (career) can also mean a race.

cards.target: inglés · medicina · ingeniería · letras
cards.native: English · medicine · engineering · humanities (fields of study)
cards.exampleTarget: Soy estudiante de inglés. Ella es estudiante de ingeniería.
cards.exampleNative: I'm an English student. She's an engineering student.

cards.target: alt@ / baj@
cards.native: tall / short (a person)
cards.exampleTarget: Mi hermano es alto, pero yo soy bajo.
cards.exampleNative: My brother is tall, but I'm short.
cards.remember: A short person is bajo; short hair is el pelo corto.

cards.target: gord@ / delgad@
cards.native: heavy, fat / thin, slim
cards.exampleTarget: Mi perro es gordo y mi gato es delgado.
cards.exampleNative: My dog is fat and my cat is thin.

cards.target: guap@ · bonit@ · hermos@
cards.native: good-looking · pretty · beautiful
cards.exampleTarget: Tu hija es muy bonita. La playa es hermosa.
cards.exampleNative: Your daughter is very pretty. The beach is beautiful.
cards.remember: Warmth climbs: guapo (good-looking) → bonito (pretty) → hermoso (beautiful).
cards.replyTarget: Gracias, es igual a su mamá.
cards.replyNative: Thanks, she looks just like her mom.

cards.target: joven / mayor · menor
cards.native: young / older, elderly · younger
cards.exampleTarget: Mi hermano mayor es abogado y mi hermana menor es estudiante.
cards.exampleNative: My older brother is a lawyer and my younger sister is a student.
cards.remember: Use mayor (older), not viejo (old), for older people.
cards.replyNative: And what is your sister studying?

cards.target: fuerte / débil
cards.native: strong / weak
cards.exampleTarget: Soy fuerte, no soy débil.
cards.exampleNative: I'm strong, I'm not weak.
cards.remember: fuerte (strong) also means a strong coffee or a loud noise.
cards.replyNative: Do you go to the gym?

cards.target: ric@ / pobre
cards.native: wealthy / poor
cards.exampleTarget: Mi vecino es muy rico. ¡Pobre Martha!
cards.exampleNative: My neighbor is very rich. Poor Martha!
cards.remember: With ser, rico means rich. With estar, rico means tasty. Before a name, pobre = poor thing.

cards.target: inteligente · list@
cards.native: intelligent · clever, smart
cards.exampleTarget: Ana es muy lista e inteligente.
cards.exampleNative: Ana is very clever and intelligent.
cards.remember: With estar, listo means ready.

cards.target: amable · agradable · amigable
cards.native: kind · nice, pleasant · friendly
cards.exampleTarget: El dueño es muy amable y la gente es amigable.
cards.exampleNative: The owner is very kind and the people are friendly.
cards.remember: Same form for a man or a woman.
cards.replyNative: That's why we always come here.

cards.target: chistos@ / seri@
cards.native: funny / serious
cards.exampleTarget: Mi papá es serio, pero muy chistoso con sus amigos.
cards.exampleNative: My dad is serious, but very funny with his friends.

cards.target: trabajador(a) / floj@ · perezos@
cards.native: hardworking / lazy
cards.exampleTarget: Soy muy trabajador. No soy flojo.
cards.exampleNative: I'm very hardworking. I'm not lazy.
cards.remember: Feeling lazy today is tengo flojera.
cards.replyNative: How many hours do you work?

cards.target: responsable / groser@
cards.native: responsible / rude
cards.exampleTarget: Mi hijo es responsable, no es grosero.
cards.exampleNative: My son is responsible, he isn't rude.
cards.replyNative: That's great. How old is he?

cards.target: casad@ / solter@
cards.native: married / single
cards.exampleTarget: Martha está casada. Gabriel es soltero.
cards.exampleNative: Martha is married. Gabriel is single.
cards.remember: Correct with ser or estar; está casada (she's married) is the everyday way.

cards.target: famos@ · popular
cards.native: famous · popular
cards.exampleTarget: El restaurante es famoso y muy popular.
cards.exampleNative: The restaurant is famous and very popular.

cards.target: romántic@ · favorit@
cards.native: romantic · favorite
cards.exampleTarget: Mi clase favorita es el español.
cards.exampleNative: My favorite class is Spanish.

cards.target: alegre · feliz · content@
cards.native: cheerful · happy · content
cards.exampleTarget: Mi abuela es muy alegre. Hoy estoy muy feliz.
cards.exampleNative: My grandma is very cheerful. Today I'm very happy.
cards.remember: content@ (happy) goes with estar; feliz (happy) works with both.

cards.target: buen@ / mal@
cards.native: good / bad, mean
cards.exampleTarget: Es un buen doctor. Es un perro muy malo.
cards.exampleNative: He's a good doctor. It's a very bad dog.
cards.remember: Before a masculine singular noun: buen (good), mal (bad).

cards.target: güer@ / moren@
cards.native: fair, light-skinned / dark-skinned (MX)
cards.exampleTarget: Karla es güera y su papá es moreno.
cards.exampleNative: Karla is fair-skinned and her dad is dark-skinned.
cards.remember: Understand them; not practice words. A vendor may call a customer güero (blondie, fair one).

cards.target: mexican@ · american@ · colombian@
cards.native: Mexican · American (of the Americas) · Colombian
cards.exampleTarget: Somos mexicanos. Luis es colombiano.
cards.exampleNative: We are Mexican. Luis is Colombian.
cards.remember: Nationalities are lowercase in Spanish.

cards.target: estadounidense · canadiense · español(a)
cards.native: American (from the US) · Canadian · Spanish
cards.exampleTarget: Soy estadounidense, no soy canadiense.
cards.exampleNative: I'm American, I'm not Canadian.
cards.remember: -ense nationalities are the same for a man or a woman.

cards.target: de · del
cards.native: of · from (de + el = del)
cards.exampleTarget: Es el carro del vecino. Somos de México.
cards.exampleNative: It's the neighbor's car. We're from Mexico.
cards.remember: Spanish has no 's: el carro de Mario = Mario's car.

cards.target: sí / no
cards.native: yes / no, not
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Martha está en casa? → No, no está.
cards.exampleNative: Is Martha home? → No, she isn't.
cards.remember: sí (yes) has an accent. The first no answers; the second says not.
cards.replyNative: What time is she coming back?

cards.target:
ser · present
yo soy · tú eres · él / ella / usted es · nosotros somos · ellos / ustedes son
cards.native:
to be (who / what someone is) · present
I am · you are · he/she is / you (form.) are · we are · they / you all are
cards.exampleTarget: Soy estudiante y ella es maestra.
cards.exampleNative: I am a student and she is a teacher.
cards.remember: DOCTOR uses. One thing es (is), more than one son (are).

cards.target: un taco · una plaza · veintiún tacos
cards.native: uno becomes un / una right before a noun (also in 21, 31…).
cards.exampleTarget: Hay veintiún estudiantes en la clase.
cards.exampleNative: There are twenty-one students in the class.
cards.meaning: a taco · a square · twenty-one tacos

cards.target: once · doce · trece · catorce · quince
cards.native: 11 to 15 are irregular and memorized; 16 to 29 fuse into one word (dieciséis, veintidós); 31 to 99 are three words, tens + y + ones (treinta y uno).
cards.exampleTarget: cuarenta y siete · veintitrés · catorce
cards.meaning: eleven · twelve · thirteen · fourteen · fifteen
cards.replyNative: Can you repeat it for me, please?

cards.target: cien · ciento
cards.native: cien is exactly 100; ciento is 101 to 199.
cards.exampleTarget: cien pesos · ciento cincuenta pesos
cards.exampleNative: 100 pesos · 150 pesos
cards.meaning: a hundred (exactly) · a hundred (and more)
cards.replyNative: Can you give me a discount?

cards.target: doscientos cincuenta y tres
cards.native: y joins only the tens and ones, never after the hundreds. Hundreds match the noun (doscientos pesos, doscientas casas). 500, 700, 900 are irregular: quinientos, setecientos, novecientos.
cards.exampleTarget: mil quinientos cuarenta
cards.remember: mil (thousand) never takes un (a). ✗ doscientos y cincuenta (two hundred and fifty)
cards.meaning: two hundred fifty-three

cards.target: Es la una. · Son las dos.
cards.native: Telling time uses ser. One o'clock is singular (es la una); every other hour is plural (son las…).
cards.exampleTarget: Son las cuatro y media. Es la una y diez.
cards.exampleNative: It's four thirty. It's ten past one.
cards.meaning: It's one o'clock. · It's two o'clock.

cards.target: ¿Qué hora es? · ¿A qué hora es?
cards.native: ¿Qué hora es? asks the time now. ¿A qué hora…? asks when something happens; answer with a las / a la.
cards.exampleTarget: ¿A qué hora es la clase? → Es a las nueve.
cards.exampleNative: What time is class? → It's at nine.
cards.meaning: What time is it? · What time is it at?

cards.target: el lunes · el 2 de agosto · en julio · en verano
cards.native: el goes before a day or a date; en goes before a month or a season.
cards.exampleTarget: La clase es el jueves. Mi cumpleaños es en junio.
cards.exampleNative: Class is on Thursday. My birthday is in June.
cards.meaning: on Monday · on August 2 · in July · in summer

cards.target: Hoy es lunes, doce de abril.
cards.native: Dates: day before month, number + de + month. The 1st is el primero, not el uno.
cards.exampleTarget: Mi cumpleaños es el quince de junio.
cards.exampleNative: My birthday is June fifteenth.
cards.meaning: Today is Monday, April twelfth.
cards.replyNative: It's almost here! What are you going to do?

cards.target: el lunes · los lunes
cards.native: el + day = this one time; los + day = every week (a habit).
cards.exampleTarget: La fiesta es el sábado. Tengo clase los martes.
cards.exampleNative: The party is on Saturday. I have class on Tuesdays.
cards.meaning: on Monday · on Mondays

cards.target: lunes · enero · español
cards.native: Days, months, seasons, languages and nationalities are lowercase.
cards.exampleTarget: Hoy es jueves, cinco de noviembre.
cards.exampleNative: Today is Thursday, November fifth.
cards.meaning: Monday · January · Spanish
cards.replyTarget: ¿Qué vas a hacer el fin de semana?
cards.replyNative: What are you going to do on the weekend?

cards.target: el próximo lunes · la próxima semana · este mes · esta primavera
cards.native: próximo and este agree with the noun they go with.
cards.exampleTarget: La próxima semana tengo un examen.
cards.exampleNative: Next week I have an exam.
cards.meaning: next Monday · next week · this month · this spring

cards.target: esta mañana · en la mañana
cards.native: esta mañana / tarde / noche = this specific one; en la mañana / tarde / noche = in general. Mexico says en la, not por la.
cards.exampleTarget: Esta noche tengo cita. En la noche estoy en casa.
cards.exampleNative: Tonight I have an appointment. At night I'm at home.
cards.meaning: this morning · in the morning

cards.target: ¿a qué hora…?
cards.native: at what time…?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿A qué hora es la clase? → Es a las nueve.
cards.exampleNative: What time is class? → It's at nine.
cards.replyNative: And what time does it end?

cards.target: fiesta · reunión · boda
cards.native: party · get-together, meeting · wedding
cards.exampleTarget: La reunión es el sábado en mi casa.
cards.exampleNative: The get-together is on Saturday at my house.
cards.remember: Where an event takes place uses ser: La fiesta es en mi casa (The party is at my house).

cards.target: cumpleaños · aniversario
cards.native: birthday · anniversary
cards.exampleTarget: Mi cumpleaños es el quince de junio.
cards.exampleNative: My birthday is June fifteenth.
cards.remember: cumpleaños = completes + years.
cards.replyNative: And what are you going to do?

cards.target: vacaciones (f.) · viaje (m.) · planes (m.)
cards.native: vacation · trip · plans
cards.exampleTarget: Estamos de vacaciones.
cards.exampleNative: We're on vacation.
cards.remember: vacaciones (vacation) is always plural.

cards.target: película · música
cards.native: movie · music
cards.exampleTarget: La película es muy interesante.
cards.exampleNative: The movie is very interesting.

cards.target: examen (m.)
cards.native: exam
cards.exampleTarget: El examen es el viernes.
cards.exampleNative: The exam is on Friday.

cards.target: semana · mes · año
cards.native: week · month · year
cards.exampleTarget: La próxima semana tengo un examen.
cards.exampleNative: Next week I have an exam.

cards.target: hora (f.) · tiempo (m.)
cards.native: hour, clock time · time, weather
cards.exampleTarget: No tengo tiempo hoy. · ¿Qué hora es?
cards.exampleNative: I don't have time today. · What time is it?
cards.remember: hora = clock time; tiempo = an amount of time (and the weather).

cards.target: la mañana · mañana
cards.native: the morning · tomorrow
cards.exampleTarget: Mañana en la mañana tengo una cita.
cards.exampleNative: Tomorrow morning I have an appointment.

cards.target: hoy · mañana · pasado mañana
cards.native: today · tomorrow · the day after tomorrow
cards.exampleTarget: Hoy tengo clase, mañana no, pero pasado mañana sí.
cards.exampleNative: Today I have class, tomorrow no, but the day after tomorrow yes.

cards.target: temprano / tarde
cards.native: early / late
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo que llegar temprano; no puedo llegar tarde.
cards.exampleNative: I have to arrive early; I can't arrive late.
cards.remember: la tarde = the afternoon.
cards.replyTarget: ¿A qué hora tienes que estar ahí?
cards.replyNative: What time do you have to be there?

cards.target: primero · después
cards.native: first · after, later
cards.exampleTarget: Primero tengo que llamar al banco y después tengo que comer.
cards.exampleNative: First I have to call the bank and then I have to eat.

cards.target: a veces · casi · normalmente
cards.native: sometimes · almost · usually
cards.exampleTarget: Casi siempre estoy ocupado. A veces tengo flojera.
cards.exampleNative: I'm almost always busy. Sometimes I don't feel like it.
cards.replyNative: What do you do to relax?

cards.target: cero · uno · dos · tres · cuatro · cinco
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo dos hijos y tres perros.
cards.exampleNative: I have two children and three dogs.
cards.remember: Before a noun uno (one) becomes un or una (a): un taco, una plaza (a square).

cards.target: seis · siete · ocho · nueve · diez
cards.exampleTarget: Son las ocho. La clase es a las nueve.
cards.exampleNative: It's eight. Class is at nine.

cards.target: dieciséis · diecisiete · dieciocho · diecinueve · veinte
cards.exampleTarget: Valentina tiene dieciocho años.
cards.exampleNative: Valentina is eighteen.
cards.remember: 16 to 19 fuse into one word: diez y seis → dieciséis (sixteen).
cards.replyNative: Is she going to university yet?

cards.target: veintiuno · veintidós · veintitrés · veinticuatro · veinticinco
cards.exampleTarget: Luis tiene veintidós años. Hay veintiún tacos.
cards.exampleNative: Luis is twenty-two. There are twenty-one tacos.
cards.remember: 21 to 29 are one word. Before a noun: veintiún, veintiuna (twenty-one).

cards.target: veintiséis · veintisiete · veintiocho · veintinueve
cards.exampleTarget: Hoy es el veintiocho de octubre.
cards.exampleNative: Today is October twenty-eighth.

cards.target: treinta · cuarenta · cincuenta · sesenta
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo cincuenta pesos.
cards.exampleNative: I have fifty pesos.
cards.remember: 31 to 99: tens + y (and) + ones: treinta y uno (thirty-one).
cards.replyNative: Is that enough for the bus?

cards.target: setenta · ochenta · noventa · cien
cards.exampleTarget: Mi abuela tiene setenta y ocho años. Son cien pesos.
cards.exampleNative: My grandma is seventy-eight. It's a hundred pesos.
cards.remember: cien = exactly 100.
cards.replyTarget: Está muy bien para su edad.
cards.replyNative: She's doing very well for her age.

cards.target: treinta y uno · cuarenta y siete · noventa y nueve
cards.exampleTarget: Son noventa y nueve pesos.
cards.exampleNative: It's ninety-nine pesos.
cards.remember: Three words: tens + y (and) + ones.

cards.target: ciento uno · ciento cincuenta · ciento noventa y nueve
cards.exampleTarget: El jarabe cuesta ciento cincuenta pesos.
cards.exampleNative: The syrup costs a hundred fifty pesos.
cards.remember: 101 to 199 use ciento (one hundred).
cards.replyNative: Do you have a cheaper one?

cards.target: doscient@s · trescient@s · cuatrocient@s · seiscient@s · ochocient@s
cards.exampleTarget: Son doscientos veinte pesos. Hay trescientas casas.
cards.exampleNative: It's two hundred twenty pesos. There are three hundred houses.
cards.remember: Hundreds match the noun: doscientos pesos (two hundred pesos), doscientas casas (two hundred houses).

cards.target: quinient@s · setecient@s · novecient@s
cards.exampleTarget: Son quinientos pesos.
cards.exampleNative: It's five hundred pesos.
cards.remember: The three that break the pattern (500 is quinientos, not cincocientos).
cards.replyNative: Can you give me a discount?

cards.target: mil · un millón
cards.exampleTarget: Son mil quinientos cuarenta pesos.
cards.exampleNative: It's one thousand five hundred forty pesos.
cards.remember: mil (thousand) never takes un (a). y (and) joins only tens and ones: doscientos cincuenta y tres (253).
cards.replyNative: Can I pay it in two parts?

cards.target: lunes · martes · miércoles · jueves · viernes · sábado · domingo
cards.native: Monday · Tuesday · Wednesday · Thursday · Friday · Saturday · Sunday
cards.exampleTarget: La clase es el jueves. Tengo clase los martes y los jueves.
cards.exampleNative: Class is on Thursday. I have class on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
cards.remember: Lowercase. el lunes = on Monday; los lunes = on Mondays.

cards.target: enero · febrero · marzo · abril · mayo · junio
cards.native: January · February · March · April · May · June
cards.exampleTarget: Mi cumpleaños es en junio.
cards.exampleNative: My birthday is in June.
cards.remember: Months are lowercase and take en (in).

cards.target: julio · agosto · septiembre · octubre · noviembre · diciembre
cards.native: July · August · September · October · November · December
cards.exampleTarget: Hoy es el cinco de noviembre.
cards.exampleNative: Today is November fifth.

cards.target: la primavera · el verano · el otoño · el invierno
cards.native: spring · summer · fall · winter
cards.exampleTarget: En verano tengo mucho calor y en invierno tengo frío.
cards.exampleNative: In summer I'm very hot and in winter I'm cold.
cards.remember: Seasons take en (in). Spring is the only feminine one.

cards.target: el primero
cards.native: the first (of the month)
cards.exampleTarget: Mi cumpleaños es el primero de mayo.
cards.exampleNative: My birthday is May first.
cards.remember: The only date that isn't a plain number.
cards.replyNative: And what are you going to do?

cards.target: esta mañana · esta tarde · esta noche
cards.native: this morning · this afternoon · tonight
cards.exampleTarget: Esta noche tengo que preparar la cena.
cards.exampleNative: Tonight I have to make dinner.
cards.remember: A specific one.
cards.replyNative: What are you going to make?

cards.target: en la mañana · en la tarde · en la noche
cards.native: in the morning · in the afternoon · at night
cards.exampleTarget: En la mañana estoy en el trabajo.
cards.exampleNative: In the morning I'm at work.
cards.remember: In general. Mexico says en la (in the), not por la.

cards.target: al mediodía · a la medianoche
cards.native: at noon · at midnight
cards.exampleTarget: La reunión es al mediodía.
cards.exampleNative: The meeting is at noon.

cards.target: el próximo lunes · la próxima semana · el próximo mes · el próximo año
cards.native: next Monday · next week · next month · next year
cards.exampleTarget: La próxima semana tengo un examen.
cards.exampleNative: Next week I have an exam.
cards.remember: próximo matches the noun.

cards.target: este mes · esta semana · este año
cards.native: this month · this week · this year
cards.exampleTarget: Esta semana estoy muy ocupado.
cards.exampleNative: This week I'm very busy.
cards.remember: este / esta (this) matches the noun.

cards.target: ¿qué hora es?
cards.native: what time is it?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Qué hora es? → Son las tres.
cards.exampleNative: What time is it? → It's three.

cards.target: es la una · son las dos
cards.native: it's one o'clock · it's two o'clock
cards.exampleTarget: Es la una. · Son las dos.
cards.exampleNative: It's one o'clock. · It's two o'clock.
cards.remember: Only one o'clock is singular.

cards.target: y cuarto · y media · en punto
cards.native: quarter past · half past · on the dot
cards.exampleTarget: Son las cinco y cuarto. Son las cuatro y media. Son las tres en punto.
cards.exampleNative: It's a quarter past five. It's four thirty. It's three o'clock sharp.
cards.remember: Minutes: y + number: son las dos y diez (it's ten past two).

cards.target: de la mañana · de la tarde · de la noche
cards.native: a.m. · in the afternoon · at night (with a clock time)
cards.exampleTarget: Son las ocho de la mañana.
cards.exampleNative: It's eight in the morning.

cards.target: el mediodía · la medianoche
cards.native: noon · midnight
cards.exampleTarget: Es el mediodía.
cards.exampleNative: It's noon.

cards.target: a las … · a la una
cards.native: at … o'clock · at one o'clock
cards.exampleTarget: La clase es a las nueve. La cita es a la una.
cards.exampleNative: Class is at nine. The appointment is at one.
cards.remember: For when something happens.

cards.target: los martes
cards.native: on Tuesdays (every week)
cards.exampleTarget: Mis clases son los lunes y los miércoles.
cards.exampleNative: My classes are on Mondays and Wednesdays.
cards.replyNative: And what do you do on Tuesdays?

cards.target: al · del
cards.native: a + el always squeezes into al; de + el into del. Never with la, los, las.
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo que ir al banco. La farmacia está al lado del banco.
cards.exampleNative: I have to go to the bank. The pharmacy is next to the bank.
cards.meaning: to the · of the, from the

cards.target: estoy · estás · está · estamos · están
cards.native: estar = how or where someone or something is right now. Memory aid PLACE: Position, Location, Actions in progress (later), Condition, Emotions.
cards.exampleTarget: Estoy sentado. El banco está en el centro. La puerta está cerrada. Estoy contento.
cards.exampleNative: I'm sitting. The bank is downtown. The door is closed. I'm happy.
cards.meaning: I am · you are · he / she is, you (polite) are · we are · they are, you all are

cards.target: Mi mamá está en la cocina y está ocupada.
cards.native: estar can do two jobs in one sentence: where and how, joined with y.
cards.exampleTarget: Estamos de vacaciones y estamos muy contentos.
cards.exampleNative: We're on vacation and we're very happy.
cards.meaning: My mom is in the kitchen and she's busy.

cards.target: Estoy sentad@. · Estoy de pie.
cards.native: Body position is estar + a describing word that agrees. de pie never changes.
cards.exampleTarget: La niña está sentada. Los niños están parados.
cards.exampleNative: The girl is sitting. The boys are standing.
cards.remember: parado = standing in Mexico, unemployed in Spain.
cards.meaning: I'm sitting down. · I'm standing up.
cards.replyNative: Do you want to sit down?

cards.target: El gato está encima de la mesa.
cards.native: Place words link to the place with de (de + el = del). Drop de when no place follows. entre uses y.
cards.exampleTarget: El perro está afuera. Está entre el banco y la farmacia.
cards.exampleNative: The dog is outside. It's between the bank and the pharmacy.
cards.remember: aquí (here), allí, ahí (there), allá (over there) never take de (of).
cards.meaning: The cat is on top of the table.

cards.target: aquí · ahí · allá
cards.native: Distance: aquí near me, ahí / allí near you, allá far from both. The pointing words follow the same three steps: este, ese, aquel.
cards.exampleTarget: Estoy aquí, tu taza está ahí y el banco está allá.
cards.exampleNative: I'm here, your cup is there and the bank is over there.
cards.meaning: here · there (near you) · over there

cards.target: Estoy un poco cansad@. · Todavía estoy nervioso.
cards.native: How-much words (un poco, muy, bastante, demasiado) sit right before the describing word. todavía and ya usually come before estar.
cards.exampleTarget: Ya estoy lista. Estás bastante ocupado.
cards.exampleNative: I'm ready now. You're quite busy.
cards.remember: muy = very (neutral); demasiado = too much, a problem.
cards.meaning: I'm a little tired. · I'm still nervous.

cards.target: mesa · silla · sillón · sofá
cards.native: table · chair · armchair · sofa
cards.exampleTarget: La silla está al lado de la mesa.
cards.exampleNative: The chair is next to the table.
cards.remember: sillón is a "big chair": silla (chair) + -ón.

cards.target: cama · escritorio · cajón
cards.native: bed · desk · drawer
cards.exampleTarget: El perro está debajo de la cama.
cards.exampleNative: The dog is under the bed.

cards.target: puerta · ventana
cards.native: door · window
cards.exampleTarget: La puerta está cerrada y la ventana está abierta.
cards.exampleNative: The door is closed and the window is open.

cards.target: refri · taza · plato · botella
cards.native: fridge · cup · plate · bottle
cards.exampleTarget: La botella está en el refri.
cards.exampleNative: The bottle is in the fridge.
cards.replyNative: Can you pass it to me?

cards.target: llave · mochila · bolsa · bolso
cards.native: key · backpack · bag, purse
cards.exampleTarget: Las llaves están adentro de la mochila.
cards.exampleNative: The keys are inside the backpack.
cards.replyTarget: ¡Ah, gracias! Ya me iba sin ellas.
cards.replyNative: Oh, thanks! I was about to leave without them.

cards.target: teléfono · celular · computadora
cards.native: phone · cell phone · computer
cards.exampleTarget: Mi celular está apagado.
cards.exampleNative: My cell phone is off.

cards.target: control remoto · altavoz · bocina
cards.native: remote control · speaker · speaker (MX)
cards.exampleTarget: El control remoto está entre los libros.
cards.exampleNative: The remote is between the books.
cards.replyNative: Oh, thanks. What shall we watch?

cards.target: libro · capítulo · mapa
cards.native: book · chapter · map
cards.exampleTarget: Este capítulo es muy largo.
cards.exampleNative: This chapter is very long.
cards.remember: mapa (map) is masculine despite the -a.
cards.replyNative: How many pages does it have?

cards.target: carro (m.) · moto (f.)
cards.native: car · motorcycle
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Tienes carro o moto? → Tengo moto.
cards.exampleNative: Do you have a car or a motorcycle? → I have a motorcycle.
cards.remember: moto (motorbike) is feminine despite the -o.

cards.target: planta · árbol · banca · barda
cards.native: plant · tree · bench · low wall, fence
cards.exampleTarget: El gato está encima de la barda.
cards.exampleNative: The cat is on top of the fence.
cards.replyNative: How did it get up there?

cards.target: cosa (f.) · ropa (f.)
cards.native: thing · clothes
cards.exampleTarget: La ropa está en el piso.
cards.exampleNative: The clothes are on the floor.
cards.remember: ropa (clothes) is singular: la ropa está (the clothes are).
cards.replyNative: Will you help me pick it up?

cards.target: foto (f.)
cards.native: photo
cards.exampleTarget: Esta foto es muy bonita.
cards.exampleNative: This photo is very pretty.
cards.remember: Feminine despite the -o (short for fotografía).

cards.target: asiento (m.)
cards.native: seat
cards.exampleTarget: Este asiento está ocupado.
cards.exampleNative: This seat is taken.

cards.target: gat@ · perr@ · mascota (f.)
cards.native: cat · dog · pet
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo un perro y un gato.
cards.exampleNative: I have a dog and a cat.

cards.target: boletos (m.)
cards.native: tickets
cards.exampleTarget: Tenemos los boletos para el concierto.
cards.exampleNative: We have the tickets for the concert.

cards.target: content@ · feliz / triste
cards.native: happy / sad
cards.exampleTarget: Estoy contento, no estoy triste.
cards.exampleNative: I'm happy, I'm not sad.

cards.target: cansad@
cards.native: tired
cards.exampleTarget: Estoy un poco cansada, pero estoy bien.
cards.exampleNative: I'm a little tired, but I'm fine.
cards.remember: Close cousin: tengo sueño, I'm sleepy.
cards.replyNative: Do you want to rest for a while?

cards.target: enojad@ / tranquil@
cards.native: angry / calm
cards.exampleTarget: Canela está enojada, pero el gato está tranquilo.
cards.exampleNative: Canela is angry, but the cat is calm.

cards.target: nervios@ · preocupad@
cards.native: nervous · worried
cards.exampleTarget: Estoy nervioso por el examen. Mi mamá está preocupada.
cards.exampleNative: I'm nervous about the exam. My mom is worried.
cards.remember: preocupado looks like preoccupied.

cards.target: aburrid@ · ocupad@
cards.native: bored · busy, taken
cards.exampleTarget: Hoy estoy aburrido. Mi papá está muy ocupado.
cards.exampleNative: Today I'm bored. My dad is very busy.
cards.remember: With ser, aburrido means boring.
cards.replyNative: Do you want to go for a walk?

cards.target: emocionad@ · orgullos@ (de)
cards.native: excited · proud (of)
cards.exampleTarget: Estoy muy orgulloso de mi hija.
cards.exampleNative: I'm very proud of my daughter.

cards.target: enferm@ / san@
cards.native: sick / healthy
cards.exampleTarget: Mi hermano está enfermo. La fruta es muy sana.
cards.exampleNative: My brother is sick. Fruit is very healthy.
cards.remember: With ser, sano means good for you.

cards.target: crud@
cards.native: hungover (MX) · raw
cards.exampleTarget: No estoy triste, estoy crudo.
cards.exampleNative: I'm not sad, I'm hungover.
cards.remember: From crudo, raw.

cards.target: dormid@ / despiert@
cards.native: asleep / awake
cards.exampleTarget: El perro está dormido y los niños están despiertos.
cards.exampleNative: The dog is asleep and the kids are awake.

cards.target: perdid@
cards.native: lost
cards.exampleTarget: Estoy un poco perdido. No soy de aquí.
cards.exampleNative: I'm a little lost. I'm not from here.

cards.target: sol@ / junt@s
cards.native: alone / together
cards.exampleTarget: No estoy sola, estoy con mi familia. Estamos juntos.
cards.exampleNative: I'm not alone, I'm with my family. We're together.
cards.remember: sólo (only) never changes; sola (alone) agrees.

cards.target: viv@
cards.native: alive
cards.exampleTarget: Las plantas todavía están vivas.
cards.exampleNative: The plants are still alive.
cards.remember: With ser, vivo means sharp, quick.
cards.replyNative: Do you water them every day?

cards.target: sentad@ · parad@ · acostad@ · formad@ · de pie
cards.native: sitting · standing · lying down · standing in line · standing
cards.exampleTarget: Estoy sentado en el sofá y mi hijo está parado.
cards.exampleNative: I'm sitting on the sofa and my son is standing.
cards.remember: They agree like any describing word, except de pie (standing), which never changes.
cards.replyNative: Do you want to sit down too?

cards.target: abiert@ / cerrad@
cards.native: open / closed
cards.exampleTarget: El banco está abierto, pero la farmacia está cerrada.
cards.exampleNative: The bank is open, but the pharmacy is closed.
cards.replyNative: What time does the pharmacy open?

cards.target: encendid@ / apagad@
cards.native: on, turned on / off, turned off
cards.exampleTarget: La computadora está encendida y el altavoz está apagado.
cards.exampleNative: The computer is on and the speaker is off.

cards.target: limpi@ / suci@
cards.native: clean / dirty
cards.exampleTarget: La cocina está limpia, pero los platos están sucios.
cards.exampleNative: The kitchen is clean, but the dishes are dirty.

cards.target: ordenad@ / desordenad@
cards.native: tidy / messy
cards.exampleTarget: La sala está ordenada y mi cuarto está desordenado.
cards.exampleNative: The living room is tidy and my room is messy.
cards.remember: With ser, a tidy or messy person by habit.

cards.target: vací@ · rot@
cards.native: empty · broken
cards.exampleTarget: Los platos están vacíos y la silla está rota.
cards.exampleNative: The plates are empty and the chair is broken.
cards.remember: roto comes from romper, to break.

cards.target: frí@ / caliente
cards.native: cold / hot (a thing)
cards.exampleTarget: El café está frío y la comida está caliente.
cards.exampleNative: The coffee is cold and the food is hot.
cards.remember: A person uses tener: tengo frío (I'm cold), tengo calor (I'm hot).
cards.replyNative: Shall I heat it up for you?

cards.target: ahora · ya · todavía
cards.native: now · already, now (it changed) · still (no change)
cards.exampleTarget: Todavía estoy nervioso, pero ya estoy listo.
cards.exampleNative: I'm still nervous, but I'm ready now.
cards.remember: todavía (still) and ya (already, now) usually come before estar.

cards.target: aquí · acá / allí · ahí / allá
cards.native: here / there (near you) / over there (far)
cards.exampleTarget: Estoy aquí. Tu taza está ahí. El banco está allá.
cards.exampleNative: I'm here. Your cup is there. The bank is over there.
cards.remember: These never take de.
cards.replyNative: Over there, across from the plaza?

cards.target: cerca / lejos
cards.native: near / far (nothing follows)
cards.exampleTarget: La farmacia no está lejos, está muy cerca.
cards.exampleNative: The pharmacy isn't far, it's very close.
cards.remember: With a place after: cerca de (near), lejos de (far from).

cards.target: adentro / afuera
cards.native: inside / outside (nothing follows)
cards.exampleTarget: El perro está afuera y el gato está adentro.
cards.exampleNative: The dog is outside and the cat is inside.
cards.remember: With a place after: adentro de (inside), afuera de (outside).

cards.target: sólo · solo
cards.native: only, just
cards.exampleTarget: No estoy triste, sólo estoy cansado.
cards.exampleNative: I'm not sad, I'm just tired.
cards.remember: Never changes. Don't confuse it with sol@, which means alone.

cards.target: muy
cards.native: very
cards.exampleTarget: Estamos muy contentos.
cards.exampleNative: We're very happy.
cards.remember: Sits right before the describing word.

cards.target: un poco · un poquito
cards.native: a little · a tiny bit
cards.exampleTarget: Estoy un poco triste.
cards.exampleNative: I'm a little sad.
cards.remember: The -ito ending shrinks any word.

cards.target: bastante
cards.native: quite, pretty
cards.exampleTarget: Estás bastante ocupado.
cards.exampleNative: You're quite busy.
cards.remember: From bastar, to be enough. ¡Basta! = Enough!
cards.replyNative: Yes, I have a lot of work.

cards.target: demasiado
cards.native: too, too much (a problem)
cards.exampleTarget: Están demasiado cansados.
cards.exampleNative: They're too tired.
cards.remember: muy (very) is neutral; demasiado (too much) means it's a problem.

cards.target: en
cards.native: in · on · at (the general spot)
cards.exampleTarget: Estoy en casa. Las llaves están en la mesa.
cards.exampleNative: I'm at home. The keys are on the table.
cards.replyNative: Will you hand them to me?

cards.target: a · al
cards.native: to · at (a + el = al)
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo que ir al banco y a la farmacia.
cards.exampleNative: I have to go to the bank and to the pharmacy.
cards.remember: a (to) + el (the) always squeezes into al.

cards.target: con / sin
cards.native: with / without
cards.exampleTarget: Estoy con mi familia. Estoy sin mi teléfono.
cards.exampleNative: I'm with my family. I'm without my phone.
cards.remember: un café con leche (coffee with milk) · un café sin leche (coffee without milk)
cards.replyNative: Did you leave it at home?

cards.target: encima de / debajo de
cards.native: on top of / under
cards.exampleTarget: El teléfono está encima de la mesa y el perro está debajo de la cama.
cards.exampleNative: The phone is on top of the table and the dog is under the bed.
cards.remember: Most place words link with de (of); de + el = del (of the).

cards.target: arriba de
cards.native: above
cards.exampleTarget: La foto está arriba de la cama.
cards.exampleNative: The photo is above the bed.
cards.remember: arriba alone = up, upstairs.

cards.target: adentro de / afuera de
cards.native: inside / outside
cards.exampleTarget: Las llaves están adentro de la mochila.
cards.exampleNative: The keys are inside the backpack.

cards.target: enfrente de · delante de / detrás de
cards.native: in front of, across from · ahead of / behind
cards.exampleTarget: La parada está enfrente de la farmacia. Mi mochila está detrás de la puerta.
cards.exampleNative: The stop is across from the pharmacy. My backpack is behind the door.
cards.replyNative: How often does the bus come?

cards.target: al lado de
cards.native: next to, beside
cards.exampleTarget: La farmacia está al lado del banco.
cards.exampleNative: The pharmacy is next to the bank.
cards.remember: lado = side, like lateral.
cards.replyNative: Thanks. Is it open right now?

cards.target: entre … y …
cards.native: between … and …
cards.exampleTarget: La farmacia está entre el banco y la papelería.
cards.exampleNative: The pharmacy is between the bank and the stationery store.
cards.remember: entre (between) links with y (and), not de (of).

cards.target: cerca de / lejos de
cards.native: near / far from
cards.exampleTarget: El hotel está cerca del mercado y lejos del aeropuerto.
cards.exampleNative: The hotel is near the market and far from the airport.
cards.replyNative: Perfect, that way we can walk to the market.

cards.target: por aquí · en su lugar
cards.native: around here · in its place
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Hay una farmacia por aquí? Todo está en su lugar.
cards.exampleNative: Is there a pharmacy around here? Everything is in its place.
cards.replyTarget: Sí, hay una en la esquina.
cards.replyNative: Yes, there's one on the corner.

cards.target:
estar · present
yo estoy · tú estás · él / ella / usted está · nosotros estamos · ellos / ustedes están
cards.native:
to be (how / where someone is now) · present
I am · you are · he/she is / you (form.) are · we are · they / you all are
cards.exampleTarget: Estoy en casa y estoy un poco cansado.
cards.exampleNative: I'm at home and I'm a little tired.
cards.remember: PLACE uses: how and where right now.

cards.target: tengo · tienes · tiene · tenemos · tienen
cards.native: tener = to have. Memory aid PASO: Possession, Age, Sensation, Obligation.
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo un carro. Tengo 59 años. Tengo hambre. Tengo que trabajar.
cards.exampleNative: I have a car. I'm 59. I'm hungry. I have to work.
cards.meaning: I have · you have · he / she has, you (polite) have · we have · they have, you all have
cards.replyNative: Do you want to eat something?

cards.target: Tengo treinta años.
cards.native: Age uses tener ("I have 30 years"), never ser or estar.
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Cuántos años tienes? → Tengo cincuenta y nueve años.
cards.exampleNative: How old are you? → I'm fifty-nine.
cards.remember: ✗ Soy treinta. ✗ Estoy treinta años. (I'm thirty is Tengo treinta años.)
cards.meaning: I'm thirty years old.

cards.target: Tengo hambre. · Tengo frío.
cards.native: English "I am hungry / cold / sleepy / afraid / in a hurry / right / lucky" becomes tener + a noun, with no article.
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo sed. Tiene miedo. Tenemos prisa.
cards.exampleNative: I'm thirsty. He's afraid. We're in a hurry.
cards.remember: ✗ Tengo la sed. (I'm thirsty is Tengo sed.)
cards.meaning: I'm hungry. · I'm cold.

cards.target: Tengo mucha hambre. · Tengo mucho frío.
cards.native: "Very" with a tener feeling is mucho / mucha, matching the noun's gender: hambre, sed, prisa, suerte, razón are feminine; frío, calor, sueño, miedo are masculine.
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo mucha sed y mucho sueño.
cards.exampleNative: I'm very thirsty and very sleepy.
cards.remember: A little: un poco de frío (a little cold).
cards.meaning: I'm very hungry. · I'm very cold.

cards.target: Tengo frío. · El café está frío.
cards.native: A PERSON feels cold or hot with tener; a THING is cold or hot with estar.
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo calor, pero el café está frío.
cards.exampleNative: I'm hot, but the coffee is cold.
cards.remember: Never say estoy caliente about yourself: it means aroused, not warm.
cards.meaning: I'm cold. · The coffee is cold.

cards.target: Tengo que pagar.
cards.native: Obligation is tener + que + infinitive. Keep the que. Only tener changes; the second verb stays in its base form.
cards.exampleTarget: Tenemos que trabajar hoy. ¿Tienes que estudiar?
cards.exampleNative: We have to work today. Do you have to study?
cards.remember: ✗ Tengo pagar (that just means "I have").
cards.meaning: I have to pay.
cards.replyNative: Yes, I have a test tomorrow.

cards.target: Hay leche. · Hay tres perros.
