cards.native: hay = there is / there are. It never changes for one or many.
cards.exampleTarget: Hay una farmacia en la esquina. No hay nadie.
cards.exampleNative: There's a pharmacy on the corner. There's nobody.
cards.remember: hay que + infinitive = one has to: Hay que lavar los platos.
cards.meaning: There's milk. · There are three dogs.

cards.group: Rules: how Spanish relates to English
cards.target: hambre · hijo · hacer
cards.native: Many Latin f- words turned into a silent h-: fames → hambre (famished), filius → hijo (filial), facere → hacer (factory).
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo hambre.
cards.exampleNative: I'm hungry.
cards.remember: The h is always silent.
cards.meaning: hunger · son · to do, to make

cards.group: Rules: how Spanish relates to English
cards.target: Tengo hambre. · Tengo 30 años.
cards.native: Spanish often "has" what English "is": hungry, thirsty, cold, hot, sleepy, afraid, in a hurry, right, lucky, and years old.
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo calor y tengo sueño.
cards.exampleNative: I'm hot and I'm sleepy.
cards.meaning: I'm hungry. · I'm 30 years old.

cards.group: Rules: how Spanish relates to English
cards.target: dos apellidos
cards.native: Mexicans carry two last names: father's first, then mother's. Day to day they go by the first one.
cards.exampleTarget: María García Hernández = Sra. García
cards.exampleNative: María García Hernández goes by García.
cards.remember: Parents can now agree on the order.
cards.meaning: two last names

cards.target: ¿cuántos? · ¿cuántas?
cards.native: how many?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Cuántos años tienes? · ¿Cuántas hermanas tienes?
cards.exampleNative: How old are you? · How many sisters do you have?
cards.remember: Matches the noun.

cards.target: ¿cuánto es? · ¿cuánto cuesta?
cards.native: how much is it? · how much does it cost?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Cuánto cuesta el kilo de fruta? → Treinta pesos.
cards.exampleNative: How much is a kilo of fruit? → Thirty pesos.

cards.target: comida · cena · desayuno
cards.native: food, meal · dinner · breakfast
cards.exampleTarget: La cena está lista.
cards.exampleNative: Dinner is ready.

cards.target: tacos · taco de birria · torta
cards.native: tacos · birria taco · sandwich (MX)
cards.exampleTarget: Los tacos están muy ricos.
cards.exampleNative: The tacos are really tasty.
cards.replyNative: Can you give me two more, please?

cards.target: salsa (f.)
cards.native: salsa · sauce
cards.exampleTarget: La salsa de mi mamá está muy rica.
cards.exampleNative: My mom's salsa is really tasty.

cards.target: fruta · manzana
cards.native: fruit · apple
cards.exampleTarget: Esta fruta todavía está verde.
cards.exampleNative: This fruit isn't ripe yet.
cards.replyNative: Then I'd better take that one.

cards.target: leche (f.) · agua (f.) · café (m.)
cards.native: milk · water · coffee
cards.exampleTarget: No hay leche, pero hay agua.
cards.exampleNative: There's no milk, but there's water.
cards.remember: agua (water) is feminine but takes el: el agua.
cards.replyTarget: Voy a la tienda por leche.
cards.replyNative: I'm going to the store for milk.

cards.target: bebida (f.) · tequila (m.)
cards.native: drink, beverage · tequila
cards.exampleTarget: Hay bebidas para todos.
cards.exampleNative: There are drinks for everyone.

cards.target: pastel (m.)
cards.native: cake
cards.exampleTarget: El pastel está en la mesa.
cards.exampleNative: The cake is on the table.

cards.target: mariscos (m.)
cards.native: seafood
cards.exampleTarget: Los mariscos están deliciosos.
cards.exampleNative: The seafood is delicious.

cards.target: medicina · pastilla · jarabe
cards.native: medicine · pill · syrup, cough syrup
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo que tomar una pastilla.
cards.exampleNative: I have to take a pill.
cards.remember: medicina (medicine) is also the field of study.

cards.target: receta · dosis
cards.native: prescription · dose
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Tiene receta, señora?
cards.exampleNative: Do you have a prescription, ma'am?
cards.remember: receta (prescription) also means recipe.

cards.target: cita · turno
cards.native: appointment · turn, appointment slot
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo una cita con el doctor a las cinco.
cards.exampleNative: I have an appointment with the doctor at five.

cards.target: fiebre (f.) · tos (f.)
cards.native: fever · cough
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo tos y un poco de fiebre.
cards.exampleNative: I have a cough and a bit of a fever.
cards.remember: With tener, no article: tengo fiebre (I have a fever).

cards.target: seguro (m.)
cards.native: insurance
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Tiene seguro? → Sí, tengo seguro.
cards.exampleNative: Do you have insurance? → Yes, I have insurance.

cards.target: dinero · efectivo · tarjeta
cards.native: money · cash · card
cards.exampleTarget: No tengo efectivo, pero tengo tarjeta.
cards.exampleNative: I don't have cash, but I have a card.

cards.target: peso · billete · cambio
cards.native: peso · bill (paper money) · change
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo un billete de cincuenta pesos.
cards.exampleNative: I have a fifty-peso bill.
cards.remember: peso (the currency) also means weight.

cards.target: precio · descuento · total
cards.native: price · discount · total
cards.exampleTarget: El total es doscientos veinte pesos.
cards.exampleNative: The total is two hundred twenty pesos.

cards.target: precios · razonables
cards.native: prices · reasonable
cards.exampleTarget: Los precios son razonables.
cards.exampleNative: The prices are reasonable.

cards.target: cuenta · pago
cards.native: bill, tab · payment
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo que pagar la cuenta.
cards.exampleNative: I have to pay the bill.
cards.replyNative: Can you bring me the check, please?

cards.target: caja · ventanilla · fila
cards.native: checkout counter · service counter · line, queue
cards.exampleTarget: La fila es muy larga.
cards.exampleNative: The line is very long.

cards.target: mandado · lista
cards.native: groceries, errand · shopping list
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo la lista del mandado.
cards.exampleNative: I have the grocery list.
cards.remember: In Mexico el mandado (the errands) is above all the food shopping.
cards.replyNative: Shall we go to the supermarket?

cards.target: producto · kilo · litro
cards.native: product · kilogram · liter
cards.exampleTarget: Son veinte pesos el litro.
cards.exampleNative: It's twenty pesos a liter.

cards.target: nombre · apellido · número
cards.native: name, first name · last name · number
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Cuál es tu apellido?
cards.exampleNative: What's your last name?
cards.remember: Mexicans carry two apellidos (last names) and go by the first one.

cards.target: tarea (f.)
cards.native: homework
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo mucha tarea.
cards.exampleNative: I have a lot of homework.

cards.target: much@ · mucho
cards.native: a lot of (matches the noun) · a lot (after a verb)
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo mucha hambre y mucho trabajo. Tengo que estudiar mucho.
cards.exampleNative: I'm very hungry and I have a lot of work. I have to study a lot.
cards.remember: With a noun it agrees; after a verb it never changes.

cards.target: poco · poco tiempo
cards.native: little, not much · not much time
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo mucha hambre y poco tiempo.
cards.exampleNative: I'm very hungry and I have little time.
cards.replyNative: There's a little diner near here.

cards.target: estar de vacaciones · estar de viaje
cards.native: to be on vacation · to be on a trip
cards.exampleTarget: Mis padres están de viaje en Oaxaca.
cards.exampleNative: My parents are on a trip in Oaxaca.

cards.target: estar bien · estar mal
cards.native: to be fine · to not be fine
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Cómo estás? → Estoy bien, gracias.
cards.exampleNative: How are you? → I'm fine, thanks.

cards.target: está ric@
cards.native: it tastes great
cards.exampleTarget: ¡La comida está muy rica!
cards.exampleNative: The food tastes great!
cards.replyNative: Will you give me the recipe?

cards.target: tener hambre · tener sed
cards.native: to be hungry · to be thirsty
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo mucha hambre y un poco de sed.
cards.exampleNative: I'm very hungry and a little thirsty.
cards.remember: No article. hambre (hunger) and sed (thirst) are feminine: mucha hambre (very hungry).

cards.target: tener frío · tener calor
cards.native: to be cold · to be hot (a person)
cards.exampleTarget: En la oficina siempre tengo frío.
cards.exampleNative: I'm always cold at the office.
cards.remember: Masculine: mucho frío (very cold). A thing está frío (is cold).

cards.target: tener sueño · tener prisa
cards.native: to be sleepy · to be in a hurry
cards.exampleTarget: Hoy tengo sueño y tengo prisa.
cards.exampleNative: Today I'm sleepy and I'm in a hurry.
cards.remember: sueño (sleepiness) is masculine; prisa (hurry) is feminine.
cards.replyNative: What time did you go to bed?

cards.target: tener miedo
cards.native: to be afraid
cards.exampleTarget: El perro tiene miedo.
cards.exampleNative: The dog is afraid.
cards.replyTarget: No pasa nada, es un perro bueno.
cards.replyNative: It's fine, he's a good dog.

cards.target: tener suerte · tener razón
cards.native: to be lucky · to be right
cards.exampleTarget: ¡Tienes suerte! · Tienes razón.
cards.exampleNative: You're lucky! · You're right.

cards.target: tener flojera
cards.native: to not feel like doing anything (MX)
cards.exampleTarget: Hoy tengo flojera.
cards.exampleNative: I don't feel like doing anything today.

cards.target: tener fiebre · tener tos
cards.native: to have a fever · to have a cough
cards.exampleTarget: Mi hija tiene tos, pero no tiene fiebre.
cards.exampleNative: My daughter has a cough, but she doesn't have a fever.
cards.replyNative: Have you gone to the doctor yet?

cards.target: tener cara de cansad@
cards.native: to look tired
cards.exampleTarget: Tienes cara de cansado.
cards.exampleNative: You look tired.

cards.target: tener … años
cards.native: to be … years old
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo cincuenta y nueve años.
cards.exampleNative: I'm fifty-nine.
cards.remember: Age always uses tener.

cards.target: tener que + infinitive
cards.native: to have to (do something)
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo que ir a la farmacia.
cards.exampleNative: I have to go to the pharmacy.
cards.remember: Keep the que (tener que = to have to). Only tener changes.

cards.target: hay · no hay
cards.native: there is, there are · there isn't, there aren't
cards.exampleTarget: Hay leche en el refri, pero no hay café.
cards.exampleNative: There's milk in the fridge, but there's no coffee.
cards.remember: Never changes for one or many.
cards.replyNative: Shall we go to the store?

cards.target: toma asiento · tome asiento
cards.native: have a seat (tú · usted)
cards.exampleTarget: Buenos días, señora. Tome asiento.
cards.exampleNative: Good morning, ma'am. Have a seat.

cards.target:
tener · present
yo tengo · tú tienes · él / ella / usted tiene · nosotros tenemos · ellos / ustedes tienen
cards.native:
to have · present
I have · you have · he/she has / you (form.) have · we have · they / you all have
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo dos hijos y tengo que trabajar.
cards.exampleNative: I have two children and I have to work.
cards.remember: PASO uses: possession, age, sensation, obligation (tener que, to have to).

cards.target: ¿Dónde está el baño?
cards.native: With a question word, the order is ¿ + question word + verb + subject ?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Cuándo es la boda? · ¿Dónde están las llaves?
cards.exampleNative: When is the wedding? · Where are the keys?
cards.remember: ✗ ¿Dónde el baño está? (Say ¿Dónde está el baño?, where's the bathroom?)
cards.meaning: Where's the bathroom?

cards.target: ¿De dónde eres? · ¿A qué hora es?
cards.native: The little word (de, a) goes in front of the question word, never at the end like English.
cards.exampleTarget: ¿De qué país eres? · ¿A qué hora es la fiesta?
cards.exampleNative: What country are you from? · What time is the party?
cards.remember: ✗ ¿Dónde eres de? (Say ¿De dónde eres?, where are you from?)
cards.meaning: Where are you from? · What time is it at?

cards.target: qué · quién · dónde · cuándo · cómo · por qué
cards.native: Question words carry an accent when they ask, even inside a sentence (No sé dónde está). As plain connectors (donde vivo, cuando llego) they have no accent.
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Por qué estás aquí? → Porque tengo una cita.
cards.exampleNative: Why are you here? → Because I have an appointment.
cards.remember: por qué (why, two words, accent) ↔ porque (because, one word, no accent).
cards.meaning: what · who · where · when · how · why

cards.target: ¿Estás cansado? → No, no estoy cansado.
cards.native: Answering no: the first no answers, the second no makes the verb negative.
cards.exampleTarget: Laura es doctora, ¿no? → No, no es doctora. Es enfermera.
cards.exampleNative: Laura is a doctor, right? → No, she isn't a doctor. She's a nurse.
cards.remember: Correct someone with "No, no … + what's true".
cards.meaning: Are you tired? → No, I'm not tired.

cards.target: …, ¿no? · …, ¿verdad?
cards.native: Add ¿no? or ¿verdad? to the end of a statement to mean "right?".
cards.exampleTarget: Tienes frío, ¿verdad? → Sí, tengo mucho frío.
cards.exampleNative: You're cold, right? → Yes, I'm very cold.
cards.meaning: …, right? · …, right?

cards.target: No tengo nada. · Nunca estoy aburrida.
cards.native: Double negative: a no word AFTER the verb needs no in front of the verb too. A no word BEFORE the verb needs no extra no.
cards.exampleTarget: No hay nadie en casa. = Nadie está en casa.
cards.exampleNative: There's nobody home. = Nobody is home.
cards.remember: ✗ Nadie no está. · ✗ Tengo nada. (Say No está nadie, nobody's here · No tengo nada, I don't have anything.)
cards.meaning: I don't have anything. · I'm never bored.

cards.target: I don't have anything → No tengo nada.
cards.native: English "any" in a negative sentence keeps the Spanish no word.
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Tienes algo? → No, no tengo nada.
cards.exampleNative: Do you have anything? → No, I don't have anything.
cards.remember: ✗ No tengo algo. (Say No tengo nada, I don't have anything.)
cards.meaning: I don't have anything.

cards.target: algún problema · ningún problema
cards.native: algún / ningún stay singular even when English says "any ___s".
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Tienes algún problema? → No, no tengo ningún problema.
cards.exampleNative: Do you have any problems? → No, I don't have any problems.
cards.remember: algún (some), ningún (no) before masculine; alguna, ninguna before feminine.
cards.meaning: any problem · no problem
cards.replyTarget: Qué bueno. Avísame si necesitas algo.
cards.replyNative: Good. Let me know if you need anything.

cards.target: Yo también. · Yo tampoco.
cards.native: "Me too" after a yes sentence = también; "me neither" after a no sentence = tampoco.
cards.exampleTarget: Estoy cansada. → Yo también. · No tengo efectivo. → Yo tampoco.
cards.exampleNative: I'm tired. → Me too. · I don't have cash. → Me neither.
cards.meaning: Me too. · Me neither.

cards.target: Laura e Iván · siete u ocho
cards.native: y becomes e before an i sound; o becomes u before an o sound. It's about the sound.
cards.exampleTarget: madre e hija · mujer u hombre
cards.exampleNative: mother and daughter · woman or man
cards.meaning: Laura and Iván · seven or eight
cards.replyNative: How many are coming, seven or eight?

cards.target: ¿Dónde es la fiesta? → Es en mi casa.
cards.native: Where an EVENT takes place uses ser, not estar.
cards.exampleTarget: La boda es en el hotel. La reunión es a las ocho.
cards.exampleNative: The wedding is at the hotel. The meeting is at eight.
cards.remember: A person, thing or place uses estar: ¿Dónde está el baño? (Where's the bathroom?)
cards.meaning: Where's the party? → It's at my house.

cards.target: ¿Cómo es tu hermano? · ¿Cómo está tu hermano?
cards.native: cómo es asks what someone is like; cómo está asks how they are right now.
cards.exampleTarget: Es alto y chistoso. · Está enfermo.
cards.exampleNative: He's tall and funny. · He's sick.
cards.meaning: What's your brother like? · How's your brother doing?
cards.replyNative: I hope he gets better soon.

cards.target: He's tall · She's worried · I'm hungry · There's milk
cards.native: English "is / am / are" splits four ways: what it is like → ser; how or where it is → estar; feelings of the body and age → tener; there is → hay.
cards.exampleTarget: Es alto. · Está preocupada. · Tengo hambre. · Hay leche.
cards.exampleNative: He's tall. · She's worried. · I'm hungry. · There's milk.

cards.group: Rules: meaning that changes with the verb
cards.target: es list@ · está list@
cards.native: A few describing words change meaning with the verb: aburrido (boring / bored), bueno (good / still good), listo (clever / ready), malo (bad / gone bad), rico (rich / tasty), verde (green / not ripe), vivo (sharp / alive).
cards.exampleTarget: Carlos es muy listo. La cena ya está lista.
cards.exampleNative: Carlos is very clever. Dinner is ready now.
cards.meaning: is clever · is ready

cards.group: Rules: meaning that changes with the verb
cards.target: es barato · hoy está barato
cards.native: Most describing words keep their meaning: ser = what it's usually like, estar = how it is right now.
cards.exampleTarget: Mi carro es lento. Hoy la computadora está lenta.
cards.exampleNative: My car is slow. Today the computer is slow.
cards.meaning: it's cheap · today it's cheap

cards.group: Rules: meaning that changes with the verb
cards.target: Estoy mal. · La leche está mala.
cards.native: mal (how you are, like bien) never changes. malo / mala matches its noun.
cards.exampleTarget: Martha está mal hoy. Las frutas están malas.
cards.exampleNative: Martha isn't well today. The fruit has gone bad.
cards.meaning: I'm not well. · The milk is bad.

cards.target: este libro · esa mesa
cards.native: Pointing words go BEFORE the noun and take the place of el / la.
cards.exampleTarget: Estas sillas están sucias. Ese carro es de Mario.
cards.exampleNative: These chairs are dirty. That car is Mario's.
cards.remember: ✗ el este libro (the this book). (el libro este exists in casual speech, often with a negative tone.)
cards.meaning: this book · that table

cards.target: ¿Qué es esto? · ¿Qué es eso?
cards.native: esto / eso point at an unknown thing with no noun after them and no gender.
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Qué es eso? → Es una bocina.
cards.exampleNative: What's that? → It's a speaker.
cards.meaning: What's this? · What's that?

cards.target: este carro rojo
cards.native: Order: pointing word, then noun, then color or describing word.
cards.exampleTarget: Esta taza negra es de mi papá.
cards.exampleNative: This black cup is my dad's.
cards.meaning: this red car
cards.replyNative: How pretty! Where did he buy it?

cards.target: Tiene el pelo largo. · Es alta.
cards.native: Hair uses tener + el pelo + description. Height and looks use ser.
cards.exampleTarget: Juan tiene el pelo corto y negro. Karla es güera.
cards.exampleNative: Juan has short black hair. Karla is fair-skinned.
cards.remember: A short person is baj@ (short); short hair is el pelo corto.
cards.meaning: She has long hair. · She's tall.
cards.replyNative: Oh, I know who he is.

cards.group: Rules: how Spanish relates to English
cards.target: largo · parado
cards.native: False friends: largo = long (not large); parado = standing in Mexico (unemployed in Spain); grande = big.
cards.exampleTarget: El capítulo es largo.
cards.exampleNative: The chapter is long.
cards.meaning: long · standing
cards.replyNative: How many pages does it have?

cards.target: ¿qué onda? · órale
cards.native: what's up? · wow, okay (casual)
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Qué onda, amigo? → ¡Órale!
cards.exampleNative: What's up, friend? → Wow!
cards.remember: Friends only, never an elder or a boss.
cards.replyNative: Nothing, just hanging out. And you?

cards.target: ¡está chido! · ¡qué chido! · está chid@
cards.native: cool! · how cool! · is cool (casual)
cards.exampleTarget: El hotel está chido.
cards.exampleNative: The hotel is cool.
cards.remember: Friends only.

cards.target: ¡no manches!
cards.native: no way! (casual)
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Tienes tres perros? ¡No manches!
cards.exampleNative: You have three dogs? No way!
cards.remember: Friends only.

cards.target: ¡qué padre! · está padre · padrísim@
cards.native: how cool! · is great · amazing (MX)
cards.exampleTarget: ¡Qué padre! La fiesta está padrísima.
cards.exampleNative: How cool! The party is amazing.

cards.target: ¡qué bueno! · ¡qué bien!
cards.native: great! · how nice!
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo un trabajo nuevo. → ¡Qué bueno!
cards.exampleNative: I have a new job. → Great!
cards.replyNative: Where are you going to work?

cards.target: ¡qué…!
cards.native: how…! · what a…!
cards.exampleTarget: ¡Qué delicioso! · ¡Qué bonito!
cards.exampleNative: How delicious! · How pretty!
cards.remember: ¡qué + describing word! (how …!) makes any exclamation.

cards.target: ¡claro! · exacto · ¡es verdad!
cards.native: of course! · exactly · that's true!
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Hay tacos? → ¡Sí, claro!
cards.exampleNative: Are there tacos? → Yes, of course!

cards.target: ¿en serio? · ¡qué raro!
cards.native: seriously? really? · how strange!
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Tienes calor? ¡Qué raro! Yo tengo frío.
cards.exampleNative: You're hot? How strange! I'm cold.

cards.target: ¡qué envidia! · me da gusto
cards.native: lucky you! (I'm jealous) · I'm glad
cards.exampleTarget: Estoy de vacaciones en la playa. → ¡Qué envidia!
cards.exampleNative: I'm on vacation at the beach. → Lucky you!

cards.target: ¡qué mal! · que se mejore
cards.native: that's too bad! · feel better (usted)
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo fiebre. → ¡Qué mal! Que se mejore.
cards.exampleNative: I have a fever. → That's too bad! Feel better.
cards.remember: que se mejore (get well soon) is a fixed wish form.
cards.replyNative: Do you need anything from the pharmacy?

cards.target: ¡ay, no!
cards.native: oh, no!
cards.exampleTarget: ¡Ay, no! No hay café.
cards.exampleNative: Oh, no! There's no coffee.

cards.target: oye · a ver · pues
cards.native: hey, listen · let's see · well…
cards.exampleTarget: Oye, ¿dónde están mis llaves? → A ver…
cards.exampleNative: Hey, where are my keys? → Let's see…
cards.remember: oye (hey, listen) is for tú.
cards.replyNative: Did you look in the kitchen yet?

cards.target: tranquil@ · no te preocupes
cards.native: relax, take it easy · don't worry
cards.exampleTarget: Tranquilo, todo está bien. No te preocupes.
cards.exampleNative: Relax, everything is fine. Don't worry.
cards.remember: no te preocupes (don't worry) is a fixed negative command.

cards.target: mija
cards.native: dear (to a girl or woman, MX)
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Cómo estás, mija?
cards.exampleNative: How are you, dear?
cards.remember: From mi hija, my daughter.

cards.target: ya sabes · creo que
cards.native: you know · I think…
cards.exampleTarget: Creo que la farmacia está cerca.
cards.exampleNative: I think the pharmacy is close.

cards.target: de acuerdo · estar de acuerdo
cards.native: okay, agreed · to agree
cards.exampleTarget: ¿A las ocho? → De acuerdo. · Estoy de acuerdo.
cards.exampleNative: At eight? → Okay. · I agree.
cards.replyNative: Then we'll see each other there.

cards.target: este · esta · estos · estas
cards.native: this · these (near me, aquí)
cards.exampleTarget: Este carro es nuevo. Estas sillas están sucias.
cards.exampleNative: This car is new. These chairs are dirty.
cards.remember: Goes before the noun and takes the place of el / la (the).

cards.target: ese · esa · esos · esas
cards.native: that · those (near you, ahí)
cards.exampleTarget: Esa puerta está abierta. ¿De quién son esos platos?
cards.exampleNative: That door is open. Whose plates are those?
cards.replyNative: They're mine. I'll wash them now.

cards.target: aquel · aquella · aquellos · aquellas
cards.native: that · those over there (allá)
cards.exampleTarget: Aquella casa es muy vieja.
cards.exampleNative: That house over there is very old.
cards.remember: In Mexico ese (that) often does the job of aquel (that over there) too.

cards.target: esto · eso
cards.native: this · that (no noun; an unknown thing)
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Qué es esto? → Es una llave. · ¿Qué es eso? → Es una bocina.
cards.exampleNative: What's this? → It's a key. · What's that? → It's a speaker.
cards.remember: No gender, never followed by a noun.

cards.target: este es… · esta es… · estos son…
cards.native: this is… · these are… (introducing people)
cards.exampleTarget: Esta es mi hermana, Karla. Estos son mis padres.
cards.exampleNative: This is my sister, Karla. These are my parents.

cards.target: todos · todo
cards.native: everyone · everything
cards.exampleTarget: Todos están contentos y todo está listo.
cards.exampleNative: Everyone is happy and everything is ready.

cards.target: ¿qué?
cards.native: what? · which? (¿qué + noun?)
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Qué hay en el refri? · ¿Qué hora es?
cards.exampleNative: What's in the fridge? · What time is it?
cards.remember: Every question word carries an accent.

cards.target: ¿quién? · ¿quiénes?
cards.native: who? (one person · more than one)
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Quién es tu maestra? · ¿Quiénes son ellos?
cards.exampleNative: Who is your teacher? · Who are they?

cards.target: ¿dónde? · ¿de dónde?
cards.native: where? · from where?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Dónde está el baño? · ¿De dónde eres?
cards.exampleNative: Where is the bathroom? · Where are you from?
cards.remember: Question word + verb + subject.

cards.target: ¿cuándo?
cards.native: when?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Cuándo es la reunión? → Es el sábado.
cards.exampleNative: When is the get-together? → It's on Saturday.

cards.target: ¿cómo?
cards.native: how? · what is … like?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Cómo es tu casa? · ¿Cómo está tu mamá?
cards.exampleNative: What is your house like? · How is your mom?
cards.remember: cómo es = what it's like; cómo está = how it is right now.

cards.target: ¿por qué? · porque
cards.native: why? · because
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Por qué estás aquí? → Porque tengo una cita.
cards.exampleNative: Why are you here? → Because I have an appointment.
cards.remember: Two words with an accent asks; one word with no accent answers.

cards.target: ¿cuál?
cards.native: which? · what?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Cuál es tu carro?
cards.exampleNative: Which one is your car?

cards.target: ¿de qué país…? · ¿de qué color…?
cards.native: from what country…? · what color…?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿De qué color es tu carro? → Es rojo.
cards.exampleNative: What color is your car? → It's red.
cards.remember: The little word goes first.

cards.target: ¿de quién es? · ¿de quién son?
cards.native: whose is it? · whose are they?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿De quién es esta mochila? → Es de Andrea.
cards.exampleNative: Whose backpack is this? → It's Andrea's.
cards.remember: Never ¿Quién es de…? (Who is from…?)

cards.target: ¿verdad? · ¿no?
cards.native: right? · isn't it? (tagged on the end)
cards.exampleTarget: Eres de Monterrey, ¿verdad?
cards.exampleNative: You're from Monterrey, right?

cards.target: roj@ · amarill@ · blanc@ · negr@ · morad@
cards.native: red · yellow · white · black · purple
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo una mochila roja y dos sillas blancas.
cards.exampleNative: I have a red backpack and two white chairs.
cards.remember: Four forms: rojo, roja, rojos, rojas (red).
cards.replyTarget: ¿Y de qué color es tu carro?
cards.replyNative: And what color is your car?

cards.target: verde · azul · gris · rosa · naranja
cards.native: green · blue · gray · pink · orange
cards.exampleTarget: Las sillas son azules y el carro es gris.
cards.exampleNative: The chairs are blue and the car is gray.
cards.remember: Two forms: one and more (azul · azules, blue). Not ripe yet: está verde (it's green).

cards.target: rosa mexicano
cards.native: Mexico's hot pink (bougainvillea color)
cards.exampleTarget: La casa es rosa mexicano.
cards.exampleNative: The house is hot pink.

cards.target: el pelo largo · corto · lacio · chino
cards.native: long · short · straight · curly hair
cards.exampleTarget: Karla tiene el pelo largo y lacio.
cards.exampleNative: Karla has long, straight hair.
cards.remember: Hair uses tener (to have) + el pelo (the hair). chino is curly in Mexico.

cards.target: el pelo negro · castaño · rubio · tener barba
cards.native: black · brown · blond hair · to have a beard
cards.exampleTarget: El abuelo tiene barba y el pelo blanco.
cards.exampleNative: Grandpa has a beard and white hair.

cards.group: Describing words that change meaning (ser vs estar)
cards.target: es aburrid@ · está aburrid@
cards.native: is boring · is bored
cards.exampleTarget: La clase es aburrida, por eso el estudiante está aburrido.
cards.exampleNative: The class is boring, so the student is bored.
cards.remember: ser = what it's like; estar = how someone feels now.

cards.group: Describing words that change meaning (ser vs estar)
cards.target: es mal@ · está mal@
cards.native: is bad, mean · has gone bad
cards.exampleTarget: La película es muy mala. La leche está mala.
cards.exampleNative: The movie is very bad. The milk has gone bad.
cards.remember: About a person, está mala (casual) = she's sick.
cards.replyNative: Throw it out, it's sour already.

cards.group: Describing words that change meaning (ser vs estar)
cards.target: es ric@ · está ric@
cards.native: is rich · is tasty
cards.exampleTarget: Mi vecino es muy rico. Los tacos están muy ricos.
cards.exampleNative: My neighbor is very rich. The tacos are really tasty.
cards.replyNative: Will you give me the recipe?

cards.group: Describing words that change meaning (ser vs estar)
cards.target: es buen@ · está buen@
cards.native: is good · is still good
cards.exampleTarget: Es una película muy buena. La leche todavía está buena.
cards.exampleNative: It's a very good movie. The milk is still good.
cards.remember: For tastes good, Mexicans say está rico.

cards.group: Describing words that change meaning (ser vs estar)
cards.target: es verde · está verde
cards.native: is green · isn't ripe yet
cards.exampleTarget: La puerta es verde. Esta fruta todavía está verde.
cards.exampleNative: The door is green. This fruit isn't ripe yet.

cards.group: Describing words that change meaning (ser vs estar)
cards.target: es viv@ · está viv@
cards.native: is sharp, quick · is alive
cards.exampleTarget: Mi abuela es muy viva. La planta todavía está viva.
cards.exampleNative: My grandma is very sharp. The plant is still alive.
cards.replyNative: How often do you water it?

cards.group: Describing words that change meaning (ser vs estar)
cards.target: estoy mal · está mal@
cards.native: I'm not well · it has gone bad
cards.exampleTarget: Martha y Carlos dicen: "Estoy mal." La leche está mala.
cards.exampleNative: Martha and Carlos say, "I'm not well." The milk has gone bad.
cards.remember: mal (how you are) never changes; malo, mala, malos, malas (bad) matches its noun.
cards.replyNative: What's wrong? Shall I take you to the doctor?

cards.group: Describing words that change meaning (ser vs estar)
cards.target: es guap@ · está guap@
cards.native: is good-looking · looks great right now
cards.exampleTarget: Mi esposa es guapa. ¡Qué guapa estás hoy!
cards.exampleNative: My wife is good-looking. You look great today!
cards.remember: Many describing words work this way: ser = usually, estar = right now.
cards.replyNative: Thanks! I'm going to a wedding.

cards.group: Describing words that change meaning (ser vs estar)
cards.target: es barat@ · está barat@
cards.native: is cheap (always) · is cheap right now
cards.exampleTarget: El mercado es barato. Hoy la fruta está barata.
cards.exampleNative: The market is cheap. Today fruit is cheap.
cards.remember: Same pattern with caro (expensive), pesado (heavy), ligero (light), lento (slow), oscuro (dark), nervioso (nervous), tranquilo (calm), ruidoso (noisy).

cards.target: algo / nada
cards.native: something, anything / nothing
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Hay algo en el refri? → No, no hay nada.
cards.exampleNative: Is there anything in the fridge? → No, there's nothing.
cards.replyNative: Then let's go to the supermarket.

cards.target: alguien / nadie
cards.native: someone, anyone / nobody
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Hay alguien en la oficina? → No, no hay nadie.
cards.exampleNative: Is anyone in the office? → No, nobody's there.

cards.target: siempre / nunca
cards.native: always / never
cards.exampleTarget: Siempre tengo prisa. ↔ Nunca tengo prisa.
cards.exampleNative: I'm always in a hurry. ↔ I'm never in a hurry.
cards.replyNative: Why are you in a hurry?

cards.target: algún · alguna / ningún · ninguna
cards.native: some, any / no, not any (one thing)
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Tienes algún problema? → No, no tengo ningún problema.
cards.exampleNative: Do you have any problems? → No, I don't have any problems.
cards.remember: Stays singular even when English says "any ___s".

cards.target: también / tampoco
cards.native: also, too / neither, not either
cards.exampleTarget: Estoy cansada. → Yo también. · No tengo efectivo. → Yo tampoco.
cards.exampleNative: I'm tired. → Me too. · I don't have cash. → Me neither.
cards.replyNative: Then let's go to the ATM.

cards.target: todavía / ya no
cards.native: still / not anymore
cards.exampleTarget: Todavía tengo efectivo. ↔ Ya no tengo efectivo.
cards.exampleNative: I still have cash. ↔ I don't have cash anymore.
cards.replyTarget: Hay un cajero en la esquina.
cards.replyNative: There's an ATM on the corner.

cards.target: todo / nada
cards.native: everything / nothing
cards.exampleTarget: Todo está listo. ↔ Nada está listo.
cards.exampleNative: Everything is ready. ↔ Nothing is ready.
cards.replyNative: Can I help you with anything?

cards.target: no sé · ni idea
cards.native: I don't know · no idea
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Dónde está el banco? → No sé, ni idea.
cards.exampleNative: Where's the bank? → I don't know, no idea.
cards.remember: sé (I know) is from saber (to know). Learn no sé (I don't know) as a whole phrase for now.
cards.replyTarget: Voy a preguntar en la tienda.

cards.target: depende · depende de…
cards.native: it depends · it depends on…
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Es caro el hotel? → Depende de la fecha.
cards.exampleNative: Is the hotel expensive? → It depends on the date.
cards.remember: de + el = del: depende del día (it depends on the day).

cards.target: tal vez · a lo mejor
cards.native: maybe · maybe, probably
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Está Ana en casa? → A lo mejor está en el mercado.
cards.exampleNative: Is Ana home? → Maybe she's at the market.
cards.remember: a lo mejor is the everyday Mexican "maybe". It doesn't mean "the best".

cards.target: igual y…
cards.native: maybe… (casual MX)
cards.exampleTarget: Igual y hay tacos en la fiesta.
cards.exampleNative: Maybe there are tacos at the party.
cards.remember: Very Mexican and casual. You'll hear it more than you'll need it.

cards.target: creo que sí · creo que no
cards.native: I think so · I don't think so
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Hay una farmacia aquí? → Creo que sí.
cards.exampleNative: Is there a pharmacy here? → I think so.
cards.remember: Just sí (yes) or no after creo que (I think), no extra words.

cards.target: claro que sí · claro que no · por supuesto
cards.native: of course · of course not · of course (a bit formal)
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Tienes tiempo? → ¡Claro que sí!
cards.exampleNative: Do you have time? → Of course!
cards.remember: claro (sure) alone is the short version.
cards.replyNative: Shall we go for a coffee?

cards.target: con gusto
cards.native: my pleasure, gladly (reply to thanks)
cards.exampleTarget: Gracias, señor. → Con gusto.
cards.exampleNative: Thank you, sir. → My pleasure.
cards.remember: In Mexico you hear con gusto (gladly) as often as de nada (you're welcome), especially in shops.

cards.target: ¡qué amable! · muy amable
cards.native: how kind! · very kind (of you)
cards.exampleTarget: Aquí está su café. → ¡Qué amable, gracias!
cards.exampleNative: Here's your coffee. → How kind, thanks!
cards.remember: Add de su parte (on your part) for extra politeness: muy amable de su parte (very kind of you).
cards.replyNative: Could you bring me sugar, please?

cards.target: todavía no
cards.native: not yet
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Ya estás lista? → Todavía no.
cards.exampleNative: Are you ready yet? → Not yet.
cards.remember: The answer to any question with ya (already, yet).

cards.target: la verdad · la verdad es que…
cards.native: honestly · the truth is…
cards.exampleTarget: La verdad, no tengo hambre.
cards.exampleNative: Honestly, I'm not hungry.
cards.remember: A soft way to start an honest answer.

cards.target: o sea
cards.native: I mean, in other words
cards.exampleTarget: Es mi suegra, o sea, la mamá de mi esposa.
cards.exampleNative: She's my mother-in-law, I mean, my wife's mom.
cards.remember: Mexicans use it constantly to rephrase or explain.

cards.target: bueno · bueno, pues…
cards.native: well, okay · well then…
cards.exampleTarget: Bueno, ¿a qué hora es la fiesta?
cards.exampleNative: Okay, what time is the party?
cards.remember: A filler to start or wrap up a thought. On the phone, ¿bueno? means hello.

cards.target: este…
cards.native: um… (filler)
cards.exampleTarget: Es, este… el hermano de Luis.
cards.exampleNative: He's, um… Luis's brother.
cards.remember: The Mexican "um". Using it buys you time and sounds natural.
cards.replyNative: Oh, I know who he is.

cards.target: sale · está bien
cards.native: okay, deal (casual MX) · that's fine
cards.exampleTarget: Nos vemos a las tres, ¿sale? → Sale.
cards.exampleNative: See you at three, okay? → Okay.
cards.remember: sale (OK, sure) is friendly and casual; está bien (all right) works with anyone.

cards.target: no hay problema · no pasa nada
cards.native: no problem · no worries, it's fine
cards.exampleTarget: ¡Perdón, señora! → No pasa nada.
cards.exampleNative: Sorry, ma'am! → No worries.
cards.remember: no pasa nada (no problem) is the kind reply to an apology.

cards.target: no importa · da igual
cards.native: it doesn't matter · it's all the same to me
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Café o té? → Da igual.
cards.exampleNative: Coffee or tea? → Either is fine.
cards.remember: Both are neutral, not rude.

cards.target: ¡qué pena!
cards.native: how embarrassing!, I'm so sorry! (MX)
cards.exampleTarget: ¡Qué pena, señor! Es su asiento.
cards.exampleNative: I'm so sorry, sir! It's your seat.
cards.remember: In Mexico pena means embarrassment more than sadness.

cards.unitName: Unit 8 · Regular verbs in the present
cards.target: trabajar · comer · vivir
cards.native: Every verb's base form (infinitive) ends in -ar, -er or -ir. The ending decides how the verb changes.
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo que trabajar, comer y vivir bien.
cards.exampleNative: I have to work, eat and live well.
cards.meaning: to work · to eat · to live

cards.unitName: Unit 8 · Regular verbs in the present
cards.target: Tengo que ir. · algo para comer
cards.native: After tener que, hay que and para, the second verb stays in its base form.
cards.exampleTarget: Hay que lavar los platos. Es algo para leer.
cards.exampleNative: The dishes need washing. It's something to read.
cards.meaning: I have to go. · something to eat

cards.unitName: Unit 8 · Regular verbs in the present
cards.target: presente
cards.native: Units 1 to 7 build everything on ser, estar, tener and hay in the present. Unit 8 opens the present tense of every verb, and each later unit adds one more tense.
cards.exampleTarget: Soy, estoy, tengo, hay. → Trabajo, como, vivo.
cards.exampleNative: I am, I am, I have, there is. → I work, I eat, I live.
cards.remember: Learn each tense in its unit; the verb cards for it sit in the same unit.
cards.meaning: the present tense

cards.unitName: Unit 8 · Regular verbs in the present
cards.group: Grammar: present tense of every verb
cards.target: hablo · hablas · habla · hablamos · hablan
cards.native: Present of -ar verbs: drop -ar and add o, as, a, amos, an.
cards.exampleTarget: Trabajo en la oficina y mi esposa trabaja en casa.
cards.exampleNative: I work at the office and my wife works at home.
cards.remember: You already saw these in the stories: trabaja (works), estudia (studies), llama (calls).
cards.meaning: I speak · you speak · he / she speaks, you (polite) speak · we speak · they speak, you all speak

cards.unitName: Unit 8 · Regular verbs in the present
cards.group: Grammar: present tense of every verb
cards.target: como · comes · come · comemos · comen
cards.native: Present of -er verbs: drop -er and add o, es, e, emos, en.
cards.exampleTarget: Comemos tacos los viernes.
cards.exampleNative: We eat tacos on Fridays.
cards.meaning: I eat · you eat · he / she eats, you (polite) eat · we eat · they eat, you all eat

cards.unitName: Unit 8 · Regular verbs in the present
cards.group: Grammar: present tense of every verb
cards.target: vivo · vives · vive · vivimos · viven
cards.native: Present of -ir verbs: same as -er except nosotros, which ends in -imos.
cards.exampleTarget: Vivimos en Puerto Vallarta. ¿Dónde vives?
cards.exampleNative: We live in Puerto Vallarta. Where do you live?
cards.remember: Seen in Lesson 3: Gabriel vive en Guadalajara (Gabriel lives in Guadalajara).
cards.meaning: I live · you live · he / she lives, you (polite) live · we live · they live, you all live

cards.unitName: Unit 8 · Regular verbs in the present
cards.group: Grammar: present tense of every verb
cards.target: Trabajo.
cards.native: One present form covers three English ones: I work, I'm working, I do work. With a time word it can also mean a plan.
cards.exampleTarget: Mañana trabajo hasta las seis.
cards.exampleNative: Tomorrow I'm working until six.
cards.meaning: I work. · I'm working. · I do work.
cards.replyNative: Then we'll see each other on Thursday.

cards.unitName: Unit 8 · Regular verbs in the present
cards.group: Grammar: present tense of every verb
cards.target: ¿Hablas inglés? · ¿Dónde vives?
cards.native: Questions with any verb follow the same rules: yes/no keeps statement order; a question word goes first, then the verb.
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Trabajas hoy? ¿A qué hora llegas?
cards.exampleNative: Are you working today? What time are you arriving?
cards.meaning: Do you speak English? · Where do you live?

cards.unitName: Unit 8 · Regular verbs in the present
cards.group: Grammar: present tense of every verb
cards.target: vosotros · habláis
cards.native: Spain has a fifth form, vosotros (you all, informal). Mexico never uses it; ustedes covers everyone. Recognize it in Spanish films and books.
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Vosotros habláis inglés? = ¿Ustedes hablan inglés?
cards.exampleNative: Do you all speak English?
cards.remember: You never need to produce it in Mexico.
cards.meaning: you all (in Spain, casual) · you all speak

cards.unitName: Unit 8 · Regular verbs in the present
cards.target: siempre → a menudo → a veces → casi nunca → nunca
cards.native: always → often → sometimes → hardly ever → never
cards.exampleTarget: Siempre desayuno, pero nunca como pastel.
cards.exampleNative: I always eat breakfast, but I never eat cake.
cards.remember: Frequency words usually go before the verb or at the end. After the verb, nunca (never) needs no: No manejo nunca (I never drive).

cards.unitName: Unit 8 · Regular verbs in the present
cards.target: hay que + infinitive
cards.native: one has to, you need to (in general)
cards.exampleTarget: Hay que lavar los platos.
cards.exampleNative: The dishes need washing.
cards.remember: No person named; just what needs doing.

cards.unitName: Unit 8 · Regular verbs in the present
cards.target: llama · llama a
cards.native: calls · calls (someone)
cards.exampleTarget: Marcela llama a Ramón.
cards.exampleNative: Marcela calls Ramón.
cards.remember: From llamar (to call).

cards.unitName: Unit 8 · Regular verbs in the present
cards.target: vive · trabaja · estudia
cards.native: lives · works · studies
cards.exampleTarget: Gabriel es de Colombia, pero vive en Guadalajara.
cards.exampleNative: Gabriel is from Colombia, but he lives in Guadalajara.
cards.remember: Present tense of regular verbs; you'll learn these forms soon.

cards.unitName: Unit 8 · Regular verbs in the present
cards.target: ¿a qué te dedicas? · ¿a qué se dedica? · me dedico a…
cards.native: what do you do for a living? (tú) · what do you do for a living? (usted) · I work in…
cards.exampleTarget: ¿A qué se dedica usted? → Me dedico al turismo.
cards.exampleNative: What do you do for a living? → I work in tourism.
cards.remember: Fixed phrases from dedicarse (to do for a living). Politer than asking ¿cuál es tu trabajo? (what's your job?)

cards.unitName: Unit 8 · Regular verbs in the present
cards.target: soy jubilad@
cards.native: I'm retired
cards.exampleTarget: Don Ernesto es jubilado. Su esposa también es jubilada.
cards.exampleNative: Don Ernesto is retired. His wife is retired too.
cards.remember: Estoy jubilad@ (I'm retired) is also common. Both are correct.
cards.replyTarget: Ahora tengo tiempo para aprender español.
cards.replyNative: Now I have time to learn Spanish.

cards.unitName: Unit 8 · Regular verbs in the present
cards.target: trabajo en… · trabajo de…
cards.native: I work at… · I work as…
cards.exampleTarget: Trabajo en un hotel. Trabajo de recepcionista.
cards.exampleNative: I work at a hotel. I work as a receptionist.
cards.remember: No un (a) after trabajo de: Trabajo de mesero (I work as a waiter).
cards.replyNative: How many years have you been there?

cards.unitName: Unit 8 · Regular verbs in the present
cards.target: el negocio · tener un negocio
cards.native: business, shop · to have a business
cards.exampleTarget: Mi hermano tiene un negocio de tacos.
cards.exampleNative: My brother has a taco business.
cards.remember: negocio (business) also means a small shop: el negocio de la esquina (the corner shop).

cards.unitName: Unit 8 · Regular verbs in the present
cards.target: la empresa · la compañía
cards.native: company, firm · company
cards.exampleTarget: Mi hija trabaja en una empresa grande.
cards.exampleNative: My daughter works at a big company.
cards.remember: empresa (company) is the most common word.

cards.unitName: Unit 8 · Regular verbs in the present
cards.target: la junta
cards.native: work meeting (MX)
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo una junta a las diez.
cards.exampleNative: I have a meeting at ten.
cards.remember: reunión (meeting) also works; junta (meeting) is the office word in Mexico.
cards.replyNative: And what time do you finish?

cards.unitName: Unit 8 · Regular verbs in the present
cards.target: el horario · de lunes a viernes
cards.native: schedule, hours · Monday to Friday
cards.exampleTarget: Trabajo de lunes a viernes, de nueve a cinco.
cards.exampleNative: I work Monday to Friday, from nine to five.
cards.remember: Ranges use de… a… (from… to…).
cards.replyNative: And do you rest on weekends?

cards.unitName: Unit 8 · Regular verbs in the present
cards.target: tiempo completo · medio tiempo
cards.native: full time · part time
cards.exampleTarget: Luis trabaja medio tiempo en una tienda.
cards.exampleNative: Luis works part time at a store.
cards.replyNative: And does he study in the afternoon?

cards.unitName: Unit 8 · Regular verbs in the present
cards.target: trabajo desde casa · en línea
cards.native: I work from home · online
cards.exampleTarget: Trabajo desde casa los lunes. Vendo en línea.

cards.remember: Now, habits and facts.

cards.unitName: Unit 9 · Irregular verbs in the present
cards.target: empezar
cards.native: to start · begin
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo que empezar el trabajo a las ocho.
cards.exampleNative: I have to start work at eight.
cards.remember: -ar verb. After tener que (have to), hay que (one has to) and para (to, in order to) it never changes.

cards.unitName: Unit 9 · Irregular verbs in the present
cards.target:
empezar · present
yo empiezo · tú empiezas · él / ella / usted empieza · nosotros empezamos · ellos / ustedes empiezan
cards.native:
to start · begin · present
I start · you start · he/she starts / you (form.) start · we start · they / you all start
cards.exampleTarget: Yo empiezo el trabajo a las ocho.
cards.exampleNative: I start work at eight.
cards.remember: Now, habits and facts.

cards.unitName: Unit 9 · Irregular verbs in the present
cards.target:
cerrar · present
yo cierro · tú cierras · él / ella / usted cierra · nosotros cerramos · ellos / ustedes cierran
cards.native:
to close · present
I close · you close · he/she closes / you (form.) close · we close · they / you all close
cards.exampleTarget: Yo cierro la puerta.
cards.exampleNative: I close the door.
cards.remember: Now, habits and facts.

cards.unitName: Unit 9 · Irregular verbs in the present
cards.target: recordar

cards.exampleTarget: Tengo que recordar su nombre.
