cards.remember: -ar verb. After tener que (have to), hay que (one has to) and para (to, in order to) it never changes.

cards.unitName: Unit 9 · Irregular verbs in the present
cards.target:
recordar · present
yo recuerdo · tú recuerdas · él / ella / usted recuerda · nosotros recordamos · ellos / ustedes recuerdan
cards.native:
to remember · remind · present
I remember · you remember · he/she remembers / you (form.) remember · we remember · they / you all remember
cards.exampleTarget: Yo recuerdo su nombre.
cards.exampleNative: I remember her name.
cards.remember: Now, habits and facts.

cards.unitName: Unit 9 · Irregular verbs in the present
cards.target: jugar
cards.native: to play (a game or sport)
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo que jugar futbol.
cards.exampleNative: I have to play soccer.
cards.remember: -ar verb. After tener que (have to), hay que (one has to) and para (to, in order to) it never changes.

cards.unitName: Unit 9 · Irregular verbs in the present
cards.target:
jugar · present
yo juego · tú juegas · él / ella / usted juega · nosotros jugamos · ellos / ustedes juegan
cards.native:
to play (a game or sport) · present
I play · you play · he/she plays / you (form.) play · we play · they / you all play
cards.exampleTarget: Yo juego futbol.
cards.exampleNative: I play soccer.
cards.remember: Now, habits and facts.

cards.unitName: Unit 9 · Irregular verbs in the present
cards.target: perder
cards.native: to lose · miss
cards.exampleTarget: No quiero perder mis llaves.
cards.exampleNative: I don't want to lose my keys.
cards.remember: -er verb. After tener que (have to), hay que (one has to) and para (to, in order to) it never changes.

cards.unitName: Unit 9 · Irregular verbs in the present
cards.target:
perder · present
yo pierdo · tú pierdes · él / ella / usted pierde · nosotros perdemos · ellos / ustedes pierden
cards.native:
to lose · miss · present
I lose · you lose · he/she loses / you (form.) lose · we lose · they / you all lose
cards.exampleTarget: Yo pierdo mis llaves.
cards.exampleNative: I lose my keys.
cards.remember: Now, habits and facts.

cards.unitName: Unit 9 · Irregular verbs in the present
cards.target: oír
cards.native: to hear
cards.exampleTarget: Desde mi casa puedo oír el mar.
cards.exampleNative: From my house I can hear the ocean.
cards.remember: -ir verb. After tener que (have to), hay que (one has to) and para (to, in order to) it never changes.

cards.unitName: Unit 9 · Irregular verbs in the present
cards.target:
oír · present
yo oigo · tú oyes · él / ella / usted oye · nosotros oímos · ellos / ustedes oyen
cards.native:
to hear · present
I hear · you hear · he/she hears / you (form.) hear · we hear · they / you all hear
cards.exampleTarget: Oigo la música desde mi casa.
cards.exampleNative: I hear the music from my house.
cards.remember: Now, habits and facts.

cards.unitName: Unit 9 · Irregular verbs in the present
cards.target: seguir
cards.native: to keep going · follow · continue
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo que seguir derecho.
cards.exampleNative: I have to keep going straight.
cards.remember: -ir verb. After tener que (have to), hay que (one has to) and para (to, in order to) it never changes.

cards.unitName: Unit 9 · Irregular verbs in the present
cards.target:
seguir · present
yo sigo · tú sigues · él / ella / usted sigue · nosotros seguimos · ellos / ustedes siguen
cards.native:
to keep going · follow · continue · present
I keep going · you keep going · he/she keeps going / you (form.) keep going · we keep going · they / you all keep going
cards.exampleTarget: Yo sigo derecho.
cards.exampleNative: I keep going straight.
cards.remember: Now, habits and facts.

cards.unitName: Unit 9 · Irregular verbs in the present
cards.target: probar
cards.native: to try · taste
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo que probar la comida.
cards.exampleNative: I have to try the food.
cards.remember: -ar verb. After tener que (have to), hay que (one has to) and para (to, in order to) it never changes.

cards.unitName: Unit 9 · Irregular verbs in the present
cards.target:
probar · present
yo pruebo · tú pruebas · él / ella / usted prueba · nosotros probamos · ellos / ustedes prueban
cards.native:
to try · taste · present
I try · you try · he/she tries / you (form.) try · we try · they / you all try
cards.exampleTarget: Yo pruebo la comida.
cards.exampleNative: I try the food.
cards.remember: Now, habits and facts.

cards.target: Sigues derecho y das vuelta en la esquina.
cards.native: Directions are often given in the plain present: sigues, das vuelta, cruzas, pasas.
cards.exampleTarget: Cruzas el puente y doblas a la izquierda.
cards.exampleNative: You cross the bridge and turn left.
cards.remember: You'll also hear command forms (siga, go on; dé vuelta, turn; cruce, cross). Those come in unit 25.
cards.meaning: You go straight and turn at the corner.
cards.replyNative: Is it far from the bridge?

cards.target: a la derecha / a la izquierda
cards.native: to the right, on the right / to the left, on the left
cards.exampleTarget: La farmacia está a la derecha.
cards.exampleNative: The pharmacy is on the right.
cards.remember: Same phrase for "to the right" and "on the right".

cards.target: derecho · todo derecho
cards.native: straight ahead · straight on, all the way
cards.exampleTarget: Sigues todo derecho dos cuadras.
cards.exampleNative: You keep going straight for two blocks.
cards.remember: In directions, derecho (straight) never changes to agree with anything.

cards.target: derecho / a la derecha
cards.native: straight / to the right
cards.exampleTarget: Sigues derecho y das vuelta a la derecha.
cards.exampleNative: You keep going straight and turn right.
cards.remember: Classic mix-up. derecho (-o) goes straight; derecha (-a) turns right.

cards.target: a la vuelta · a la vuelta de la esquina
cards.native: around the corner · just around the corner
cards.exampleTarget: La tienda está a la vuelta.
cards.exampleNative: The store is around the corner.
cards.remember: Very common answer when something is close.

cards.target: dar vuelta · dar vuelta a la derecha · dar vuelta a la izquierda
cards.native: to turn · to turn right · to turn left
cards.exampleTarget: En el semáforo das vuelta a la izquierda.
cards.exampleNative: At the traffic light you turn left.
cards.remember: Mexico's everyday way to say turn. From dar (to give): doy, das, da.

cards.target: doblar · doblar en la esquina
cards.native: to turn · to turn at the corner
cards.exampleTarget: Doblas a la derecha en la esquina.
cards.exampleNative: You turn right at the corner.
cards.remember: Same meaning as dar vuelta (to turn). doblar (to turn) also means to fold (clothes).

cards.target: seguir derecho · seguir por esta calle
cards.native: to keep going straight · to continue along this street
cards.exampleTarget: Sigues por esta calle hasta el mercado.
cards.exampleNative: You continue along this street to the market.
cards.remember: seguir (to keep going) changes e → i: sigo, sigues, sigue. por here means along.

cards.target: cruzar · cruzar la calle
cards.native: to cross · to cross the street
cards.exampleTarget: Cruzas la calle y está enfrente.
cards.exampleNative: You cross the street and it's across from you.
cards.remember: cruzar el puente (cross the bridge), cruzar la avenida (cross the avenue) work the same way.

cards.target: pasar · pasar el…
cards.native: to go past · to go past the…
cards.exampleTarget: Pasas el banco y está a la izquierda.
cards.exampleNative: You go past the bank and it's on the left.
cards.remember: You already know pasar (to come in, to pass) from pásale (come in).

cards.target: hasta · hasta el semáforo
cards.native: as far as, until · up to the traffic light
cards.exampleTarget: Sigues derecho hasta el semáforo.
cards.exampleNative: You go straight up to the traffic light.
cards.remember: hasta (until, as far as) marks where to stop going.

cards.target: el semáforo
cards.native: traffic light
cards.exampleTarget: En el segundo semáforo das vuelta a la derecha.
cards.exampleNative: At the second light you turn right.
cards.remember: Directions in Mexico often count traffic lights.
cards.replyNative: And then is it on the left?

cards.target: la glorieta
cards.native: traffic circle, roundabout
cards.exampleTarget: En la glorieta sigues derecho.
cards.exampleNative: At the roundabout you keep going straight.
cards.remember: Many glorietas (roundabouts) have a statue or fountain and work as landmarks.

cards.target: el puente
cards.native: bridge
cards.exampleTarget: Cruzas el puente y el hotel está a la izquierda.
cards.exampleNative: You cross the bridge and the hotel is on the left.

cards.target: la avenida · la calle principal
cards.native: avenue · main street
cards.exampleTarget: La parada está en la avenida, enfrente del banco.
cards.exampleNative: The stop is on the avenue, across from the bank.
cards.remember: Big avenues are where the buses run.

cards.target: la colonia
cards.native: neighborhood (MX)
cards.exampleTarget: ¿En qué colonia vive usted?
cards.exampleNative: What neighborhood do you live in?
cards.remember: Mexican addresses always include the colonia (neighborhood). Taxi drivers and deliveries ask for it.
cards.replyTarget: En el Centro, cerca de la plaza.

cards.target: la dirección
cards.native: address, direction
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Cuál es la dirección del restaurante?
cards.exampleNative: What's the restaurant's address?
cards.remember: Usually it means the address.
cards.replyNative: Can you write it down for me, please?

cards.target: la esquina con…
cards.native: at the corner of … and …
cards.exampleTarget: Está en la avenida del Mar, esquina con la calle Palma.
cards.exampleNative: It's on Avenida del Mar, at the corner of Calle Palma.
cards.remember: Mexicans give locations as one street "esquina con" (on the corner of) another.

cards.target: primera · segunda · tercera
cards.native: first · second · third
cards.exampleTarget: Das vuelta en la segunda calle a la derecha.
cards.exampleNative: You turn at the second street on the right.
cards.remember: These agree with the noun: el primer semáforo (the first traffic light), la primera calle (the first street). primero (first) drops the -o before a masculine noun.

cards.target: de este lado · del otro lado
cards.native: on this side · on the other side
cards.exampleTarget: El cajero está del otro lado de la calle.
cards.exampleNative: The ATM is on the other side of the street.

cards.target: adelante · más adelante · atrás
cards.native: ahead · further ahead · back, behind
cards.exampleTarget: La farmacia está un poco más adelante.
cards.exampleNative: The pharmacy is a little further ahead.

cards.target: aquí mero · ahí mero
cards.native: right here · right there (MX)
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Dónde está la parada? → Aquí mero.
cards.exampleNative: Where's the stop? → Right here.
cards.remember: Very Mexican. mero adds "exactly".
cards.replyNative: And how often does it come?

cards.target: está a dos cuadras · está a un kilómetro
cards.native: it's two blocks away · it's a kilometer away
cards.exampleTarget: El mercado está a dos cuadras de aquí.
cards.exampleNative: The market is two blocks from here.
cards.remember: Distance uses estar a (to be … away) + the distance.

cards.target: a cinco minutos caminando · a diez minutos en carro
cards.native: five minutes on foot · ten minutes by car
cards.exampleTarget: La playa está a cinco minutos caminando.
cards.exampleNative: The beach is five minutes away on foot.
cards.remember: caminando = walking. Same pattern: estar a + time.

cards.target: ¿qué tan lejos está? · ¿está cerca de aquí?
cards.native: how far is it? · is it near here?
cards.exampleTarget: Disculpe, ¿qué tan lejos está el centro?
cards.exampleNative: Excuse me, how far is downtown?
cards.remember: qué tan (how) + describing word = how (far, big, expensive).
cards.replyNative: Should I take a taxi instead?

cards.target: ¿dónde queda…?
cards.native: where is … located?
cards.exampleTarget: Disculpe, ¿dónde queda el mercado?
cards.exampleNative: Excuse me, where is the market?
cards.remember: Same as ¿dónde está…? (where is…?) for places. You'll hear it a lot.

cards.target: la banqueta · el tope
cards.native: sidewalk (MX) · speed bump (MX)
cards.exampleTarget: Hay un tope antes del puente.
cards.exampleNative: There's a speed bump before the bridge.
cards.remember: Watch for topes (speed bumps) in every Mexican town.

cards.target: la entrada / la salida
cards.native: entrance / exit
cards.exampleTarget: La entrada está del otro lado.
cards.exampleNative: The entrance is on the other side.
cards.remember: You'll see both on every sign.

cards.target: el letrero
cards.native: sign
cards.exampleTarget: Das vuelta donde está el letrero azul.
cards.exampleNative: You turn where the blue sign is.

cards.target: el taxi · el sitio
cards.native: taxi · taxi stand (MX)
cards.exampleTarget: Hay un sitio de taxis en la esquina.
cards.exampleNative: There's a taxi stand on the corner.
cards.remember: A sitio is a stand where taxis wait.
cards.replyNative: How much do they charge to downtown?

cards.target: el Uber · la app · pedir un Uber
cards.native: Uber · the app · to order an Uber
cards.exampleTarget: Pido un Uber con la app.
cards.exampleNative: I order an Uber with the app.
cards.remember: pedir = to ask for, order. pido, pides, pide (I ask for, you ask for, he / she asks for).

cards.target: el chofer
cards.native: driver (taxi, bus, private)
cards.exampleTarget: El chofer es muy amable.
cards.exampleNative: The driver is very nice.
cards.remember: Mexico stresses the last syllable: cho-FER (driver). Spain writes and says chófer.

cards.target: ¿cuánto cobra a…? · ¿cuánto cobra al…?
cards.native: how much do you charge to…? · how much to the…?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Cuánto cobra al aeropuerto?
cards.exampleNative: How much do you charge to the airport?
cards.remember: Ask before you get in. Many taxis charge a set price by zone, not by meter.

cards.target: ¿me deja aquí? · ¿me deja en la esquina?
cards.native: can you drop me here? · can you drop me at the corner?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Me deja aquí, por favor? Gracias.
cards.exampleNative: Can you drop me off here, please? Thanks.
cards.remember: From dejar, to leave or drop off. Learn the me as part of the phrase.
cards.replyNative: How much do I owe you?

cards.target: aquí está bien · ¿puede parar aquí?
cards.native: here is fine · can you stop here?
cards.exampleTarget: Aquí está bien, gracias. ¿Cuánto es?
cards.exampleNative: Here is fine, thanks. How much is it?

cards.target: ¿tiene cambio?
cards.native: do you have change?
cards.exampleTarget: Sólo tengo un billete de quinientos. ¿Tiene cambio?
cards.exampleNative: I only have a 500 bill. Do you have change?
cards.remember: Carry small bills. Drivers often don't have change.
cards.replyNative: If not, I'll pay by card.

cards.target: la ruta · ¿qué ruta va a…?
cards.native: bus route · which route goes to…?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Qué ruta va al centro?
cards.exampleNative: Which route goes downtown?
cards.remember: Buses show their route and stops painted on the windshield.

cards.target: ¿este camión va a…? · ¿pasa por…?
cards.native: does this bus go to…? · does it go by…?
cards.exampleTarget: Disculpe, ¿este camión va a la playa?
cards.exampleNative: Excuse me, does this bus go to the beach?
cards.remember: Ask the chofer (driver) as you get on.
cards.replyNative: Will you tell me where to get off?

cards.target: subir al camión / bajar del camión
cards.native: to get on the bus / to get off the bus
cards.exampleTarget: Bajo del camión en la plaza.
cards.exampleNative: I get off the bus at the plaza.
cards.remember: You go up into the bus (subir a) and down out of it (bajar de).

cards.target: ¡bajan! · en la esquina, por favor
cards.native: getting off! · at the corner, please
cards.exampleTarget: ¡Bajan! → El chofer para en la esquina.
cards.exampleNative: Getting off! → The driver stops at the corner.
cards.remember: Call out ¡bajan! (getting off!) or press the button so the bus stops.

cards.target: el pasaje · la tarifa
cards.native: bus fare · rate, fare
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Cuánto es el pasaje?
cards.exampleNative: How much is the bus fare?
cards.remember: Pay the chofer (driver) when you get on.
cards.replyNative: Do you have change for a fifty?

cards.target: ¿cada cuánto pasa el camión? · ¿cuánto tarda?
cards.native: how often does the bus come? · how long does it take?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Cada cuánto pasa el camión al centro? → Cada diez minutos.
cards.exampleNative: How often does the bus to downtown come? → Every ten minutes.
cards.remember: cada = every. Learn ¿cuánto tarda? (how long does it take?) as a whole phrase.
cards.replyTarget: ¿Y el último a qué hora pasa?
cards.replyNative: And what time does the last one come?

cards.target: en camión · en taxi · en carro · a pie
cards.native: by bus · by taxi · by car · on foot
cards.exampleTarget: Voy al centro en camión y regreso a pie.
cards.exampleNative: I go downtown by bus and come back on foot.
cards.remember: "By" a vehicle is en. On foot is a pie.

cards.target: el autobús · la central de autobuses
cards.native: coach, long-distance bus · bus station
cards.exampleTarget: El autobús a Guadalajara sale de la central.
cards.exampleNative: The bus to Guadalajara leaves from the bus station.
cards.remember: camión (bus) is the everyday word for any bus. autobús (bus) is more formal and common on long-distance signs and tickets.

cards.target: la gasolinera · la gasolina
cards.native: gas station · gasoline
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Hay una gasolinera cerca de aquí?
cards.exampleNative: Is there a gas station near here?
cards.remember: An attendant pumps the gas. A small tip is normal.

cards.target: lleno, por favor · quinientos de magna
cards.native: fill it up, please · 500 pesos of regular
cards.exampleTarget: Lleno, por favor. Con tarjeta.
cards.exampleNative: Fill it up, please. With card.
cards.remember: You can ask for a full tank or a peso amount. Magna is regular gas.
cards.replyTarget: ¿Me revisa el aire de las llantas?
cards.replyNative: Can you check the tire pressure?

cards.target: estacionar · el estacionamiento
cards.native: to park · parking lot
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Dónde puedo estacionar? → Hay un estacionamiento a la vuelta.
cards.exampleNative: Where can I park? → There's a parking lot around the corner.
cards.replyNative: How much do they charge per hour?

cards.target: manejar · rentar un carro
cards.native: to drive (MX) · to rent a car
cards.exampleTarget: Rento un carro y manejo a Sayulita.
cards.exampleNative: I rent a car and drive to Sayulita.
cards.remember: Mexico says manejar for drive.
cards.replyNative: Do you need an international license?

cards.target: la licencia de manejo
cards.native: driver's license
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Tiene su licencia de manejo?
cards.exampleNative: Do you have your driver's license?

cards.target: el tráfico · hay mucho tráfico
cards.native: traffic · there's a lot of traffic
cards.exampleTarget: Hay mucho tráfico en la avenida a las seis.
cards.exampleNative: There's a lot of traffic on the avenue at six.

cards.target: la bici · la lancha
cards.native: bike · small boat, water taxi
cards.exampleTarget: Hay una lancha a la playa a las diez.
cards.exampleNative: There's a water taxi to the beach at ten.
cards.remember: bici (bike) is short for bicicleta (bicycle).

cards.target: otro · otra · más
cards.native: another (m.) · another (f.) · more
cards.exampleTarget: Otra cerveza, por favor. · Más tortillas.
cards.exampleNative: Another beer, please. · More tortillas.
cards.remember: Never say un otro (an another). otro / otra (another) never takes un or una (a).

cards.target: desayuno · comida · cena
cards.native: breakfast · main midday meal · light evening meal
cards.exampleTarget: La comida es a las tres y la cena es ligera.
cards.exampleNative: The main meal is at three and dinner is light.
cards.remember: In Mexico la comida (the main meal) is the big meal, about 2 to 4 p.m. Lunch at noon is rare.

cards.target: una mesa para dos · ¿cuántos son? · somos cuatro
cards.native: a table for two · how many are you? · there are four of us
cards.exampleTarget: Buenas noches. Una mesa para dos, por favor.
cards.exampleNative: Good evening. A table for two, please.
cards.replyTarget: ¿Tiene una mesa cerca de la ventana?
cards.replyNative: Do you have a table by the window?

cards.target: adentro o en la terraza
cards.native: inside or on the patio
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Adentro o en la terraza? → En la terraza, por favor.
cards.exampleNative: Inside or on the patio? → On the patio, please.

cards.target: la reservación
cards.native: reservation
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo una reservación a las ocho para cuatro.
cards.exampleNative: I have a reservation at eight for four.
cards.remember: Mexico says reservación (reservation) more than reserva.

cards.target: el menú · la carta
cards.native: menu · menu (a bit more formal)
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Me trae la carta, por favor?
cards.exampleNative: Could you bring me the menu, please?
cards.remember: Both are used. menú (menu) can also mean the set lunch.

cards.target: quisiera…
cards.native: I'd like…
cards.exampleTarget: Quisiera una cerveza y la sopa, por favor.
cards.exampleNative: I'd like a beer and the soup, please.
cards.remember: A softer form of querer (to want). Learn it as a fixed phrase for ordering and shopping.

cards.target: quiero / quisiera
cards.native: I want / I'd like
cards.exampleTarget: Quiero agua. · Quisiera agua, por favor.
cards.exampleNative: I want water. · I'd like water, please.
cards.remember: Both are fine with por favor (please). quisiera (I would like) sounds more polite.

cards.target: ¿me trae…?
cards.native: could you bring me…?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Me trae más tortillas, por favor?
cards.exampleNative: Could you bring me more tortillas, please?
cards.remember: From traer (to bring): literally "do you bring me".

cards.target: ¿me da…?
cards.native: can I have…? (literally "do you give me")
cards.exampleTarget: Me da dos tacos de pastor y un agua de horchata.
cards.exampleNative: I'll have two al pastor tacos and a horchata.
cards.remember: At taco stands and counters this is the normal way to order.
cards.replyTarget: ¿De cuál es el agua de hoy?
cards.replyNative: What flavor is today's agua fresca?

cards.target: la orden · una orden de…
cards.native: order · an order (plate) of…
cards.exampleTarget: Una orden de tacos de pescado, por favor.
cards.exampleNative: An order of fish tacos, please.
cards.remember: Taco stands sell by la orden (the order), a plate of several tacos. Ask how many come in one.

cards.target: ¿qué me recomienda? · ¿qué es lo más rico?
cards.native: what do you recommend? · what's the best thing here?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Qué me recomienda? → El pescado está muy rico.
cards.exampleNative: What do you recommend? → The fish is very good.
cards.remember: Learn ¿qué me recomienda? (what do you recommend?) whole.

cards.target: ¿qué lleva?
cards.native: what's in it?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Qué lleva la ensalada? → Lechuga, jitomate y queso.
cards.exampleNative: What's in the salad? → Lettuce, tomato and cheese.
cards.remember: llevar (to carry) here means to contain.
cards.replyNative: Can you bring it to me without cheese?

cards.target: sin cebolla · con todo
cards.native: without onion · with everything
cards.exampleTarget: Dos tacos con todo y uno sin cebolla.
cards.exampleNative: Two tacos with everything and one without onion.
cards.remember: With tacos, con todo (with everything) means with onion and cilantro.
cards.replyNative: And the salsa on the side?

cards.target: ¿pica? · pica mucho · no pica
cards.native: is it spicy? · it's very spicy · it isn't spicy
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Pica la salsa verde? → Sí, pica mucho.
cards.exampleNative: Is the green salsa spicy? → Yes, it's very spicy.
cards.remember: picar = to sting, burn. "No pica" (it's not spicy) can still mean "a little" to a local.

cards.target: sin picante · picante
cards.native: not spicy · spicy, hot
cards.exampleTarget: La sopa sin picante, por favor.
cards.exampleNative: The soup with no chile, please.
cards.remember: picante (spicy) describes the dish; ¿pica? (is it spicy?) asks about it.
cards.replyTarget: Y la salsa aparte, por favor.
cards.replyNative: And the salsa on the side, please.

cards.target: para mí… · para ella…
cards.native: for me… · for her…
cards.exampleTarget: Para mí, el pollo. Para ella, la ensalada.
cards.exampleNative: For me, the chicken. For her, the salad.
cards.remember: Ordering for each person at the table.

cards.target: ¿algo más? · es todo
cards.native: anything else? · that's all
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Algo más? → No, es todo, gracias.
cards.exampleNative: Anything else? → No, that's all, thanks.

cards.target: ¿qué les traigo? · ¿qué van a tomar?
cards.native: what can I bring you? · what will you have to drink?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Qué les traigo? → Dos aguas naturales.
cards.exampleNative: What can I bring you? → Two still waters.
cards.remember: What the waiter says. tomar = to drink here.
cards.replyNative: What aguas frescas do you have?

cards.target: ya no hay · se acabó
cards.native: there's none left · it's all gone
cards.exampleTarget: Lo siento, ya no hay pescado.
cards.exampleNative: Sorry, there's no more fish.
cards.replyTarget: ¿Y qué me recomienda en su lugar?
cards.replyNative: And what do you recommend instead?

cards.target: el plato del día · la comida corrida
cards.native: dish of the day · set lunch (MX)
cards.exampleTarget: La comida corrida incluye sopa, arroz, plato fuerte y agua.
cards.exampleNative: The set lunch includes soup, rice, a main dish and a drink.
cards.remember: Cheap, filling and only at midday. Look for it in small fondas (family-run eateries).

cards.target: para llevar / para comer aquí
cards.native: to go / to eat here
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Para llevar o para comer aquí? → Para llevar.
cards.exampleNative: To go or to eat here? → To go.
cards.remember: You'll hear this at every counter.
cards.replyNative: Can you put the salsa on the side?

cards.target: ¿me cobra? · cuentas separadas
cards.native: can I pay? (MX) · separate checks
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Me cobra, por favor? Cuentas separadas.
cards.exampleNative: Can I pay, please? Separate checks.
cards.remember: ¿me cobra? (can I pay?) is what Mexicans say at a counter instead of asking for the check.
cards.replyTarget: Yo pago lo mío con tarjeta.

cards.target: la propina · dejar propina
cards.native: tip · to leave a tip
cards.exampleTarget: Dejo el quince por ciento de propina.
cards.exampleNative: I leave a fifteen percent tip.
cards.remember: 10 to 15 % is normal in restaurants. por ciento = percent.
cards.replyNative: Can I put it on the card?

cards.target: ¿está incluida la propina?
cards.native: is the tip included?
cards.exampleTarget: Disculpe, ¿está incluida la propina?
cards.exampleNative: Excuse me, is the tip included?
cards.remember: Check the bill for "servicio" (service charge). Some tourist places add it.
cards.replyTarget: Entonces le dejo el diez por ciento.
cards.replyNative: Then I'll leave you ten percent.

cards.target: el almuerzo · el antojito · la botana
cards.native: late-morning brunch · snack, street bite · bar snack
cards.exampleTarget: Con la cerveza traen una botana.
cards.exampleNative: They bring a snack with the beer.
cards.remember: In Mexico almuerzo is a late breakfast, not lunch.

cards.target: el vaso
cards.native: drinking glass
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Me trae un vaso con hielo?
cards.exampleNative: Could you bring me a glass with ice?
cards.remember: vaso is the glass you drink from; vidrio is the material.

cards.target: la cuchara · el tenedor · el cuchillo
cards.native: spoon · fork · knife
cards.exampleTarget: Necesito una cuchara para la sopa.
cards.exampleNative: I need a spoon for the soup.

cards.target: la servilleta · el popote
cards.native: napkin · drinking straw (MX)
cards.exampleTarget: Una servilleta, por favor. · Sin popote, gracias.
cards.exampleNative: A napkin, please. · No straw, thanks.
cards.remember: popote (straw) is Mexican. Elsewhere it's pajita or pitillo.
cards.replyNative: Can you bring me the check?

cards.target: el hielo · con hielo · sin hielo
cards.native: ice · with ice · without ice
cards.exampleTarget: Una limonada sin hielo, por favor.
cards.exampleNative: A lemonade without ice, please.
cards.remember: Most restaurants use ice made from purified water. At street stalls it's less certain.

cards.target: la sal · la pimienta
cards.native: salt · pepper
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Me pasa la sal?
cards.exampleNative: Could you pass me the salt?
cards.remember: ¿me pasa…? is the polite "pass me".

cards.target: agua natural · agua mineral
cards.native: still water · sparkling water
cards.exampleTarget: Un agua natural y un agua mineral, por favor.
cards.exampleNative: A still water and a sparkling water, please.
cards.remember: agua mineral (mineral water) is always fizzy. Ask for natural (plain) if you want plain.

cards.target: el agua de jamaica · el agua de horchata · las aguas frescas
cards.native: hibiscus drink · rice-cinnamon drink · fresh fruit waters
cards.exampleTarget: Un agua de jamaica grande, por favor.
cards.exampleNative: A large hibiscus water, please.
cards.remember: agua (water) is feminine but takes el in the singular: el agua fresca (fruit water).
cards.replyTarget: Y una de horchata para ella.

cards.target: el refresco · el jugo
cards.native: soda · juice
cards.exampleTarget: Un jugo de naranja y un refresco, por favor.
cards.exampleNative: An orange juice and a soda, please.

cards.target: la cerveza · bien fría
cards.native: beer · nice and cold
cards.exampleTarget: Una cerveza bien fría, por favor.
cards.exampleNative: A nice cold beer, please.
cards.remember: bien before a describing word = really, nice and.

cards.target: el vino · tinto · blanco
cards.native: wine · red · white
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Tiene vino tinto de la casa?
cards.exampleNative: Do you have a red house wine?
cards.remember: Red wine is vino tinto, never vino rojo.

cards.target: el pollo · la carne · la res · el puerco
cards.native: chicken · meat · beef · pork
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Los tacos son de res o de puerco?
cards.exampleNative: Are the tacos beef or pork?
cards.remember: carne asada is grilled beef. tacos de… tells you the filling.

cards.target: el pescado / el pez
cards.native: fish (food) / fish (alive)
cards.exampleTarget: El pescado está fresco. · Hay un pez en el agua.
cards.exampleNative: The fish is fresh. · There's a fish in the water.
cards.remember: You eat pescado. A pez is swimming.

cards.target: los camarones · el pulpo · el ceviche
cards.native: shrimp · octopus · ceviche
cards.exampleTarget: Quisiera un ceviche de camarón.
cards.exampleNative: I'd like a shrimp ceviche.
cards.remember: Under mariscos (seafood) on the menu.

cards.target: el arroz · los frijoles
cards.native: rice · beans
cards.exampleTarget: La comida incluye arroz y frijoles.
cards.exampleNative: The meal comes with rice and beans.
cards.remember: frijoles refritos = mashed, refried beans.

cards.target: las tortillas de maíz · de harina · los totopos
cards.native: corn tortillas · flour tortillas · tortilla chips
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Tortillas de maíz o de harina? → De maíz.
cards.exampleNative: Corn or flour tortillas? → Corn.
cards.remember: Corn is the default in Jalisco.

cards.target: los huevos · revueltos · estrellados
cards.native: eggs · scrambled · fried (sunny side up)
cards.exampleTarget: Quisiera dos huevos estrellados con frijoles.
cards.exampleNative: I'd like two fried eggs with beans.
cards.remember: huevos rancheros are fried eggs with salsa on a tortilla.

cards.target: el pan · el pan dulce · la concha
cards.native: bread · Mexican sweet bread · sweet roll with a shell-shaped top
cards.exampleTarget: Un café y un pan dulce, por favor.
cards.exampleNative: A coffee and a sweet roll, please.

cards.target: el queso · la crema
cards.native: cheese · Mexican sour cream
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Lleva queso? → Sí, queso y crema.
cards.exampleNative: Does it have cheese? → Yes, cheese and cream.

cards.target: las verduras · la ensalada
cards.native: vegetables · salad
cards.exampleTarget: Quisiera el pollo con verduras.
cards.exampleNative: I'd like the chicken with vegetables.

cards.target: la sopa · el caldo
cards.native: soup · brothy soup, stew
cards.exampleTarget: Hay caldo de pollo los lunes.
cards.exampleNative: There's chicken soup on Mondays.
cards.remember: sopa de fideo (noodle soup) is a classic first course.
cards.replyNative: Then I'll come back on Monday.

cards.target: el postre · el flan
cards.native: dessert · flan, caramel custard
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Qué hay de postre? → Flan y pastel.
cards.exampleNative: What is there for dessert? → Flan and cake.

cards.target: el limón
cards.native: lime (the small green one)
cards.exampleTarget: Una cerveza con limón y sal.
cards.exampleNative: A beer with lime and salt.
cards.remember: In Mexico limón means the green lime. Yellow lemons are rare.

cards.target: el aguacate · el guacamole
cards.native: avocado · guacamole
cards.exampleTarget: ¿El guacamole lleva cebolla?
cards.exampleNative: Does the guacamole have onion?

cards.target: el jitomate · la cebolla · el chile · el cilantro
cards.native: tomato · onion · chili pepper · cilantro
cards.exampleTarget: Sin chile y sin cilantro, por favor.
cards.exampleNative: No chili and no cilantro, please.
cards.remember: jitomate is the red tomato in Mexico. tomate (verde) is the green tomatillo.

cards.target: frito · asado · a la plancha · empanizado
cards.native: fried · grilled · cooked on a griddle · breaded
cards.exampleTarget: Quisiera el pescado a la plancha, no frito.
cards.exampleNative: I'd like the fish griddled, not fried.
cards.remember: These agree with the food: pollo asado (roast chicken), carne asada (grilled beef).

cards.target: dulce · salado · picante · ácido
cards.native: sweet · salty · spicy · sour
cards.exampleTarget: La salsa está muy picante y un poco salada.
cards.exampleNative: The salsa is very spicy and a little salty.
cards.replyNative: Can you bring me water, please?

cards.target: soy vegetarian@ · no como carne
cards.native: I'm vegetarian · I don't eat meat
cards.exampleTarget: Soy vegetariana. ¿Qué platos no llevan carne?
cards.exampleNative: I'm vegetarian. Which dishes have no meat?
cards.remember: Ask about the beans too. Some are made with lard (manteca).
cards.replyNative: Do the beans have lard in them?

cards.target: me queda / me quedan
cards.native: it fits me / they fit me
cards.exampleTarget: La falda me queda bien, pero los zapatos me quedan chicos.
cards.exampleNative: The skirt fits well, but the shoes are too small.
cards.remember: Works like gustar (to please, unit 13): queda (fits) for one thing, quedan for more than one.
cards.replyNative: Do you have a bigger size?

cards.target: nada más estoy viendo · ¿en qué le puedo ayudar?
cards.native: I'm just looking · how can I help you?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿En qué le puedo ayudar? → Nada más estoy viendo, gracias.
cards.exampleNative: How can I help you? → I'm just looking, thanks.
cards.remember: Learn the -ndo form as part of the phrase. It's unit 16.
cards.replyNative: Well, how much is this one?

cards.target: la tienda de ropa · la zapatería
cards.native: clothing store · shoe store
cards.exampleTarget: La zapatería está a dos cuadras.
cards.exampleNative: The shoe store is two blocks away.
cards.remember: -ería is a shop: zapatería (shoe store), panadería (bakery), papelería (stationery store).

cards.target: la talla · ¿qué talla es?
cards.native: size (clothes) · what size is it?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Qué talla es esta playera? → Es mediana.
cards.exampleNative: What size is this T-shirt? → It's a medium.
cards.remember: Sizes in Mexican stores often run small.
cards.replyNative: Do you have a large one?

cards.target: chica · mediana · grande · extra grande
cards.native: small · medium · large · extra large
cards.exampleTarget: ¿La tiene en chica o en mediana?
cards.exampleNative: Do you have it in small or medium?
cards.remember: Sizes say chica (small), not pequeña. Matches la talla (the size).

cards.target: el número · ¿qué número usa?
cards.native: shoe size · what size do you wear?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Qué número usa? → Uso el veintiséis.
cards.exampleNative: What size do you wear? → I wear a 26.
cards.remember: Mexico measures shoes in centimeters, about 22 to 30.
cards.replyNative: Do you have these in brown?

cards.target: ¿me lo puedo probar? · ¿me la puedo probar?
cards.native: can I try it on? (a masculine thing · a feminine thing)
cards.exampleTarget: Me gusta este vestido. ¿Me lo puedo probar?
cards.exampleNative: I like this dress. Can I try it on?
cards.remember: Learn it whole. lo / la (it) matches the clothing.

cards.target: el probador
cards.native: fitting room
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Dónde está el probador?
cards.exampleNative: Where is the fitting room?

cards.target: me queda grande · me queda chico
cards.native: it's too big on me · it's too small on me
cards.exampleTarget: La camisa me queda grande.
cards.exampleNative: The shirt is too big on me.
cards.remember: Fixed phrase. No "too" needed in Spanish.
cards.replyNative: Do you have a smaller one?

cards.target: me queda bien · ¿cómo me queda?
cards.native: it fits me well · how does it look on me?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Cómo me queda? → Te queda muy bien.
cards.exampleNative: How does it look on me? → It looks really good on you.
cards.remember: te queda (it fits you) for tú, le queda for usted.

cards.target: la camisa · la playera
cards.native: shirt (with buttons) · T-shirt (MX)
cards.exampleTarget: Quisiera una playera blanca, talla grande.
cards.exampleNative: I'd like a white T-shirt, size large.
cards.remember: playera (T-shirt) is Mexican. Elsewhere it's camiseta.
cards.replyNative: Do you have it in blue?

cards.target: manga corta · manga larga
cards.native: short-sleeved · long-sleeved
cards.exampleTarget: Una camisa de manga corta para el calor.
cards.exampleNative: A short-sleeved shirt for the heat.
cards.replyNative: Do you have it in white?

cards.target: los pantalones · los shorts
cards.native: pants · shorts
cards.exampleTarget: Estos pantalones me quedan largos.
cards.exampleNative: These pants are too long on me.
cards.remember: Both are plural in Spanish, like English.
cards.replyNative: Can they be altered for me?

cards.target: el vestido · la falda
cards.native: dress · skirt
cards.exampleTarget: El vestido azul es más barato que la falda.
cards.exampleNative: The blue dress is cheaper than the skirt.

cards.target: los zapatos · las sandalias · los tenis
cards.native: shoes · sandals · sneakers
cards.exampleTarget: Necesito tenis para caminar.
cards.exampleNative: I need sneakers for walking.
cards.remember: tenis = sneakers in Mexico, and it stays tenis for one shoe too.
cards.replyNative: What size shoe do you wear?

cards.target: los calcetines · la ropa interior
cards.native: socks · underwear
cards.exampleTarget: Los calcetines están en la caja.
cards.exampleNative: The socks are at the register.

cards.target: el sombrero · la gorra
cards.native: hat (with a brim) · cap
cards.exampleTarget: Necesito un sombrero para la playa.
cards.exampleNative: I need a hat for the beach.
cards.replyNative: Do you have a bigger one?

cards.target: los lentes de sol · los lentes
cards.native: sunglasses · glasses (MX)
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Dónde están mis lentes de sol?
cards.exampleNative: Where are my sunglasses?
cards.remember: Mexico says lentes (glasses). You may also hear gafas.

cards.target: el traje de baño
cards.native: swimsuit
cards.exampleTarget: Busco un traje de baño para niña.
cards.exampleNative: I'm looking for a girl's swimsuit.

cards.target: la chamarra · el suéter
cards.native: jacket (MX) · sweater
cards.exampleTarget: En diciembre necesito un suéter en la noche.
cards.exampleNative: In December I need a sweater at night.
cards.remember: chamarra is Mexican for a jacket.

cards.target: el cinturón · la cartera
cards.native: belt · wallet
cards.exampleTarget: Mi cartera está en la bolsa.
cards.exampleNative: My wallet is in the bag.

cards.target: ¿tiene otro color? · ¿lo tiene en azul?
cards.native: do you have another color? · do you have it in blue?
cards.exampleTarget: Me gusta, pero ¿tiene otro color?
cards.exampleNative: I like it, but do you have another color?
cards.remember: Remember: otro color (another color), never un otro color.

cards.target: ¿lo tiene en otra talla?
cards.native: do you have it in another size?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Lo tiene en otra talla? Me queda chico.
cards.exampleNative: Do you have it in another size? It's too small on me.
cards.replyNative: I need it in a medium.

cards.target: ¿tiene más barato? · ¿tiene algo más barato?
cards.native: anything cheaper? · do you have something cheaper?
cards.exampleTarget: Está muy caro. ¿Tiene algo más barato?
cards.exampleNative: It's very expensive. Do you have something cheaper?
cards.remember: más barato = cheaper. Same pattern: más grande (bigger), más chico (smaller).
cards.replyTarget: Mi presupuesto es de quinientos pesos.
cards.replyNative: My budget is five hundred pesos.

cards.target: ¿me hace un descuento? · ¿me lo deja en…?
cards.native: can you give me a discount? · will you let me have it for…?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Me lo deja en trescientos?
cards.exampleNative: Will you let me have it for three hundred?
cards.remember: Bargaining is normal at markets and stalls, but not in stores.
cards.replyTarget: Si me llevo dos, ¿me hace precio?
cards.replyNative: If I take two, will you give me a deal?

cards.target: la oferta · en oferta
cards.native: special offer, sale · on sale
cards.exampleTarget: Las sandalias están en oferta.
cards.exampleNative: The sandals are on sale.

cards.target: me lo llevo · me la llevo
cards.native: I'll take it (masculine thing · feminine thing)
cards.exampleTarget: Me queda bien. Me la llevo.
cards.exampleNative: It fits well. I'll take it.
cards.remember: Fixed phrase from llevar (to take). lo / la (it) matches the item.
cards.replyNative: Can you gift wrap it for me?

cards.target: ¿cuánto le debo?
cards.native: what do I owe you?
cards.exampleTarget: Son dos playeras y una gorra. ¿Cuánto le debo?
cards.exampleNative: It's two T-shirts and a cap. What do I owe you?
cards.remember: A polite way to ask for the total.
cards.replyNative: Can I have the receipt, please?

cards.target: ¿quiere bolsa? · traigo mi bolsa
cards.native: do you want a bag? · I have my own bag
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Quiere bolsa? → No, gracias, traigo mi bolsa.
cards.exampleNative: Do you want a bag? → No thanks, I have my bag.
cards.remember: Many stores charge for bags or don't give them.

cards.target: el ticket · el recibo · la factura
cards.native: receipt (store slip) · receipt · official tax invoice
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Me da el ticket, por favor?
cards.exampleNative: Can I have the receipt, please?
cards.remember: Keep the ticket to exchange things. A factura is the formal invoice for taxes.
cards.replyNative: Can you make me a tax invoice?

cards.target: cambiar · ¿lo puedo cambiar?
cards.native: to exchange · can I exchange it?
cards.exampleTarget: Me queda chico. ¿Lo puedo cambiar? Aquí está el ticket.
cards.exampleNative: It's too small for me. Can I exchange it? Here's the receipt.
cards.remember: cambiar = to change or exchange. el cambio is your change.
cards.replyTarget: Lo quiero en una talla más grande.
cards.replyNative: I want it in a bigger size.

cards.target: no hay devoluciones · sólo cambios
cards.native: no refunds · exchanges only
cards.exampleTarget: Lo siento, no hay devoluciones, sólo cambios.
cards.exampleNative: Sorry, no refunds, only exchanges.
cards.remember: A common sign at the register.
cards.replyNative: Okay, can I exchange it for another color?

cards.group: Grammar: pronouns: me, lo, le, and the personal a
cards.target: me llamo · te llamas · se llama
cards.native: Reflexive verbs: the action comes back to the subject. me llamo = I call myself. The pronoun matches the subject: me, te, se, nos, se.
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Cómo te llamas? → Me llamo Tony. Mi amiga se llama Ana.
cards.exampleNative: What's your name? → My name is Tony. My friend's name is Ana.
cards.remember: Seen in Lesson 1.
cards.meaning: my name is · your name is · his / her name is, your (polite) name is

cards.group: Grammar: pronouns: me, lo, le, and the personal a
cards.target: cuidarse · preocuparse · mejorarse
cards.native: Reflexive verbs end in -se in the dictionary. Conjugate the verb and move the pronoun in front: me cuido, te preocupas, se mejora.
cards.exampleTarget: Me cuido mucho. No te preocupes. Que se mejore.
cards.exampleNative: I take good care of myself. Don't worry. Feel better.
cards.remember: Seen in Lessons 1, 4 and 5.
cards.meaning: to take care of yourself · to worry · to get better

cards.group: Grammar: pronouns: me, lo, le, and the personal a
cards.target: lo · la · los · las
cards.native: Direct object pronouns: it, him, her, them. They match the noun they replace and go before the conjugated verb.
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Tienes el celular? → Sí, ya lo tengo. ¿Y las llaves? → Las tengo también.
cards.exampleNative: Do you have the phone? → Yes, I already have it. And the keys? → I have them too.
cards.remember: Seen: ya lo tengo, I have it now (L5); no lo conozco, I don't know him (L3); si la necesitas, if you need it (L4); lo siento, I'm sorry (L1).
cards.meaning: it, him · it, her · them (m.) · them (f.)

cards.group: Grammar: pronouns: me, lo, le, and the personal a
cards.target: Lo tengo que comprar. = Tengo que comprarlo.
cards.native: With a verb + infinitive, the pronoun goes before the first verb or attaches to the end of the infinitive. Never between them.
cards.exampleTarget: La voy a llamar. = Voy a llamarla.
cards.exampleNative: I'm going to call her.
cards.meaning: I have to buy it. (two ways to say it)

cards.group: Grammar: pronouns: me, lo, le, and the personal a
cards.target: me · te · le · nos · les
cards.native: Indirect object pronouns: to / for me, you, him, her, you (form.), us, them.
cards.exampleTarget: La cajera le dice: "¿Tiene receta?" Me da gusto.
cards.exampleNative: The cashier says to her, "Do you have a prescription?" I'm glad (it gives me pleasure).
cards.remember: Seen in Lesson 5: le dice, les dice (says to him, says to them). Lesson 4: me da gusto (I'm glad).
cards.meaning: to / for me · you · him, her, you (polite) · us · them, you all

cards.group: Grammar: pronouns: me, lo, le, and the personal a
cards.target: Llamo a Ramón. · Conozco a Gabriel.
cards.native: The personal a: put a before a PERSON who receives the action. Not before things.
cards.exampleTarget: Conozco a la maestra y conozco la escuela.
cards.exampleNative: I know the teacher and I know the school.
cards.remember: Seen in Lesson 4: Marcela llama a Ramón (Marcela calls Ramón).
cards.meaning: I call Ramón. · I know Gabriel.
cards.replyNative: Will you introduce her to me?

cards.group: Grammar: pronouns: me, lo, le, and the personal a
cards.target: me gusta · me gustan
cards.native: gustar (to like) works backwards: "it pleases me". Use gusta for one thing or a verb, gustan for more than one.
cards.exampleTarget: Me gusta el café. Me gustan los tacos. Me gusta caminar.
cards.exampleNative: I like coffee. I like tacos. I like to walk.
cards.remember: Cousins you already know: mucho gusto (nice to meet you), me da gusto (I'm glad).
cards.meaning: I like it · I like them

cards.group: Grammar: pronouns: me, lo, le, and the personal a
cards.target: te gusta · le gusta · nos gusta · les gusta
cards.native: The pronoun shows who likes it. Add a + person for clarity: a mi esposa le gusta…
cards.exampleTarget: A mi esposa le gusta la playa. ¿Te gusta Puerto Vallarta?
cards.exampleNative: My wife likes the beach. Do you like Puerto Vallarta?
cards.meaning: you like it · he / she likes it, you (polite) like it · we like it · they like it, you all like it

cards.group: Grammar: pronouns: me, lo, le, and the personal a
cards.target: para mí · para ti · con él · conmigo · contigo
cards.native: After a preposition use mí, ti, él, ella, usted, nosotros, ellos. With con: conmigo, contigo.
cards.exampleTarget: El café es para ti. Mis hermanos están conmigo.
cards.exampleNative: The coffee is for you. My siblings are with me.
cards.remember: Seen in Lesson 4: ¿Están contigo? (Are they with you?) · con él (with him).
cards.meaning: for me · for you · with him · with me · with you

cards.group: Grammar: pronouns: me, lo, le, and the personal a
cards.target: se dice · se habla
cards.native: Impersonal se = "one / people / you" in general.
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Cómo se dice "key"? Aquí se habla español.
cards.exampleNative: How do you say "key"? Spanish is spoken here.
cards.remember: Seen in Lesson 1: ¿cómo se dice…? (how do you say…?)
cards.meaning: people say, it's said · people speak, it's spoken

cards.target: me lo · te lo · nos lo
cards.native: it to me · it to you · it to us
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Me lo puede mandar? · Te lo doy.
cards.exampleNative: Can you send it to me? · I'll give it to you.
cards.remember: Two pronouns: the person (me, te, nos: me, you, us) comes first, then the thing (lo, la, los, las: it, them).
cards.replyNative: Sure, I'll send it to you today.

cards.target: se lo · se la · se los · se las
cards.native: it (m.) to him, her, you · it (f.) to him, her, you · them (m.) to him, her, you · them (f.) to him, her, you
cards.exampleTarget: Se lo doy. · Se las mando mañana.
cards.exampleNative: I give it to him. · I'll send them to you tomorrow.
cards.remember: le and les (to him, her, them) become se before lo, la, los, las. Never say "le lo".

cards.target: le doy el libro → se lo doy
cards.native: I give him the book → I give it to him
cards.exampleTarget: Le doy la llave a Luis. → Se la doy.
cards.exampleNative: I give the key to Luis. → I give it to him.
cards.remember: Swap the thing for lo / la (it), then le (to him, her) changes to se.

cards.target: se lo doy a usted · a él · a ella
cards.native: I give it to you · to him · to her
cards.exampleTarget: Se lo doy a ella, no a él.
cards.exampleNative: I give it to her, not to him.
cards.remember: se can mean him, her, you or them. Add a (to) + person to make it clear.
cards.replyTarget: Ella se lo da a él.

cards.target: Te lo puedo mandar. = Puedo mandártelo.
cards.native: I can send it to you.
cards.exampleTarget: Se lo tengo que dar. = Tengo que dárselo.
cards.exampleNative: I have to give it to him.
cards.remember: Both pronouns go before the conjugated verb or attach to the infinitive, together. Attached, add an accent.
cards.replyNative: Send it to me today, please.

cards.target: me parece · me parecen
cards.native: it seems to me · they seem to me
cards.exampleTarget: Me parece caro. · Me parecen caros.
cards.exampleNative: It seems expensive to me. · They seem expensive to me.
cards.remember: parecer (to seem) works like gustar (to please): parece (seems) for one thing, parecen for more than one.

cards.target: ya lo tengo
cards.native: I already have it
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Tienes el celular? → Sí, ya lo tengo.
cards.exampleNative: Do you have the phone? → Yes, I already have it.

cards.target: no lo conozco
cards.native: I don't know him
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Quién es tu amigo? No lo conozco.
cards.exampleNative: Who's your friend? I don't know him.
cards.remember: From conocer (to know a person or place).
cards.replyNative: Will you introduce him to me?

cards.target: si la necesitas
cards.native: if you need it
cards.exampleTarget: La parada está ahí si la necesitas.
cards.exampleNative: The stop is there if you need it.
cards.remember: si without an accent = if.
cards.replyNative: Thanks, I'll look for it right now.

cards.target: ¿se lo cobro? · ¿se lo envuelvo?
cards.native: shall I ring it up for you? · shall I wrap it for you?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Se lo cobro? → Sí, por favor.
cards.exampleNative: Shall I ring it up for you? → Yes, please.
cards.remember: You'll hear se lo (it to you) from every cashier.

cards.target: me parece que…
cards.native: I think that…, it seems to me that…
cards.exampleTarget: Me parece que el restaurante está cerrado.
cards.exampleNative: I think the restaurant is closed.
cards.remember: Same idea as creo que (I think), a little softer.
cards.replyNative: Shall we look for another one?

cards.target: me parece bien · ¿te parece bien? · ¿qué te parece?
cards.native: sounds good to me · is that OK with you? · what do you think?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Comemos a las tres? ¿Te parece bien? → Me parece bien.
cards.exampleNative: Shall we eat at three? Is that OK with you? → Sounds good.
cards.remember: With usted: ¿le parece bien? (is that OK with you?) ¿qué le parece? (what do you think?)

cards.target: llamarse
cards.native: to be called (me llamo = my name is)
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Cómo se va a llamar el perro?
cards.exampleNative: What's the dog going to be called?
cards.remember: -ar verb, reflexive. After tener que (have to) or para (to, in order to) the pronoun attaches and matches the person: tengo que llamarme, tienes que llamarte.

cards.target:
llamarse · present
yo me llamo · tú te llamas · él / ella / usted se llama · nosotros nos llamamos · ellos / ustedes se llaman
cards.native:
to be called (me llamo = my name is) · present
my name is · your name is · his/her / your (form.) name is · our names are · their / your names are
cards.exampleTarget: Me llamo Tony y mi amigo se llama Luis.
cards.exampleNative: My name is Tony and my friend's name is Luis.
cards.remember: Now, habits and facts.

cards.target: cuidarse
cards.native: to take care of yourself (cuídate)
cards.exampleTarget: Tienes que cuidarte mucho.
cards.exampleNative: You have to take good care of yourself.
cards.remember: -ar verb, reflexive. After tener que (have to) or para (to, in order to) the pronoun attaches and matches the person: tengo que cuidarme, tienes que cuidarte.

cards.target:
cuidarse · present
yo me cuido · tú te cuidas · él / ella / usted se cuida · nosotros nos cuidamos · ellos / ustedes se cuidan
cards.native:
to take care of yourself (cuídate) · present
I take care · you take care · he/she takes care / you (form.) take care · we take care · they / you all take care
cards.exampleTarget: Me cuido mucho.
cards.exampleNative: I take good care of myself.
cards.remember: Now, habits and facts.

cards.target: preocuparse
cards.native: to worry (no te preocupes)
cards.exampleTarget: No tienes que preocuparte.
cards.exampleNative: You don't have to worry.
cards.remember: -ar verb, reflexive. After tener que (have to) or para (to, in order to) the pronoun attaches and matches the person: tengo que preocuparme, tienes que preocuparte.

cards.target:
preocuparse · present
yo me preocupo · tú te preocupas · él / ella / usted se preocupa · nosotros nos preocupamos · ellos / ustedes se preocupan
cards.native:
to worry (no te preocupes) · present
I worry · you worry · he/she worries / you (form.) worry · we worry · they / you all worry
cards.exampleTarget: Me preocupo por mi familia.
cards.exampleNative: I worry about my family.
cards.remember: Now, habits and facts.

cards.target: mejorarse
cards.native: to get better (que se mejore)
cards.exampleTarget: Tienes que mejorarte pronto.
cards.exampleNative: You have to get better soon.
cards.remember: -ar verb, reflexive. After tener que (have to) or para (to, in order to) the pronoun attaches and matches the person: tengo que mejorarme, tienes que mejorarte.

cards.target:
mejorarse · present
yo me mejoro · tú te mejoras · él / ella / usted se mejora · nosotros nos mejoramos · ellos / ustedes se mejoran
cards.native:
to get better (que se mejore) · present
I get better · you get better · he/she gets better / you (form.) get better · we get better · they / you all get better
cards.exampleTarget: Me mejoro poco a poco.
cards.exampleNative: I'm getting better little by little.
cards.remember: Now, habits and facts.

cards.target: me duele · me duelen
cards.native: it hurts (me) · they hurt (me)
cards.exampleTarget: Me duele la cabeza. · Me duelen los pies.
cards.exampleNative: My head hurts. · My feet hurt.
cards.remember: doler (to hurt) works like gustar (to please): duele (hurts) for one body part, duelen for more than one.
cards.replyNative: Do you have something for the pain?

cards.target: Me duele la espalda. (not mi espalda)
cards.native: My back hurts.
cards.exampleTarget: Me duele la rodilla y me duelen los ojos.
cards.exampleNative: My knee hurts and my eyes hurt.
cards.remember: With body parts Spanish uses el / la (the), not my. The me (to me) already says whose.

cards.target: ¿qué le duele? · ¿dónde le duele?
cards.native: what hurts? · where does it hurt? (usted)
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Dónde le duele? → Aquí, en el pecho.
cards.exampleNative: Where does it hurt? → Here, in my chest.
cards.remember: le duele (it hurts you) for usted, te duele for tú.

cards.target: tengo dolor de… · un dolor fuerte
cards.native: I have a … ache · a strong pain
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo dolor de estómago desde ayer.
cards.exampleNative: I've had a stomachache since yesterday.
cards.remember: dolor de cabeza = headache, dolor de muela = toothache.
cards.replyNative: What do you recommend I take?

cards.target: el cuerpo · la cara
cards.native: body · face
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo la cara roja del sol.
cards.exampleNative: My face is red from the sun.

cards.target: la cabeza · el cuello · la garganta
cards.native: head · neck · throat
cards.exampleTarget: Me duele la garganta y tengo tos.
cards.exampleNative: My throat hurts and I have a cough.

cards.target: el ojo · la nariz · la boca
cards.native: eye · nose · mouth
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo los ojos rojos.
cards.exampleNative: My eyes are red.

cards.target: el oído / la oreja
cards.native: ear (inside, hearing) / ear (outside)
cards.exampleTarget: Me duele el oído.
cards.exampleNative: My ear hurts.
cards.remember: An earache is in el oído. The part you see is la oreja.

cards.target: la muela · el diente
cards.native: molar · tooth
cards.exampleTarget: Me duele una muela. Necesito un dentista.
cards.exampleNative: I have a toothache. I need a dentist.
cards.remember: A toothache is almost always una muela (a back tooth).
cards.replyNative: Do you know a good one?

cards.target: el pecho · la espalda · el estómago
cards.native: chest · back · stomach
cards.exampleTarget: Me duele el pecho cuando camino.
cards.exampleNative: My chest hurts when I walk.
cards.remember: Chest pain: go to urgencias (the emergency room).
cards.replyTarget: Tiene que ver a un médico hoy.
cards.replyNative: You need to see a doctor today.

cards.target: el brazo · la mano · el dedo
cards.native: arm · hand · finger
cards.exampleTarget: Me duele la mano derecha.
cards.exampleNative: My right hand hurts.
cards.remember: la mano (the hand) is feminine even though it ends in -o.

cards.target: la pierna · la rodilla · el pie
cards.native: leg · knee · foot
cards.exampleTarget: Me duelen la rodilla y el pie.
cards.exampleNative: My knee and my foot hurt.

cards.target: la piel · quemad@ por el sol
cards.native: skin · sunburned
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo la piel quemada por el sol.
cards.exampleNative: My skin is sunburned.
cards.replyNative: Do you have something for burns?

cards.target: estoy hinchad@ · está hinchad@
cards.native: I'm swollen · it's swollen
cards.exampleTarget: La rodilla está hinchada.
cards.exampleNative: My knee is swollen.
cards.remember: Agrees with the body part: el pie hinchado (the swollen foot), la mano hinchada (the swollen hand).

cards.target: la gripa · tengo gripa
cards.native: a cold, the flu (MX) · I have a cold
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo gripa y me duele la garganta.
cards.exampleNative: I have a cold and my throat hurts.
cards.remember: Mexico says gripa (flu). You may hear gripe in other countries.
cards.replyNative: Do you have something for the throat?

cards.target: las náuseas · el vómito · la diarrea
cards.native: nausea · vomiting · diarrhea
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo náuseas y diarrea desde anoche.
cards.exampleNative: I've had nausea and diarrhea since last night.
cards.remember: tener náuseas = to feel nauseous.

cards.target: mareado · estoy mareado · estoy mareada
cards.native: dizzy · I'm dizzy (man) · I'm dizzy (woman)
cards.exampleTarget: Estoy mareada y tengo calor.
cards.exampleNative: I'm dizzy and hot.
cards.remember: Uses estar. Also means seasick or carsick.

cards.target: deshidratad@ · el suero oral
cards.native: dehydrated · oral rehydration drink
cards.exampleTarget: Estoy deshidratado. Necesito suero.
cards.exampleNative: I'm dehydrated. I need an electrolyte drink.
cards.remember: Pharmacies sell suero (rehydration drink) in bottles or packets.
cards.replyTarget: Te traigo uno de la farmacia.
cards.replyNative: I'll bring you one from the pharmacy.

cards.target: me siento mal · me siento mejor
cards.native: I feel sick · I feel better
cards.exampleTarget: Hoy me siento mejor, gracias.
cards.exampleNative: I feel better today, thanks.
cards.remember: From sentirse (to feel). Learn both whole.
cards.replyNative: I don't have a fever anymore.

cards.target: la presión alta · la presión baja
cards.native: high blood pressure · low blood pressure
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo la presión alta. Tomo una pastilla.
cards.exampleNative: I have high blood pressure. I take a pill.
cards.remember: Pharmacies often check it for free or a small fee.

cards.target: la alergia · soy alérgic@ a…
cards.native: allergy · I'm allergic to…
cards.exampleTarget: Soy alérgico a la penicilina.
cards.exampleNative: I'm allergic to penicillin.
cards.remember: soy (I am) for a permanent allergy. tengo alergia (I have an allergy) for symptoms right now.
cards.replyNative: Does this medicine have it in it?

cards.target: el mosco · el piquete
cards.native: mosquito (MX) · bite, sting
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo muchos piquetes de mosco en las piernas.
cards.exampleNative: I have a lot of mosquito bites on my legs.
cards.remember: Mexico says mosco (mosquito) more than mosquito.
cards.replyNative: Do you have something for the itching?

cards.target: ¿es grave? · no es grave
cards.native: is it serious? · it's not serious
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Es grave, doctora? → No, no es grave.
cards.exampleNative: Is it serious, doctor? → No, it's not serious.
cards.replyNative: Do I have to come back?

cards.target: el consultorio · la consulta
cards.native: doctor's office · visit, consultation
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Cuánto cuesta la consulta? → Doscientos pesos.
cards.exampleNative: How much is the visit? → Two hundred pesos.
cards.remember: Many pharmacies have a consultorio (doctor's office) next door with a cheap doctor's visit.

cards.target: el médico · el especialista
cards.native: doctor · specialist
cards.exampleTarget: Necesito un especialista para la espalda.
cards.exampleNative: I need a specialist for my back.
cards.remember: médico and doctor (doctor) mean the same.

cards.target: urgencias
cards.native: emergency room
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Dónde está urgencias? Es para mi esposa.
cards.exampleNative: Where is the emergency room? It's for my wife.
cards.remember: Look for the sign URGENCIAS (emergency room) at the hospital.

cards.target: la inyección · la vacuna
cards.native: injection, shot · vaccine
cards.exampleTarget: Necesita una inyección para el dolor.
cards.exampleNative: You need a shot for the pain.

cards.target: los análisis · la sangre
cards.native: lab tests · blood
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo que hacer unos análisis de sangre.
cards.exampleNative: I have to get some blood tests.
cards.remember: Labs are walk-in and fast. Some tests need you to come without eating (en ayunas).
cards.replyNative: Do I have to go fasting?

cards.target: ¿cada cuánto tomo…? · cada ocho horas
cards.native: how often do I take…? · every eight hours
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Cada cuánto tomo la pastilla? → Cada ocho horas.
cards.exampleNative: How often do I take the pill? → Every eight hours.
cards.remember: cada = every. cada día, cada semana (every day, every week).

cards.target: por cinco días · antes de comer · después de comer
cards.native: for five days · before meals · after meals
cards.exampleTarget: Una pastilla cada doce horas por cinco días, después de comer.
cards.exampleNative: One pill every twelve hours for five days, after meals.
cards.remember: por (for) + time = for how long.

cards.target: doler
cards.native: to hurt (me duele = it hurts me)
cards.exampleTarget: Me va a doler un poco.
cards.exampleNative: It's going to hurt a little.
cards.remember: -er verb. After tener que (have to), hay que (one has to) and para (to, in order to) it never changes.

cards.target:
doler · present
me duele (duelen) · te duele (duelen) · le duele (duelen) · nos duele (duelen) · les duele (duelen)
cards.native:
to hurt · present
it hurts me · it hurts you · it hurts him / her / you (form.) · it hurts us · it hurts them
cards.exampleTarget: Me duele la cabeza.
cards.exampleNative: My head hurts.
cards.remember: Works like gustar: the thing that hurts is the subject. One thing: duele; more than one: duelen.

cards.target: me levanto · te levantas · se levanta · nos levantamos · se levantan
cards.native: Reflexive verbs carry a pronoun that matches the subject: me, te, se, nos, se. It goes right before the verb.
cards.exampleTarget: Nos levantamos a las siete y los niños se levantan a las ocho.
cards.exampleNative: We get up at seven and the kids get up at eight.
cards.remember: In the dictionary the se is on the end: levantarse (to get up).
cards.meaning: I get up · you get up · he / she gets up · we get up · they get up
cards.replyNative: What time do you get up?

cards.target: antes de desayunar · después de comer
cards.native: After antes de, después de and other prepositions, use the -r form (infinitive), never -ndo.
cards.exampleTarget: Antes de dormir, leo un poco.
cards.exampleNative: Before sleeping, I read a little.
cards.remember: English says "before sleeping"; Spanish says antes de dormir.
cards.meaning: before having breakfast · after eating

cards.target: me despierto · me levanto
cards.native: I wake up · I get up
cards.exampleTarget: Me despierto a las seis, pero me levanto a las seis y media.
cards.exampleNative: I wake up at six, but I get up at six thirty.
cards.remember: despertarse = open your eyes; levantarse = get out of bed.
cards.replyTarget: ¿Y qué haces en esa media hora?
cards.replyNative: And what do you do in that half hour?

cards.target: ¿a qué hora te levantas? · me levanto a las siete
cards.native: what time do you get up? · I get up at seven
cards.exampleTarget: ¿A qué hora se levanta usted? → Me levanto temprano, a las siete.
cards.exampleNative: What time do you get up? → I get up early, at seven.
cards.replyNative: And what time do you go to bed?

cards.target: me baño · bañarse
cards.native: I shower · to shower, bathe
cards.exampleTarget: Me baño en la mañana.
cards.exampleNative: I shower in the morning.
cards.remember: In Mexico bañarse (to bathe) is the normal word for showering.

cards.target: me lavo los dientes · me lavo la cara · me lavo las manos
cards.native: I brush my teeth · I wash my face · I wash my hands
cards.exampleTarget: Me lavo los dientes después de desayunar.
cards.exampleNative: I brush my teeth after breakfast.
cards.remember: Spanish says "the teeth", not "my teeth".

cards.target: me visto · me pongo… · me cambio
cards.native: I get dressed · I put on… · I change (clothes)
cards.exampleTarget: Me visto y me pongo los zapatos.
cards.exampleNative: I get dressed and put on my shoes.
cards.remember: me visto (I get dressed) is from vestirse (to get dressed, (e → i).

cards.target: me arreglo
cards.native: I get ready (fix myself up)
cards.exampleTarget: Me arreglo para la fiesta.
cards.exampleNative: I'm getting ready for the party.
cards.remember: arreglarse = get ready; arreglar = fix something.

cards.target: me peino · me rasuro · me maquillo
cards.native: I comb my hair · I shave · I put on makeup
cards.exampleTarget: Luis se rasura y Ana se maquilla.
cards.exampleNative: Luis shaves and Ana puts on makeup.
cards.remember: rasurarse (to shave) is the Mexican word for shave.

cards.target: desayuno · como · ceno
cards.native: I have breakfast · I have lunch (the main meal) · I have dinner
cards.exampleTarget: Desayuno a las ocho, como a las tres y ceno poco.
cards.exampleNative: I have breakfast at eight, lunch at three and a light dinner.
cards.remember: In Mexico la comida (the main meal) is the big meal, around 2 to 4 p.m.
cards.replyNative: And what do you have for breakfast?

cards.target: voy al trabajo · regreso a casa
cards.native: I go to work · I come home
cards.exampleTarget: Voy al trabajo en camión y regreso a casa a las seis.
cards.exampleNative: I go to work by bus and come home at six.
cards.replyNative: How long does it take you?

cards.target: ya me voy · me voy
cards.native: I'm leaving now · I'm leaving, I'm off
cards.exampleTarget: ¡Ya me voy! Nos vemos en la noche.
cards.exampleNative: I'm leaving now! See you tonight.
cards.remember: me voy is from irse (to leave).

cards.target: se me hace tarde · llego tarde
cards.native: I'm running late · I arrive late
cards.exampleTarget: ¡Ay, se me hace tarde para el trabajo!
cards.exampleNative: Oh, I'm running late for work!
cards.remember: se me hace tarde (I'm running late) is a fixed phrase. Learn it whole.
cards.replyNative: Shall I give you a ride?

cards.target: me acuesto · me duermo
cards.native: I go to bed · I fall asleep
cards.exampleTarget: Me acuesto a las diez, pero me duermo a las once.
cards.exampleNative: I go to bed at ten, but I fall asleep at eleven.
cards.remember: acostarse = lie down; dormirse = drop off to sleep.

cards.target: me siento · siéntese
cards.native: I sit down · sit down (usted)
cards.exampleTarget: Me siento en la sala. → Siéntese, por favor.
cards.exampleNative: I sit in the living room. → Sit down, please.

cards.target: me siento (sentarse) · me siento (sentirse)
cards.native: I sit down · I feel
cards.exampleTarget: Me siento en la silla. · Hoy me siento bien.
cards.exampleNative: I sit on the chair. · Today I feel good.
cards.remember: Same words, two verbs. The rest of the sentence tells you which.

cards.target: me quedo en casa · quedarse
cards.native: I stay home · to stay
cards.exampleTarget: Hoy me quedo en casa. Estoy cansada.
cards.exampleNative: Today I'm staying home. I'm tired.
cards.remember: quedarse = stay. Without se, quedar (to fit, to agree) has other meanings (see unit 17).
cards.replyNative: Do you want to watch a movie?

cards.target: la rutina · un día normal
cards.native: routine · a normal day
cards.exampleTarget: En un día normal me levanto temprano.
cards.exampleNative: On a normal day I get up early.
cards.replyNative: What time do you get up?

cards.target: en la madrugada · madrugar
cards.native: in the early hours (after midnight) · to get up very early
cards.exampleTarget: Mi vecino llega en la madrugada.
cards.exampleNative: My neighbor gets home in the early hours.
cards.remember: madrugada (the small hours) is from midnight until dawn.

cards.target: la siesta · tomar una siesta
cards.native: nap · to take a nap
cards.exampleTarget: Después de comer tomo una siesta.
cards.exampleNative: After lunch I take a nap.

cards.target: el despertador · suena el despertador
cards.native: alarm clock · the alarm goes off
cards.exampleTarget: El despertador suena a las seis.
cards.exampleNative: The alarm goes off at six.
cards.remember: Many people just use la alarma del celular (the phone's alarm).

cards.target: la regadera
cards.native: shower (MX)
cards.exampleTarget: La regadera no tiene agua caliente.
cards.exampleNative: The shower has no hot water.
cards.remember: Mexico says regadera (shower); Spain says ducha.
cards.replyNative: Did you turn on the water heater?

cards.target: la toalla · el jabón · el champú
cards.native: towel · soap · shampoo
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Hay toallas limpias? Necesito jabón.
cards.exampleNative: Are there clean towels? I need soap.

cards.target: el cepillo de dientes · la pasta de dientes
cards.native: toothbrush · toothpaste
cards.exampleTarget: Necesito un cepillo de dientes nuevo.
cards.exampleNative: I need a new toothbrush.

cards.target: la pijama · hacer la cama
cards.native: pajamas · to make the bed
cards.exampleTarget: Me pongo la pijama y hago la cama.
cards.exampleNative: I put on my pajamas and make the bed.
cards.remember: In Mexico it's la pijama (pajamas, feminine).

cards.target: lavo el carro · me lavo las manos
cards.native: I wash the car · I wash my hands
cards.exampleTarget: Baño al perro y después me baño.
cards.exampleNative: I bathe the dog and then I shower.
cards.remember: Use me / te / se (myself, yourself, himself or herself) when you do the action to yourself; drop it when you do it to something else.
cards.replyNative: Will you help me bathe the dog?

cards.target: levantarse
cards.native: to get up
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo que levantarme temprano.
cards.exampleNative: I have to get up early.
cards.remember: -ar verb, reflexive. After tener que (have to) or para (to, in order to) the pronoun attaches and matches the person: tengo que levantarme, tienes que levantarte.

cards.target:
levantarse · present
yo me levanto · tú te levantas · él / ella / usted se levanta · nosotros nos levantamos · ellos / ustedes se levantan
cards.native:
to get up · present
I get up · you get up · he/she gets up / you (form.) get up · we get up · they / you all get up
cards.exampleTarget: Me levanto a las siete.
cards.exampleNative: I get up at seven.
cards.remember: Now, habits and facts.

cards.target: bañarse
cards.native: to take a shower · bathe
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo que bañarme antes de cenar.
cards.exampleNative: I have to shower before dinner.
