cards.target: voy a + infinitive
cards.native: ir a + infinitive = going to (do something). It's the most common way to talk about the future in Mexico.
cards.exampleTarget: Voy a comprar fruta. Vamos a viajar a Oaxaca.
cards.exampleNative: I'm going to buy fruit. We're going to travel to Oaxaca.
cards.remember: Conjugate only ir (to go): voy a, vas a, va a, vamos a, van a.
cards.meaning: I'm going to + verb

cards.target: más … que · menos … que
cards.native: Comparisons: more … than, less … than.
cards.exampleTarget: Mi hermano es más alto que yo. El hotel es menos caro que el otro.
cards.exampleNative: My brother is taller than me. The hotel is less expensive than the other one.
cards.remember: Seen: más despacio, slower (L1); más cercana, closer (L4).
cards.meaning: more … than · less … than
cards.replyNative: Then let's go to that one.

cards.target: mejor · peor · mayor · menor
cards.native: Irregular comparisons: better, worse, older, younger. No más with these.
cards.exampleTarget: Hoy estoy mejor. Mi hermana es mayor que yo.
cards.exampleNative: Today I'm better. My sister is older than me.
cards.remember: Seen in Lesson 4: ya está un poco mejor (he's a little better now).
cards.meaning: better · worse · older · younger

cards.target: para · por
cards.native: para = for (a person, a purpose, a deadline), in order to. por = through, around, by, because of, per.
cards.exampleTarget: Esto es para ti. Paso por el mercado. Llama por teléfono.
cards.exampleNative: This is for you. I'm stopping by the market. She calls by phone.
cards.remember: Fixed ones you know: por favor (please), por aquí (this way), por qué (why), ¿para qué? (what for?)
cards.meaning: for, in order to · for, by, through

cards.target: hace calor · hace frío · hace sol · hace viento
cards.native: Weather uses hacer: hace + noun. A person uses tener (tengo calor); the weather uses hacer.
cards.exampleTarget: Hoy hace mucho calor y hace sol.
cards.exampleNative: Today it's very hot and sunny.
cards.remember: tiempo also means weather: hace buen tiempo = the weather is nice.
cards.meaning: it's hot · it's cold · it's sunny · it's windy

cards.target: poquito · casita · perrito · ahorita
cards.native: -ito / -ita makes things small or affectionate. In Mexico ahorita means "right now" or "in a little while".
cards.exampleTarget: Un poquito, por favor. Tengo un perrito.
cards.exampleNative: Just a tiny bit, please. I have a little dog.
cards.remember: Seen in Lesson 4: un poquito (a little bit).
cards.meaning: a little bit · little house · little dog · right now

cards.group: Grammar: acabar de, volver a, tener ganas de
cards.target: acabar de + infinitive
cards.native: acabar de + infinitive = to have just done something. Use the present: acabo de…
cards.exampleTarget: Acabo de comer.
cards.exampleNative: I just ate.
cards.remember: acabar alone means to finish: Ya acabo.
cards.meaning: to have just + verb

cards.group: Grammar: acabar de, volver a, tener ganas de
cards.target: volver a + infinitive
cards.native: volver a + infinitive = to do something again.
cards.exampleTarget: Vuelvo a llamar mañana.
cards.exampleNative: I'll call again tomorrow.
cards.remember: More natural than adding otra vez (again).
cards.meaning: to + verb again

cards.group: Grammar: acabar de, volver a, tener ganas de
cards.target: tener ganas de + infinitive
cards.native: tener ganas de + infinitive = to feel like doing something.
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo ganas de ir a la playa.
cards.exampleNative: I feel like going to the beach.
cards.remember: tener (to have) changes; ganas (desire) never does.
cards.meaning: to feel like + verb-ing

cards.group: Grammar: acabar de, volver a, tener ganas de
cards.target: desde hace · vivo aquí desde hace dos años
cards.native: for (up to now) · I've lived here for two years
cards.exampleTarget: Estudio español desde hace un año.
cards.exampleNative: I've been studying Spanish for a year.
cards.remember: Spanish uses the present here, not "have lived". Don't mix it up with hace dos años = two years ago.

cards.target: para · hasta · desde
cards.native: for, in order to · until · from, since
cards.exampleTarget: Algo para la fiesta. Tenemos que trabajar hasta las seis.
cards.exampleNative: Something for the party. We have to work until six.
cards.remember: A verb after para (to, in order to) stays in its base form.
cards.replyNative: And what time do you start tomorrow?

cards.target: tan … como
cards.native: as … as
cards.exampleTarget: Soy tan alto como mi papá.
cards.exampleNative: I'm as tall as my dad.

cards.target: el / la más … de
cards.native: the most … in / of (superlative)
cards.exampleTarget: Es la persona más agradable de la clase.
cards.exampleNative: She's the nicest person in the class.
cards.remember: Seen in Lesson 3.

cards.target: el mismo · la misma
cards.native: the same
cards.exampleTarget: Tenemos el mismo carro. Al mismo tiempo.
cards.exampleNative: We have the same car. At the same time.
cards.remember: Seen in Lesson 5: al mismo tiempo (at the same time).

cards.target: está nublado · llueve
cards.native: it's cloudy · it's raining
cards.exampleTarget: Hoy está nublado y mañana llueve.
cards.exampleNative: Today it's cloudy and tomorrow it rains.
cards.remember: From llover (to rain, (o → ue).

cards.target: padrísimo · muchísimo · riquísimo
cards.native: -ísimo / -ísima = extremely, very very.
cards.exampleTarget: Los tacos están riquísimos. Gracias, muchísimas gracias.
cards.exampleNative: The tacos are super tasty. Thanks, thank you so much.
cards.remember: Seen in Lesson 4: padrísim@ (really cool).
cards.replyNative: You're welcome, do you want another one?

cards.target: hasta luego · hasta pronto · luego · pronto
cards.native: luego = later, then; pronto = soon.
cards.exampleTarget: Primero como y luego estudio. Nos vemos pronto.
cards.exampleNative: First I eat and then I study. See you soon.
cards.remember: Seen in Lesson 1.

cards.group: Grammar: acabar de, volver a, tener ganas de
cards.target: acabo de llegar · acaba de salir · acabamos de comer
cards.native: I just arrived · he / she just left · we just ate
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Está Luis? → No, acaba de salir.
cards.exampleNative: Is Luis there? → No, he just left.
cards.replyNative: Can you tell him to call me?

cards.group: Grammar: acabar de, volver a, tener ganas de
cards.target: volver a llamar · volver a empezar · volver a intentar
cards.native: to call again · to start over · to try again
cards.exampleTarget: No contesta. Voy a volver a llamar.
cards.exampleNative: No answer. I'm going to call again.
cards.replyNative: I'd better send him a message.

cards.group: Grammar: acabar de, volver a, tener ganas de
cards.target: vuelvo a casa · vuelvo a llamar
cards.native: I go back home · I call again
cards.exampleTarget: Vuelvo a casa a las seis y vuelvo a llamar a Ana.
cards.exampleNative: I go back home at six and call Ana again.
cards.remember: volver a + place = return; volver a + verb = again.

cards.group: Grammar: acabar de, volver a, tener ganas de
cards.target: no tengo ganas · tengo muchas ganas de… · ¡qué ganas!
cards.native: I don't feel like it · I really want to… · I can't wait!
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo muchas ganas de ver a mi hijo. ¡Qué ganas!
cards.exampleNative: I really want to see my son. I can't wait!

cards.group: Grammar: acabar de, volver a, tener ganas de
cards.target: dentro de · dentro de una hora
cards.native: in (time from now) · in an hour
cards.exampleTarget: Nos vemos dentro de una hora.
cards.exampleNative: See you in an hour.
cards.remember: en una hora (in an hour) also works in Mexico.

cards.group: Grammar: acabar de, volver a, tener ganas de
cards.target: ¿desde cuándo…? · ¿cuánto tiempo hace que…?
cards.native: since when…? · how long have you…?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Desde cuándo vives en Puerto Vallarta?
cards.exampleNative: How long have you lived in Puerto Vallarta?
cards.remember: Answer with desde hace: desde hace tres años (for three years).

cards.target: el fin de semana · este fin de semana
cards.native: the weekend · this weekend
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Qué vas a hacer este fin de semana?
cards.exampleNative: What are you going to do this weekend?
cards.replyNative: I'm going to the beach. Want to come?

cards.target: el tiempo libre · el pasatiempo
cards.native: free time · hobby
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Qué haces en tu tiempo libre? → Mi pasatiempo es leer.
cards.exampleNative: What do you do in your free time? → My hobby is reading.
cards.remember: You'll also hear el hobby.

cards.target: nadar · pescar · bailar
cards.native: to swim · to fish · to dance
cards.exampleTarget: Los domingos pescamos y en la noche bailamos.
cards.exampleNative: On Sundays we fish and at night we dance.

cards.target: el gimnasio · hacer ejercicio
cards.native: gym · to exercise
cards.exampleTarget: Voy al gimnasio tres veces a la semana.
cards.exampleNative: I go to the gym three times a week.
cards.remember: Many Mexicans just say el gym.

cards.target: el cine · ir al cine
cards.native: movie theater · to go to the movies
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Vamos al cine el viernes?
cards.exampleNative: Shall we go to the movies on Friday?
cards.remember: una película (a movie) is the film itself.
cards.replyNative: What movie do you want to see?

cards.target: el partido · el equipo · ¿quién gana?
cards.native: game, match · team · who's winning?
cards.exampleTarget: Hoy hay partido. ¿Quién gana?
cards.exampleNative: There's a game today. Who's winning?

cards.target: el futbol · el futbol americano · el beisbol
cards.native: soccer · football · baseball
cards.exampleTarget: Mi vecino ve el futbol todos los domingos.
cards.exampleNative: My neighbor watches soccer every Sunday.
cards.remember: In Mexico futbol (soccer) has no accent.
cards.replyNative: And which team does he root for?

cards.target: jugar futbol · tocar la guitarra
cards.native: to play soccer · to play the guitar
cards.exampleTarget: Luis juega futbol y toca la guitarra.
cards.exampleNative: Luis plays soccer and plays the guitar.
cards.remember: jugar (to play) for games and sports; tocar (to play, to touch) for instruments. Mexicans often drop the al: jugar futbol (play soccer).
cards.replyNative: And you, do you play anything?

cards.target: el billar · las cartas · el dominó
cards.native: pool (billiards) · cards · dominoes
cards.exampleTarget: Los viernes jugamos dominó en el bar.
cards.exampleNative: On Fridays we play dominoes at the bar.

cards.target: el malecón · dar una vuelta
cards.native: seafront boardwalk · to go for a stroll
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Damos una vuelta por el malecón?
cards.exampleNative: Shall we take a stroll on the boardwalk?
cards.replyNative: Yes, and then an ice cream.

cards.target: tomar el sol · la sombra
cards.native: to sunbathe · shade
cards.exampleTarget: Ella toma el sol y yo estoy en la sombra.
cards.exampleNative: She sunbathes and I'm in the shade.

cards.target: andar en bici · hacer yoga
cards.native: to ride a bike · to do yoga
cards.exampleTarget: En la mañana ando en bici y hago yoga.
cards.exampleNative: In the morning I ride my bike and do yoga.
cards.remember: bici (bike) is short for bicicleta (bicycle).

cards.target: ir de excursión · la caminata
cards.native: to go on an outing, a hike · hike, walk
cards.exampleTarget: Vamos a ir de excursión a la montaña.
cards.exampleNative: We're going on a hike in the mountains.

cards.target: salir con amigos · salir a cenar
cards.native: to go out with friends · to go out to dinner
cards.exampleTarget: Los sábados salimos a cenar.
cards.exampleNative: On Saturdays we go out to dinner.

cards.target: la música en vivo
cards.native: live music
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Hay música en vivo en el bar?
cards.exampleNative: Is there live music at the bar?

cards.target: me encanta · no me gusta nada
cards.native: I love it · I don't like it at all
cards.exampleTarget: Me encanta bailar, pero no me gusta nada correr.
cards.exampleNative: I love dancing, but I don't like running at all.
cards.remember: encantar (to delight) works like gustar (to please): me encantan los tacos (I love tacos).
cards.replyNative: Will you teach me to dance salsa?

cards.target: ¿tienes planes? · ¿qué vas a hacer…?
cards.native: do you have plans? · what are you going to do…?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Tienes planes el sábado?
cards.exampleNative: Do you have plans on Saturday?
cards.replyNative: Do you want to go to the boardwalk?

cards.target: ¿quieres ir…? · ¿quieres venir?
cards.native: do you want to go…? · do you want to come?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Quieres ir al cine conmigo?
cards.exampleNative: Do you want to go to the movies with me?
cards.replyNative: Which movie do you want to see?

cards.target: ¿te gustaría…? · ¿le gustaría…?
cards.native: would you like to…? (tú · usted)
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Te gustaría ir a la playa el domingo?
cards.exampleNative: Would you like to go to the beach on Sunday?
cards.remember: Learn it as a fixed phrase; the "would" form comes in unit 23.
cards.replyTarget: Llevo la comida y tú las bebidas.
cards.replyNative: I'll bring the food and you bring the drinks.

cards.target: ¡va! · ¡me late!
cards.native: deal! · I'm in! (casual MX)
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Vamos por unos tacos? → ¡Va!
cards.exampleNative: Shall we go get tacos? → Deal!
cards.remember: Friends only. With usted, say ¡claro! (of course!) or con gusto (gladly).

cards.target: ¿a qué hora nos vemos? · ¿dónde nos vemos?
cards.native: what time shall we meet? · where shall we meet?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿A qué hora nos vemos? → A las ocho en la plaza.
cards.exampleNative: What time shall we meet? → At eight in the plaza.
cards.replyTarget: Perfecto. Te mando un mensaje cuando llegue.
cards.replyNative: Perfect. I'll text you when I get there.

cards.target: ¿paso por ti? · paso por ti a las ocho
cards.native: shall I pick you up? · I'll pick you up at eight
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Paso por ti o nos vemos allá?
cards.exampleNative: Shall I pick you up or shall we meet there?
cards.remember: pasar por = to pick someone up.
cards.replyTarget: Sí, por favor. Te espero afuera.
cards.replyNative: Yes, please. I'll wait for you outside.

cards.target: quedamos a las ocho · quedamos de vernos
cards.native: we're meeting at eight (it's agreed) · we agreed to meet
cards.exampleTarget: Quedamos de vernos en el café.
cards.exampleNative: We agreed to meet at the cafe.
cards.remember: quedar de (to agree to) + infinitive is Mexican. Spain says quedar en.

cards.target: no puedo · otro día · ¿qué tal otro día?
cards.native: I can't · another day · how about another day?
cards.exampleTarget: Hoy no puedo. ¿Qué tal otro día?
cards.exampleNative: I can't today. How about another day?

cards.target: ya tengo planes · tal vez la próxima
cards.native: I already have plans · maybe next time
cards.exampleTarget: Gracias, pero ya tengo planes. Tal vez la próxima.
cards.exampleNative: Thanks, but I already have plans. Maybe next time.
cards.remember: A polite no.

cards.target: te invito · yo invito
cards.native: my treat · I'm paying
cards.exampleTarget: Vamos por un café. Yo invito.
cards.exampleNative: Let's go get a coffee. My treat.
cards.remember: invitar means to invite and also to pay for someone.
cards.replyNative: Thanks. Next time it's on me.

cards.target: ir por un café · ir por unas cervezas
cards.native: to go get a coffee · to go get some beers
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Vamos por un café después de la clase?
cards.exampleNative: Shall we go get a coffee after class?
cards.remember: ir por = to go get.
cards.replyNative: I know a really good place.

cards.target: una carne asada
cards.native: a cookout (MX)
cards.exampleTarget: El domingo hay carne asada en casa de Marco.
cards.exampleNative: On Sunday there's a cookout at Marco's house.
cards.remember: Means grilled beef and also the party around it.

cards.target: pasarla bien · ¡que te diviertas!
cards.native: to have a good time · have fun!
cards.exampleTarget: Vamos a pasarla bien. → ¡Que te diviertas!
cards.exampleNative: We're going to have a good time. → Have fun!
cards.remember: que te diviertas (have fun) is a fixed wish form.
cards.replyNative: Thanks, I'll tell you about it tomorrow.

cards.target: la renta · rentar
cards.native: rent · to rent
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Cuánto es la renta del departamento?
cards.exampleNative: How much is the rent for the apartment?
cards.remember: Mexico says renta (rent); Spain says alquiler.
cards.replyNative: Does it include electricity and water?

cards.target: el departamento · amueblado
cards.native: apartment · furnished
cards.exampleTarget: Rentamos un departamento amueblado.
cards.exampleNative: We rent a furnished apartment.
cards.remember: Often shortened to el depa (the apartment).
cards.replyNative: How many bedrooms does it have?

cards.target: el casero · la casera
cards.native: landlord · landlady
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo que hablar con la casera.
cards.exampleNative: I have to talk to the landlady.
cards.remember: el dueño / la dueña (owner) is used the same way.

cards.target: el depósito · un mes de depósito
cards.native: security deposit · one month's deposit
cards.exampleTarget: Piden un mes de renta y un mes de depósito.
cards.exampleNative: They ask for one month's rent and one month's deposit.
cards.remember: depósito (deposit) is also a bank deposit (unit 19).
cards.replyNative: Do I get the deposit back at the end?

cards.target: el contrato · firmar
cards.native: lease, contract · to sign
cards.exampleTarget: El contrato es por un año. ¿Dónde firmo?
cards.exampleNative: The lease is for one year. Where do I sign?

cards.target: los servicios · ¿incluye los servicios?
cards.native: utilities · does it include utilities?
cards.exampleTarget: La renta no incluye los servicios.
cards.exampleNative: The rent doesn't include utilities.
cards.replyTarget: ¿Cuánto se paga de luz más o menos?
cards.replyNative: About how much is the electric bill?

cards.target: la luz · se fue la luz
cards.native: electricity, power · the power went out
cards.exampleTarget: Se fue la luz otra vez.
cards.exampleNative: The power went out again.
cards.remember: la luz (the light) is light and electric power. se fue la luz (the power went out) is a fixed phrase.

cards.target: el agua caliente · no hay agua
cards.native: hot water · there's no water
cards.exampleTarget: No hay agua caliente en la regadera.
cards.exampleNative: There's no hot water in the shower.
cards.remember: agua (water) is feminine but takes el.
cards.replyNative: Did you check the water heater yet?

cards.target: el gas · el tanque de gas · el gasero
cards.native: gas · gas tank · gas delivery man
cards.exampleTarget: Se acaba el gas. Hay que llamar al gasero.
cards.exampleNative: The gas is running out. We need to call the gas man.
cards.remember: In Mexico gas trucks come by playing a jingle.

cards.target: el internet · la señal · el módem
cards.native: internet · signal · modem
cards.exampleTarget: No hay internet. ¿Está prendido el módem?
cards.exampleNative: There's no internet. Is the modem on?
cards.replyTarget: Lo apago y lo prendo otra vez.
cards.replyNative: I'll turn it off and on again.

cards.target: la contraseña del wifi · ¿cuál es la contraseña?
cards.native: wifi password · what's the password?
cards.exampleTarget: Disculpe, ¿cuál es la contraseña del wifi?
cards.exampleNative: Excuse me, what's the wifi password?
cards.remember: In Mexico wifi sounds like "wai-fai".
cards.replyNative: Can you write it down for me?

cards.target: el recibo de luz · el recibo del agua
cards.native: electric bill · water bill
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo que pagar el recibo de luz.
cards.exampleNative: I have to pay the electric bill.
cards.remember: recibo is the utility bill; la cuenta is the restaurant check.

cards.target: el aire acondicionado · el clima
cards.native: air conditioning · air conditioning (MX)
cards.exampleTarget: El clima del cuarto no enfría.
cards.exampleNative: The bedroom A/C isn't cooling.
cards.remember: On the coast many people call the A/C unit el clima.
cards.replyNative: We have to call the repair technician.

cards.target: el ventilador · el ventilador de techo
cards.native: fan · ceiling fan
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Puedes prender el ventilador?
cards.exampleNative: Can you turn on the fan?

cards.target: prender / apagar
cards.native: to turn on / to turn off
cards.exampleTarget: Prendo la luz y apago la tele.
cards.exampleNative: I turn on the light and turn off the TV.
cards.remember: prender (to turn on) is the Mexican word; encender sounds formal.

cards.target: la basura · sacar la basura · el camión de la basura
cards.native: trash · to take out the trash · garbage truck
cards.exampleTarget: El camión de la basura pasa los martes.
cards.exampleNative: The garbage truck comes by on Tuesdays.

cards.target: no funciona · no sirve
cards.native: it doesn't work · it doesn't work (MX)
cards.exampleTarget: El refri no sirve.
cards.exampleNative: The fridge doesn't work.
cards.remember: no sirve (it doesn't work) is the everyday Mexican way to say it.
cards.replyNative: Can you send someone to fix it?

cards.target: está descompuest@ · está rot@
cards.native: it's broken (not working) · it's broken (cracked, torn)
cards.exampleTarget: La lavadora está descompuesta y la ventana está rota.
cards.exampleNative: The washer is broken and the window is broken.
cards.remember: descompuesto (broken down) for machines that stop working; roto (broken) for things physically broken.

cards.target: hay una fuga · gotea
cards.native: there's a leak · it drips
cards.exampleTarget: Hay una fuga de agua en el baño. La llave gotea.
cards.exampleNative: There's a water leak in the bathroom. The faucet drips.
cards.remember: una fuga de gas (a gas leak) is an emergency: leave and call for help.
cards.replyNative: Where do you turn off the water?

cards.target: el plomero · el electricista · el técnico · el cerrajero
cards.native: plumber · electrician · repair technician · locksmith
cards.exampleTarget: Necesito un plomero. ¿Conoce uno?
cards.exampleNative: I need a plumber. Do you know one?
cards.remember: el técnico (the repair person) fixes A/C units and appliances.
cards.replyNative: Yes, I'll give you his number.

cards.target: arreglar · ¿lo puede arreglar? · ¿cuándo puede venir?
cards.native: to fix · can you fix it? · when can you come?
cards.exampleTarget: El clima no sirve. ¿Cuándo puede venir a arreglarlo?
cards.exampleNative: The A/C doesn't work. When can you come fix it?
cards.replyNative: How much are you going to charge me?

cards.target: la llave (faucet) · la llave (key)
cards.native: faucet, tap · key
cards.exampleTarget: Hay que cerrar la llave del agua. · ¿Dónde está la llave de la casa?
cards.exampleNative: You have to turn off the faucet. · Where's the house key?
cards.remember: One word, two meanings in Mexico. Context makes it clear.

cards.target: el garrafón · el agua de garrafón
cards.native: 5-gallon water jug · bottled jug water
cards.exampleTarget: Necesitamos dos garrafones para la semana.
cards.exampleNative: We need two water jugs for the week.
cards.remember: Tap water isn't for drinking; jugs are delivered to your door.
cards.replyNative: What time does the water truck come?

cards.target: la señora de la limpieza · limpiar
cards.native: the cleaning lady · to clean
cards.exampleTarget: La señora de la limpieza viene los jueves.
cards.exampleNative: The cleaning lady comes on Thursdays.
cards.remember: Most people simply call her by name or la señora (the lady).
cards.replyNative: How much do you pay her?

cards.target: la lavadora · la secadora · el tendedero
cards.native: washing machine · dryer · clothesline
cards.exampleTarget: No tenemos secadora; usamos el tendedero.
cards.exampleNative: We don't have a dryer; we use the clothesline.
cards.replyTarget: Con este sol se seca rápido.
cards.replyNative: In this sun it dries fast.

cards.target: la estufa · el horno · el microondas
cards.native: stove · oven · microwave
cards.exampleTarget: La estufa es de gas.
cards.exampleNative: The stove runs on gas.

cards.target: el foco · el contacto · el cable
cards.native: light bulb · outlet · cord
cards.exampleTarget: El foco no sirve y el contacto no tiene luz.
cards.exampleNative: The bulb doesn't work and the outlet has no power.
cards.remember: foco (light bulb) and contacto (outlet) are the Mexican words.
cards.replyNative: We have to call the electrician.

cards.target: el tinaco · la cisterna
cards.native: rooftop water tank · underground water tank
cards.exampleTarget: No hay agua en el tinaco.
cards.exampleNative: There's no water in the rooftop tank.
cards.remember: Most Mexican homes store water in these.
cards.replyNative: Shall we turn on the pump?

cards.target: los mosquitos · las cucarachas · fumigar
cards.native: mosquitoes · cockroaches · to spray for bugs
cards.exampleTarget: Hay muchos mosquitos. Hay que fumigar.
cards.exampleNative: There are a lot of mosquitoes. We need to spray.
cards.replyNative: Do you know someone who sprays?

cards.target: la humedad · el moho
cards.native: humidity, damp · mold
cards.exampleTarget: Por la humedad hay moho en el clóset.
cards.exampleNative: Because of the humidity there's mold in the closet.
cards.replyTarget: Hay que dejar la puerta abierta.
cards.replyNative: We have to leave the door open.

cards.target: el portón · el timbre · tocar el timbre
cards.native: front gate · doorbell · to ring the bell
cards.exampleTarget: Hay que tocar el timbre del portón.
cards.exampleNative: You have to ring the gate bell.

cards.target: la cuota de mantenimiento
cards.native: maintenance fee (condo or HOA)
cards.exampleTarget: La cuota de mantenimiento es de mil pesos al mes.
cards.exampleNative: The maintenance fee is a thousand pesos a month.

cards.target: ¿bueno?
cards.native: hello? (answering the phone, MX)
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Bueno? → Hola, ¿está Ana?
cards.exampleNative: Hello? → Hi, is Ana there?
cards.remember: Only Mexico answers with bueno (hello). Other countries say ¿aló? or ¿diga?

cards.target: ¿de parte de quién? · de parte de…
cards.native: who's calling? · this is… (calling for)
cards.exampleTarget: ¿De parte de quién? → De parte de Marco.
cards.exampleNative: Who's calling? → This is Marco.

cards.target: ¿se encuentra…? · no se encuentra
cards.native: is … there? · he / she isn't in
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Se encuentra la doctora? → No se encuentra.
cards.exampleNative: Is the doctor in? → She's not in.
cards.remember: Polite phone and office phrase.
cards.replyNative: Can I leave her a message?

cards.target: número equivocado
cards.native: wrong number
cards.exampleTarget: Perdón, tiene el número equivocado.
cards.exampleNative: Sorry, you have the wrong number.

cards.target: el mensaje · el recado · dejar un recado
cards.native: message · message (MX) · to leave a message
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Le puedo dejar un recado?
cards.exampleNative: Can I leave him a message?
cards.remember: recado (message) for a spoken message passed on by someone.

cards.target: mandar un WhatsApp · mándame un mensaje
cards.native: to send a WhatsApp · send me a message
cards.exampleTarget: Te mando un WhatsApp con la dirección.
cards.exampleNative: I'll send you a WhatsApp with the address.
cards.remember: Many people just say mándame un whats (send me a WhatsApp).

cards.target: marcar · te marco
cards.native: to dial, to call · I'll call you
cards.exampleTarget: Te marco en la tarde.
cards.exampleNative: I'll call you in the afternoon.
cards.remember: In Mexico marcar (to dial) often replaces llamar (to call).

cards.target: ¿me da su número? · ¿me pasas tu número?
cards.native: can I have your number? (usted) · can you give me your number? (tú)
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Me pasas tu número? Te mando un mensaje.
cards.exampleNative: Can you give me your number? I'll send you a message.
cards.replyTarget: Te marco ahorita para que tengas el mío.
cards.replyNative: I'll call you now so you have mine.

cards.target: la lada · el número de celular
cards.native: area code (MX) · cell number
cards.exampleTarget: La lada de Puerto Vallarta es 322.
cards.exampleNative: Puerto Vallarta's area code is 322.

cards.target: no se oye · se cortó
cards.native: I can't hear you · it cut off
cards.exampleTarget: No se oye bien. Creo que se cortó.
cards.exampleNative: I can't hear well. I think it cut off.
cards.remember: se cortó (it got cut off) is a past form; learn it as a phrase for now.

cards.target: la recarga · hacer una recarga
cards.native: phone credit top-up · to top up
cards.exampleTarget: Voy a hacer una recarga de cien pesos.
cards.exampleNative: I'm going to top up a hundred pesos.
cards.remember: You can top up at any convenience store.

cards.target: hacer una cita · tengo cita
cards.native: to make an appointment · I have an appointment
cards.exampleTarget: Quiero hacer una cita con el dentista.
cards.exampleNative: I want to make an appointment with the dentist.
cards.remember: Mexicans often drop the una (an): tengo cita (I have an appointment).
cards.replyNative: What days do you have available?

cards.target: cambiar la cita · cancelar la cita
cards.native: to change the appointment · to cancel the appointment
cards.exampleTarget: Necesito cambiar mi cita del lunes.
cards.exampleNative: I need to change my Monday appointment.
cards.replyNative: Do you have anything on Friday?

cards.target: ¿a qué hora le queda bien? · ¿qué día le queda bien?
cards.native: what time works for you? · what day works for you?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Qué día le queda bien? → El jueves.
cards.exampleNative: What day works for you? → Thursday.
cards.remember: le (to you) for usted, te for tú.
cards.replyTarget: En la mañana, si se puede.

cards.target: me queda bien · no me queda bien
cards.native: that works for me · that doesn't work for me
cards.exampleTarget: El martes no me queda bien. ¿El miércoles?
cards.exampleNative: Tuesday doesn't work for me. Wednesday?
cards.remember: Also used for clothes: the shirt fits me.
cards.replyTarget: El miércoles a las diez sí puedo.
cards.replyNative: Wednesday at ten I can do.

cards.target: confirmar la cita · llegar a tiempo
cards.native: to confirm the appointment · to arrive on time
cards.exampleTarget: Llamo para confirmar mi cita de mañana.
cards.exampleNative: I'm calling to confirm my appointment for tomorrow.
cards.replyNative: Do I need to bring anything?

cards.target: ¿me puede comunicar con…?
cards.native: can you put me through to…?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Me puede comunicar con el gerente?
cards.exampleNative: Can you put me through to the manager?

cards.target: el correo · la arroba
cards.native: email · @ sign
cards.exampleTarget: Mi correo es ana arroba gmail punto com.
cards.exampleNative: My email is ana at gmail dot com.
cards.remember: punto = dot.
cards.replyNative: I'll send you the photo now.

cards.target: el cajero automático · el cajero
cards.native: ATM · ATM (short)
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Hay un cajero por aquí?
cards.exampleNative: Is there an ATM around here?
cards.remember: el cajero (the ATM) is also the cashier. Context tells.

cards.target: sacar dinero · retirar
cards.native: to take out money · to withdraw
cards.exampleTarget: Voy a sacar dinero del cajero.
cards.exampleNative: I'm going to take money out of the ATM.
cards.remember: sacar (to take out) is the everyday word; retirar (to withdraw) is on the screen.

cards.target: depositar · el depósito
cards.native: to deposit · deposit
cards.exampleTarget: Deposito el cheque en el banco.
cards.exampleNative: I deposit the check at the bank.
cards.replyNative: When does the money show up?

cards.target: la transferencia · hacer una transferencia
cards.native: bank transfer · to make a transfer
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Le hago una transferencia o le pago en efectivo?
cards.exampleNative: Shall I send you a transfer or pay in cash?
cards.remember: Transfers are very common in Mexico, even for small payments.
cards.replyTarget: Transferencia, por favor. Le paso la cuenta.
cards.replyNative: A transfer, please. I'll give you the account number.

cards.target: el saldo · consultar el saldo
cards.native: balance · to check the balance
cards.exampleTarget: Quiero consultar mi saldo.
cards.exampleNative: I want to check my balance.
cards.remember: saldo (balance) is also prepaid phone credit.

cards.target: la comisión · ¿cobra comisión?
cards.native: fee, commission · do you charge a fee?
cards.exampleTarget: Este cajero cobra comisión.
cards.exampleNative: This ATM charges a fee.

cards.target: el tipo de cambio · ¿a cómo está el dólar?
cards.native: exchange rate · what's the dollar at?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿A cómo está el dólar hoy?
cards.exampleNative: What's the dollar at today?
cards.remember: ¿a cómo está…? (how much is…?) is how Mexicans ask any going rate.
cards.replyNative: I want to change a hundred dollars.

cards.target: cambiar dólares · la casa de cambio
cards.native: to change dollars · currency exchange office
cards.exampleTarget: Cambio dólares en la casa de cambio.
cards.exampleNative: I change dollars at the exchange office.

cards.target: pesos / dólares · ¿en pesos o en dólares?
cards.native: pesos / dollars · in pesos or in dollars?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Pago en pesos o en dólares? → En pesos, por favor.
cards.exampleNative: Do I pay in pesos or dollars? → In pesos, please.
cards.remember: Paying in pesos almost always gets you a better rate.
cards.replyNative: Can you give me the total in pesos?

cards.target: pagar el recibo · pagar la luz
cards.native: to pay the bill · to pay the electric bill
cards.exampleTarget: Mañana pago la luz y el agua.
cards.exampleNative: Tomorrow I pay the electricity and water.
cards.remember: Mexicans say pagar la luz (pay the light) for paying the power bill.
cards.replyNative: Can you pay it at the Oxxo?

cards.target: el OXXO · pagar en el OXXO
cards.native: convenience store · to pay at the store
cards.exampleTarget: Pago el recibo de luz en el OXXO.
cards.exampleNative: I pay the electric bill at the convenience store.
cards.remember: You can pay many bills, top up phones and send money there.
cards.replyNative: And do they charge a fee?

cards.target: la tarjeta de débito · la tarjeta de crédito
cards.native: debit card · credit card
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Es con tarjeta de débito o de crédito?
cards.exampleNative: Is it with a debit or credit card?
cards.remember: At the register you'll hear: ¿débito o crédito? (debit or credit?)

cards.target: la cuenta (bank) · la cuenta (check)
cards.native: bank account · the check, the bill
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo una cuenta en el banco. · La cuenta, por favor.
cards.exampleNative: I have a bank account. · The check, please.
cards.remember: Same word, two meanings. Context makes it clear.

cards.target: abrir una cuenta · el estado de cuenta
cards.native: to open an account · bank statement
cards.exampleTarget: Quiero abrir una cuenta. ¿Qué necesito?
cards.exampleNative: I want to open an account. What do I need?
cards.replyTarget: Su identificación y un comprobante de domicilio.
cards.replyNative: Your ID and proof of address.

cards.target: el NIP
cards.native: PIN (MX)
cards.exampleTarget: El cajero pide el NIP.
cards.exampleNative: The ATM asks for the PIN.
cards.remember: Mexico says NIP (the card's PIN), not PIN.

cards.target: no pasa la tarjeta · ¿la paso otra vez?
cards.native: the card isn't going through · shall I try it again?
cards.exampleTarget: No pasa la tarjeta. ¿Tiene otra?
cards.exampleNative: The card isn't going through. Do you have another one?

cards.target: solo efectivo · ¿aceptan tarjeta?
cards.native: cash only · do you take cards?
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Aceptan tarjeta? → No, solo efectivo.
cards.exampleNative: Do you take cards? → No, cash only.

cards.target: ¿tiene cambio de quinientos? · no traigo cambio
cards.native: do you have change for 500? · I don't have change on me
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Tiene cambio de quinientos? No traigo billetes chicos.
cards.exampleNative: Do you have change for 500? I don't have small bills.
cards.remember: Small shops and taxis often can't break big bills.
cards.replyTarget: Ahorita busco cambio en la tienda.
cards.replyNative: I'll get change at the store right now.

cards.target: las monedas · la feria
cards.native: coins · small change (casual MX)
cards.exampleTarget: No tengo feria, solo billetes.
cards.exampleNative: I don't have change, just bills.
cards.replyTarget: No se preocupe, luego me paga.

cards.target: a meses sin intereses
cards.native: in monthly payments with no interest
cards.exampleTarget: Puede pagar a seis meses sin intereses.
cards.exampleNative: You can pay in six monthly installments with no interest.
cards.remember: Common offer on credit card purchases in Mexico.

cards.target: la sucursal · el ejecutivo
cards.native: bank branch · bank representative
cards.exampleTarget: Tiene que ir a la sucursal y hablar con un ejecutivo.
cards.exampleNative: You have to go to the branch and talk to a representative.

cards.target: gastar / ahorrar
cards.native: to spend / to save
cards.exampleTarget: Gastamos poco y ahorramos un poco cada mes.
cards.exampleNative: We spend little and save a bit every month.

cards.target: trabajé · trabajaste · trabajó · trabajamos · trabajaron
cards.native: Preterite of -ar verbs: é, aste, ó, amos, aron. Used for finished actions at a set time.
cards.exampleTarget: Ayer trabajé hasta las seis.
cards.exampleNative: Yesterday I worked until six.
cards.remember: nosotros (we) looks like the present (trabajamos, we work); context tells you.
cards.meaning: I worked · you worked · he / she worked · we worked · they worked

cards.target: comí · comiste · comió · comimos · comieron
cards.native: Preterite of -er and -ir verbs share the same endings: í, iste, ió, imos, ieron.
cards.exampleTarget: Anoche comimos tacos y bebimos café.
cards.exampleNative: Last night we ate tacos and drank coffee.
cards.meaning: I ate · you ate · he / she ate · we ate · they ate

cards.target: hablo · habló
cards.native: The accent changes the meaning and the tense: hablo = I speak; habló = he/she spoke.
cards.exampleTarget: Hoy hablo con Ana. Ayer Ana habló con su mamá.
cards.exampleNative: Today I'm talking with Ana. Yesterday Ana talked with her mom.
cards.meaning: I speak · he / she spoke
cards.replyNative: And what did she tell her?

cards.target: llegué · pagué
cards.native: Spelling change in the yo form: -gar → -gué, -car → -qué, -zar → -cé. It keeps the sound.
cards.exampleTarget: Llegué tarde y pagué la cuenta.
cards.exampleNative: I arrived late and paid the bill.
cards.remember: Only the yo form changes.
cards.meaning: I arrived · I paid

cards.target: leyó · creyó · leyeron
cards.native: When the stem ends in a vowel, ió → yó and ieron → yeron.
cards.exampleTarget: Mi hija leyó el libro en dos días.
cards.exampleNative: My daughter read the book in two days.
cards.meaning: he / she read · he / she believed · they read

cards.target: tuve · estuve · pude · supe
cards.native: Irregular u-stem group: endings e, iste, o, imos, ieron with no accents.
cards.exampleTarget: Ayer tuve una cita y estuve en el hospital.
cards.exampleNative: Yesterday I had an appointment and was at the hospital.
cards.meaning: I had · I was · I could, I managed to · I found out

cards.target: hice · hizo · dije · dijeron · traje · trajeron
cards.native: More irregular stems: hic- (hizo with z), dij-, traj-. The j-stems end in -eron, not -ieron.
cards.exampleTarget: Ella hizo la cena y dijo que sí.
cards.exampleNative: She made dinner and said yes.
cards.meaning: I did · he / she did · I said · they said · I brought · they brought
cards.replyNative: What did she make for dinner?

cards.target: sintió · sintieron
cards.native: -ir verbs with a stem change in the present change e → i (o → u) only in the él and ellos preterite forms.
cards.exampleTarget: Ella sintió frío y ellos sintieron miedo.
cards.exampleNative: She felt cold and they felt afraid.
cards.remember: Later: pidió (asked for), durmió (slept).
cards.meaning: he / she felt · they felt

cards.target: supe · conocí · pude · no pude
cards.native: Some verbs shift meaning in the preterite: supe = I found out; conocí = I met; pude = I managed; no pude = I failed to.
cards.exampleTarget: Conocí a mi maestra el jueves.
cards.exampleNative: I met my teacher on Thursday.
cards.meaning: I found out · I met · I managed to · I couldn't (and didn't)

cards.target: de repente · al final
cards.native: suddenly · at the end, finally
cards.exampleTarget: De repente, hay un ruido afuera. Al final, todo está bien.
cards.exampleNative: Suddenly there's a noise outside. In the end, everything is fine.

cards.target: toda la mañana · al mismo tiempo
cards.native: all morning · at the same time
cards.exampleTarget: Tengo calor y sed al mismo tiempo.
cards.exampleNative: I'm hot and thirsty at the same time.
cards.replyNative: Do you want a glass of water?

cards.target: fui · fuiste · fue · fuimos · fueron
cards.native: ser and ir share the same preterite. Context tells you which.
cards.exampleTarget: Fui al mercado. La fiesta fue muy bonita.
cards.exampleNative: I went to the market. The party was very nice.

cards.target: di · dio · vi · vio
cards.native: dar and ver: short forms with no accents.
cards.exampleTarget: Le di dinero a mi hija. Vi una película.
cards.exampleNative: I gave money to my daughter. I saw a movie.

cards.target: ayer · anoche · anteayer
cards.native: yesterday · last night · the day before yesterday
cards.exampleTarget: Anoche llegué muy tarde.
cards.exampleNative: Last night I got home very late.
cards.remember: Classic preterite signal words.

cards.target: la semana pasada · el mes pasado · el año pasado
cards.native: last week · last month · last year
cards.exampleTarget: El año pasado viajamos a Oaxaca.
cards.exampleNative: Last year we traveled to Oaxaca.
cards.remember: pasado (last) matches the noun.

cards.target: hace dos días · hace un año
cards.native: two days ago · a year ago
cards.exampleTarget: Llegué a Guadalajara hace un año.
cards.exampleNative: I arrived in Guadalajara a year ago.
cards.remember: hace + time = ago. Different from hace calor (weather).
cards.replyNative: And do you like living here?

cards.target: una vez · el lunes pasado
cards.native: once · last Monday
cards.exampleTarget: Una vez comí mariscos en la playa.
cards.exampleNative: Once I ate seafood at the beach.

cards.target:
ser · preterite (simple past)
yo fui · tú fuiste · él / ella / usted fue · nosotros fuimos · ellos / ustedes fueron
cards.native:
to be (who / what someone is) · preterite (simple past)
I was · you were · he/she was / you (form.) were · we were · they / you all were
cards.exampleTarget: Ayer fue un día muy bueno.
cards.exampleNative: Yesterday was a very good day.
cards.remember: A finished action at a set time: ayer (yesterday), el lunes (on Monday), una vez (once). Same preterite as ir: fui can mean I was or I went.

estar · preterite (simple past)

I was · you were · he/she was / you (form.) were · we were · they / you all were

cards.target: trabajaré · trabajarás · trabajará · trabajaremos · trabajarán
cards.native: Future: keep the whole infinitive and add é, ás, á, emos, án. Same endings for -ar, -er and -ir.

cards.exampleNative: Tomorrow I will work at home.
cards.remember: In conversation, voy a trabajar (I'm going to work) is more common.
cards.meaning: I will work · you will work · he / she will work · we will work · they will work

cards.target: tendré · haré · diré · podré · sabré · habrá
cards.native: Irregular future stems from your verbs: tendr-, har-, dir-, podr-, sabr-, habr-. The endings stay the same.
cards.exampleTarget: El sábado habrá una fiesta y tendremos mucha comida.
cards.exampleNative: On Saturday there will be a party and we'll have a lot of food.
cards.remember: Later: pondr- (will put), saldr- (will go out), vendr- (will come), querr- (will want).
cards.meaning: I will have · I will do · I will say · I will be able to · I will know · there will be

cards.target: ¿Dónde estará?
cards.native: The future also expresses a guess about now: I wonder…, it's probably…
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Dónde estarán mis llaves? Estarán en la mochila.
cards.exampleNative: I wonder where my keys are. They're probably in the backpack.
cards.meaning: Where could he / she be? I wonder where he / she is.
cards.replyNative: I'll look for them right now.

cards.target: trabajaría · trabajarías · trabajaría · trabajaríamos · trabajarían
cards.native: Conditional (would): the same stem as the future + ía, ías, ía, íamos, ían.
cards.exampleTarget: Con más tiempo, viajaría más.
cards.exampleNative: With more time, I would travel more.
cards.remember: Irregulars use the future stems: tendría (would have), haría (would do), diría (would say), podría (could), sabría (would know), habría (there would be).
cards.meaning: I would work · you would work · he / she would work · we would work · they would work

cards.target: ¿Podría ayudarme? · Me gustaría…

cards.exampleNative: Could you repeat that, please? I would like a coffee.
cards.remember: Softer than ¿puede…? (can you…?) and quiero (I want).
cards.meaning: Could you help me? · I would like…

cards.group: Grammar: participles & the present perfect (have done)
cards.target: abierto · escrito · hecho · dicho · visto · roto
cards.native: Irregular participles from your verbs: abrir, escribir, hacer, decir, ver, romper.
cards.exampleTarget: La tienda está abierta. Ya he hecho la tarea.
cards.exampleNative: The store is open. I've already done the homework.
cards.remember: leído, creído, traído (read, believed, brought) keep an accent on the í.
cards.meaning: open, opened · written · done, made · said · seen · broken

cards.group: Grammar: participles & the present perfect (have done)
cards.target: La puerta está cerrada.
cards.native: A participle works as a describing word with estar and agrees with the noun. Many Lesson 4 words are participles: cerrado, perdido, ocupado, cansado, sentado, preocupado, roto.
cards.exampleTarget: Las ventanas están cerradas y la cena está preparada.
cards.exampleNative: The windows are closed and dinner is ready.
cards.meaning: The door is closed.
cards.replyNative: Then we can have dinner now.

cards.group: Grammar: participles & the present perfect (have done)
cards.target: he · has · ha · hemos · han
cards.native: Present perfect = haber in the present + participle. The participle never changes in this tense.
cards.exampleTarget: ¿Has comido? → Sí, ya he comido.
cards.exampleNative: Have you eaten? → Yes, I've already eaten.
cards.meaning: I have · you have · he / she has · we have · they have (+ done something)
cards.replyNative: Then let's go for a coffee.

cards.group: Grammar: participles & the present perfect (have done)
cards.target: ¿Ya comiste? · ¿Ya has comido?
cards.native: Mexico usually uses the preterite for "did you / have you". The perfect is used for "ever", "so far" and "lately".
cards.exampleTarget: Nunca he estado en Oaxaca. Este año he viajado mucho.
cards.exampleNative: I've never been to Oaxaca. This year I've traveled a lot.
cards.meaning: Did you eat yet? · Have you eaten yet?
cards.replyNative: Me neither. Shall we go together?

cards.group: Grammar: participles & the present perfect (have done)
cards.target: Lo he leído.
cards.native: Pronouns go before haber, never between haber and the participle.
cards.exampleTarget: ¿El libro? Ya lo he leído.
cards.exampleNative: The book? I've already read it.
cards.meaning: I've read it.
cards.replyNative: Will you lend it to me?

cards.group: Grammar: commands (telling someone to do something)
cards.target: ¡Habla! · ¡Come! · ¡Escribe!
cards.native: Affirmative tú command = the él / ella present form.
cards.exampleTarget: Habla más despacio, por favor. Come, mija.
cards.exampleNative: Speak more slowly, please. Eat, dear.
cards.remember: Seen: pásale, come in (pasa + -le, MX); toma asiento, have a seat.
cards.meaning: Speak! · Eat! · Write! (to a friend)

cards.group: Grammar: commands (telling someone to do something)
cards.target: ten · haz · di · ve · sé
cards.native: Irregular tú commands from your verbs: tener, hacer, decir, ir, ser. (Later: ven, pon, sal.)
cards.exampleTarget: Ten cuidado. Haz la tarea. Di la verdad.
cards.exampleNative: Be careful. Do the homework. Tell the truth.
cards.remember: ve is also the command of ver (to see); context tells you.
cards.meaning: have · do, make · say · go · be (to a friend)

cards.group: Grammar: commands (telling someone to do something)
cards.target: ¡Hable! · ¡Coma! · ¡Escriba!
cards.native: usted command: take the yo form, drop -o and switch the vowel: -ar → -e; -er / -ir → -a.
cards.exampleTarget: Tome asiento, por favor. Disculpe.
cards.exampleNative: Have a seat, please. Excuse me.
cards.remember: Yo-go verbs keep the g: tenga, haga, diga, traiga (have, do, say, bring). Seen: disculpe (excuse me), cuídese (take care), tome asiento (have a seat).
cards.meaning: Speak! · Eat! · Write! (polite)

cards.group: Grammar: commands (telling someone to do something)
cards.target: ¡No hables! · ¡No comas!
cards.native: Negative tú command: no + the usted form + s.
cards.exampleTarget: No te preocupes. No comas en el sofá.
cards.exampleNative: Don't worry. Don't eat on the sofa.
cards.remember: Seen in Lesson 5: no te preocupes (don't worry).
cards.meaning: Don't speak! · Don't eat! (to a friend)

cards.group: Grammar: commands (telling someone to do something)
cards.target: cuídate · cuídese · no te preocupes
cards.native: Pronouns attach to the end of affirmative commands (add an accent to keep the stress) and go before negative ones.
cards.exampleTarget: Cuídate mucho. No te preocupes.
cards.exampleNative: Take good care. Don't worry.
cards.meaning: take care (to a friend) · take care (polite) · don't worry

cards.group: Grammar: commands (telling someone to do something)
cards.target: ¡Hablen! · ¡Coman!
cards.native: ustedes command (affirmative and negative): the usted form + n.
cards.exampleTarget: Pasen, por favor. No se preocupen.
cards.exampleNative: Come in, please. Don't worry.

cards.group: Grammar: commands (telling someone to do something)
cards.target: ten cuidado · ¡vamos!
cards.native: be careful · let's go!
cards.exampleTarget: ¡Ten cuidado, hay muchos carros en la calle! ¡Vamos!
cards.exampleNative: Be careful, there are a lot of cars on the street! Let's go!

cards.target: que te vaya bien · que se mejore

cards.exampleNative: Have a good day. Hope it goes well.
cards.remember: Seen in Lessons 1 and 5.
cards.meaning: I hope it goes well for you · I hope you get better

cards.target: hable · hables · hable · hablemos · hablen
cards.native: Forming it: the same "switched vowel" as usted commands, in all five persons. -ar → e; -er / -ir → a.
cards.exampleTarget: Es importante que hables con el doctor.
cards.exampleNative: It's important that you talk to the doctor.
cards.meaning: that I speak · that you speak · that he / she speaks · that we speak · that they speak

cards.target: sea · esté · vaya · sepa · dé · haya
cards.native: Irregular subjunctives from your verbs: ser, estar, ir, saber, dar, haber. Yo-go verbs keep the g: tenga, haga, diga, traiga.
cards.exampleTarget: Ojalá que la fiesta sea en tu casa.
cards.exampleNative: I hope the party is at your house.
cards.meaning: that … be · that … be (how, where) · that … go · that … know · that … give · that there be

cards.target: entienda · entendamos · sienta · sintamos
cards.native: Stem changers keep the present change; -ir stem changers also change nosotros (sintamos).
cards.exampleTarget: Ojalá que entiendas la clase.
cards.exampleNative: I hope you understand the class.
cards.meaning: that … understand · that we understand · that … feel · that we feel

cards.target: ojalá (que)
cards.native: I hope… (always followed by the subjunctive)
cards.exampleTarget: Ojalá que mañana haga sol.
cards.exampleNative: I hope it's sunny tomorrow.
